story.text:
The Plane of Fire once had over seventy lords. In terms of ruling status, Thorgos was insignificant, but in terms of reputation, the name "Thorgos" was infamous.
"Duel me for two rounds. If I win, you become ash. If you win... you can choose a nice container to hold your ashen self. I truly am a merciful and generous lord, hahahaha."
From time to time, he would grab some unlucky resident from his domain, force them into a duel, and then brutally murder them.
This life of amusement finally bored Thorgos. These ordinary elemental beings were all too weak, too fragile to withstand a heavy blow.
The eternally burning flames of the plane swept violently across Thorgos's skin. During a fire bath, a new idea suddenly struck him —
What if his opponents were other lords?

"To crown the victor with the loser's crown. I like this gift. As for you... you may now perish!"
Thorgos raised his hand, and flames from his palm transformed into chains, suspending the crown in mid-air. The rare jewels still sparkled, but sadly, their former owner had been reduced to ashes at Thorgos's feet.
He disdainfully kicked the pile of dust. Where should he hang his two hundred and... forty-third trophy? Oh, he still needed an anklet.
Scorching demonic flames rose, enveloping the crown. In less than an hour, a new ornament adorned Thorgos's ankle. He glanced down with satisfaction, then walked toward the distant, rising screams.
Come on, let's burn it all down!

How could Thorgos not know how much he was hated? He had seen it in countless eyes — that unwillingness, that resentment, that desire to tear him to pieces!
But he loved to savor such looks.
The weak trembled as they gripped their daggers, struggling in extreme fear and finally bursting with the courage for revenge. Even if it meant turning to dust, they would take their enemy down with them!
Yet... take him down with them? Thorgos, who had consumed the souls of over seventy lords as fuel, was already an invincible being. A mere flick of a flame was enough to cast any avenger back into despair.
"I applaud your courage, and I admire your foolishness!"
It was said that nothing could threaten Thorgos anymore — that it was useless to even try.
In truth, in a certain plane filled with ice, there was something that could make him dissipate like smoke.

story.text:
"You... You're not a deep elf... You're a F-fallen..."
Perseus knocked down the patrol officer with ease, and the words "Fallen Soul" became drowned out by the blood erupting from her throat. As he watched her gradually unfocusing eyes, Perseus swiftly injected the poison into his prey to ensure she was kept just barely alive.
"My strength control leaves room for improvement," he thought. If his prey were to die prematurely on his way back to the nest, it would no longer make a fresh meal for Mother.

Meal? Yes, a meal. Such was not a term that would normally cross a Fallen Soul's mind — or more accurately, such beings did not have brains, and thus did not possess individual will. 
Perseus was uncertain whether he had a will himself, but it wasn't something he cared about. The only concern he had was his ability to provide Mother with the freshest and most delicious food. 
But ever since the roads to Corruption Meteor Field were blocked, there were fewer and fewer living creatures in the territory, and Sivesta's ravenous wails could constantly be heard from the Womb. Thus, Perseus chose to hunt in the most familiar place to him, near Perenthallis Nilae; it was a place where security was lax, with the occasional adventurer trespassing. 
If possible, he wished he could enjoy his prey together with Mother; it would be just like one of those countless afternoons in Perenthallis Nilae, when Sivesta was still a respectable queen, and he, as the crown prince, had the occasional opportunity of dining with her. 
"Who knew our tastes were so similar, my dear nephew," the queen had remarked to him often.

— Their tastes were still the same.
Perseus half knelt on the ground, and lifted the still-warm prey up high to the queen with his powerful upper limbs.
The tentacles in the pool of blood curled and quivered in excitement as the queen began to feast on her meal. Perseus suppressed the same bloodthirsty desire and waited in silence.
Like countless times before, he did not receive an invitation to dine together. He was well aware that, in the eyes of his queen, he was no different from the meals she devoured.
After all, he was the first prey to be swallowed by Sivesta after that meteorite fell. Then, ripped apart and reshaped into her embryo, he later became the first monster to be birthed by her.
"When will I be able to indulge in these flavors with you, my dear Mother?"

story.text:
The cold wind of the Vale howled past the cliff's edge. The old shaman and his apprentices pulled their robes tighter. There were no cheers of triumph, only a dead, reverent silence.
Ethyreis, the young shaman who had been missing for over a month, now staggered toward them. Large patches of his pure white fur were scorched, and his exposed skin was covered in dark scabs. All eyes were fixed on his chest — a slowly pulsing, abyssal flame, like a heart born from the abyss itself.
The old shaman gasped. "The Abyssal Darkfire... You actually brought it back! How is Thun?"
At the old shaman's question, the other werewolves noticed a frail wolf cub lying motionless on Ethyreis's shoulder. A red glow seeped from the cub's dangling left paw, connecting to the dark flame in faint tendrils.
Ethyreis looked up. His once ice-blue eyes were now blood-red, yet they held the same clarity as always. "As long as the dark flame burns, his life will not perish."

Months later, at the Blood-Red Pass, the war drums thundered. The invading human army surged like a tide. The commander's lips curled into a mocking smile. "Just as I predicted. The thorns in their skin that curbed their madness have also shackled their limbs."
"These self-exiled, ascetic werewolves are no longer a threat..."
Before he could finish, a dark flame rose from behind the werewolf lines. Ethyreis raised his staff, gathering the power of the relentlessly pulsing dark flame into the air. The dim fire then exploded silently, and a wave of frenzy swept the battlefield. The werewolf warriors' bodies swelled, their eyes turned blood-red, and their claws doubled in length.
"D-don't panic! Frenzied werewolves can't distinguish friend from foe! They'll... urgh!" A werewolf's claw, sharp as the finest blade, sliced through the commander's throat.

After the battle at the Blood-Red Pass, Ethyreis officially took over as shaman.
The power of the Abyssal Darkfire raised the Vale werewolves' combat prowess to an unprecedented level. Neither other races nor the werewolves themselves had ever imagined they could maintain their sanity while frenzied, and push their physical limits while fully conscious.
"Our people have suppressed themselves for too long in their daily penance... To be able to unleash their wild nature on the battlefield without fear of losing their minds — this is enough to make every werewolf warrior submit to you. However, is the price..."
The old shaman knew that to fuel the dark flame with one's own flesh and blood was to become undying. He silently painted the shamanistic runes on his successor. Beneath the runes, crimson energy flowed through Ethyreis's veins, finally converging on his chest and vanishing into the leaping flame.

story.text:
Beware of venturing into the depths of the forest lightly, for arrogant trespassers have already left behind enough gruesome lessons. 
Trespassers who have narrowly escaped all speak in horror of the wails of the Cursebinder. Its haunting cries assail from the treetops above, creep from the branches, and ooze from tree roots, instilling fear in the hearts of those who hear it. 
Most who are hunted by the Cursebinder never live to tell the tale. The fortunate few who have survived will forever remember its hollow cries. 
And those cries will be a nightmare that will haunt them for the rest of their lives.

Stegamoffyn is a nightmare of the deep forest, the traumatized embodiment of the forest itself. 
Neither a wood elf nor a Sylvan Fury, he is more akin to a monster formed from the collective wrath of nature, who instinctively attacks any living creature that comes near him. 
The woodland where he roams is marked as an absolute forbidden zone. Those who enter this zone by mistake have no hope of communicating with him and can only desperately flee while praying that they survive his arrows. 
Only the spilling of fresh blood can bring Stegamoffyn a moment of clarity, but it also only brings him greater torment.

Sometimes, Stegamoffyn dreams. 
The forest in his dreams is always so beautiful. The laughter of wood elves entwines with leaves of emerald green, and the heart of the forest glows with vitality. The seal deep within the dense forest is strong, which means that the evil Green Dragon is powerlessly forced into a slumber... 
However, Stegamoffyn's dream suddenly turns dark when the Green Dragon opens its eyes, its wicked slitted pupils casting a sinister gaze. The beautiful dream shatters, replaced by cursed whispers, shattered bonds, and defiled elegies. The forest's lament knows no end, crying out for Nythurys, the Father of the Woods. 
His frenzied visions end with the splattering of blood all over his body, his wails followed by sorrowful rasps. And Stegamoffyn mutters to himself, and resumes wandering the forest...

story.text:
Beneath a sky-blotting murder of crows, Kurvida stepped to a rhythm of wails, swinging her scythe to sever the limbs of her prey one by one.
"Please... just make it quick... argh!"
"Quick? Hahahaha... Where's the fun in that?" The prey's terror only excited her more, coldness and madness mingling in her laughter.
"That's enough, Kurvida," Premtsa warned. "Master does not wish to draw unnecessary attention."
"So what? Premtsa, don't try to make a madwoman follow your rules." The scythe ground against flesh and bone. Kurvida savored her prey's fear like the finest nectar.

Kurvida was born with a disdain for all rules. In her world, there was no right or wrong, only likes and dislikes. Naturally, she would not be bound by regulations.
During the trial of the Riscernos family, the rules were nothing more than a tedious drone to her — as long as she could seize final victory, the means were irrelevant.
So she threw a poisoned dagger at her opponent before the cliff. But in the next second, a scythe drew a precise arc of judgment, and her world was torn apart by absolute black and white. Kurvida stared blankly at the hands that had once so tightly gripped a shortcut, now lying quietly in the dust.
"The rules will not be defied." Arbiter Nastjenka's voice was as rippleless as her gaze.

In the abyss of despair, the Penultima found her. The whispers from the Outlands promised her not salvation, but a more extreme power.
She willingly embraced Chaos, offering herself to the Silent Gods. Two cold scythes were embedded into her severed arms, fusing with nerve and bone in agonizing pain.
None of that mattered... She would become strong at any cost. One day, she would personally drag that supreme embodiment of rules into a vortex of pain of her own making.
Beneath a sky-blotting murder of crows, Kurvida stepped to a rhythm of wails, her crimson eyes fixed on the distance.

story.text:
The moment Ferdinand inserted the final magic crystal into the construct's chest cavity, a nightmare started to haunt the residents of Anchorite Spiral.
The robot, named "Blah Blah", immediately played a variation of the "Funeral March" on seven different brass instruments upon activation, while its head-mounted speaker looped the message, "Happy New Year, and may you find eternal peace soon."
Its creator noted with satisfaction: "Initial test successful — knocking frequency on the neighbor's wall reached 120 times per minute."
For the next three months, Blah Blah dutifully executed its one core program: verbal harassment.
Every morning, it would appear at the entrance of the council hall and recite improvised satirical poems: "Caroux, Caroux, what a great leader, using art to fill his political meter." At noon, it would sneak into the commercial district, blowing a bugle while reminding merchants: "Short-change your customers, die an early death; sell shoddy goods, you've got no brain left." Late at night, it would patrol around the spiral tower, playing a "lullaby" mixed with burps on its bagpipes.
For a time, every gnome on Anchorite Spiral considered packing up and leaving home.

These hard times did not end, because no one knew how to deal with the all-purpose verbal assault machine.
Ferdinand had equipped his beloved creation with the most advanced harassment modules: if a victim tried to flee, Blah Blah could spray a sticky substance to prevent their escape; if someone resorted to violence, its large speaker would emit a foul-smelling gas that caused dizziness.
Once, Blah Blah was locked in a cellar by an angry baker, and as a result, the entire street was forced to listen to the "Ode to Moldy Bread" all night: "Oh, dough, oh, dough, how beautiful you are, with moldy pores that rot the gut afar..."
But its most legendary achievement was at the Anchorite Spiral's annual tech exhibition. Just as the judges were about to present the Best Invention Award to Donella, the president of the Magic Puppet Guild, Blah Blah suddenly began reciting at a volume that could knock over the magic puppet bird: "Your shiny awards are worse than grime! The judges' eyes are full of slime!"
Then, Blah Blah shot off fireworks on the venue's dome, displaying a banner that read "Blind Judges Have No Luck".
It was this incident that made Ferdinand the most infamous gnome, and Blah Blah's language module was partially sealed.

The turning point came before Donella's workshop.
While Blah Blah was looping the polite and harmonious message "Renounce the award, know your place, be a wise fool" at the Magic Puppet Guild, Donella approached its sensor directly: "Your resonance chamber design is fascinating! How about a duet with my magic puppet bird?"
In the days that followed, whenever Blah Blah was on its mission to "convince Donella to renounce the award", it would always see her helping other gnomes or teaching poor children to assemble simple mechanical bird toys. Its system truly overloaded one rainy day, when Donella actually held an umbrella over it.
Blah Blah heard her say, "Gears will hurt if they get rusty."
For the first time, Blah Blah's program glitched. A chaotic jumble of sounds burst from its speaker: "You... abnormal data detected... kindness is disgusting! Suggest... suggest..."
It gradually fell silent. Its mechanical hand unconsciously took the umbrella, and its language module began to recompile in its head: "Execute verbal harassment program... for what purpose?"
After that, the residents of Anchorite Spiral still often saw the bully spewing insults, but the volume was three notches lower. Occasionally, a polite phrase learned from Donella would be mixed in with the curses — though the combination still came out as: "Kindly get lost. Thank you for your cooperation!"

story.text:
The Plane of Ice was not always so lifeless.
The ice elementals were a playful sort, fond of using the city towers as slides, plummeting from great heights to shatter themselves into thin, hexagonal snowflakes.
There were also crystal creatures that loved to lie on the few sources of light, the light refracting through their bodies into wondrous colors.
All this beauty vanished after the old lord faded away.
The new lord, Aethereal, preferred quiet. She ordered all the city walls to be torn down, and on the ruins, she built an icy prison.
Any creature, for the slightest misstep, would be thrown into jail.

In the extreme cold of the Plane of Ice, anything could be frozen: time, emotion, thought, even memory...
Aethereal rarely visited the small room at the bottom of the Glacial Purgatory. There were no prisoners here, or rather, the only prisoner here — was herself.
In the center of the room stood a translucent ice coffin.
Aethereal gently opened it. Inside were hundreds of colored ice crystals.
Memories were useless, only a burden that disturbed the tranquility. Aethereal gently touched her temple, and another memory froze and fell into her palm.
The vexation caused by the planar conflict was thrown into the coffin along with the memory crystal. Aethereal emotionlessly brushed off the ice shards that had fallen on her, and decided it was time to rest.

A discordant crimson flame appeared in the center of the palace. Facing this uninvited guest, Aethereal's expression remained unchanged.
He was more striking than the image she had seen in her ice crystals — Thorgos, the lord who had set the entire Plane of Fire ablaze with war.
"Hand it over. The Core of Extreme Cold, the only treasure that can extinguish me."
How did he even know about this thing? An arrogant, foolish, and noisy thing! Aethereal showed a rare flash of anger, tightening her grip on the sword by her throne.
"Since I have such a fine thing, why wouldn't I — use it to extinguish you?"

story.text:
"She was once like you all... but to survive here, you must become a beast."
Facing a new cart of "goods", the oldest warden of the Crucible, Kaf, pointed to the swift, leopard-like figure in the sand pit. Another opponent was taken down in moments. Kaf couldn't help but remember when Alarys was first sold to the Crucible — slender, silent, her eyes shining with a clear, stubborn light. Such light would soon dim, Kaf thought.
Alarys's trainer was a retired gladiator called the One-eyed. He tried to teach her the first lesson with a wooden stick and a leather whip. Scars were seared onto Alarys's delicate skin. Kaf once doubted the frail woman would see another sunrise.
That day finally came. The nauseating stench of blood mixed with wine spilled out of the One-eyed's stone hut. Kaf opened the door, intending to collect the poor woman's corpse, only to find someone else lying in a pool of blood.
The One-eyed was lifeless, a broken spear deeply embedded in the left side of his neck — his blind spot. Kaf looked up and met Alarys's gaze from the corner. The light in her eyes was terrifyingly bright.

On the Crucible's most glorious night, the sand was saturated with blood, making the opponents before her appear thick and blurred. At the cost of three ribs and an ear, Alarys defeated thirteen consecutive challengers, finally standing at the peak of honor as she had envisioned.
Relying on the staggering odds against this dark horse, the Crucible's master made a fortune. His delight brought him to the stage for a rare appearance, deciding to personally crown Alarys.
"A born fighting beast. What's your name? Aly?... Oh, it doesn't matter. From now on, your title is the Queen of the Crucible..." Before he could finish, Alarys moved. There was no roar, only the muffled crunch of a throat being crushed. The man's eyes widened in shock as he fell, the screams of the crowd stifled in their throats.
Alarys ripped the pure gold collar, a symbol of "honor," from her neck and slammed it to the ground. "I seek no crown within a cage. I am here to break them."

Free from her cage, Alarys did not hide. Following clues from the warden Kaf, she moved between gladiatorial arenas and trading markets to track down the people she was looking for.
"Give me a name, and I'll shorten your suffering." Alarys never shied away from using cruel methods to extract information, making her a feared name among the desert brokers. Investors in the Crucible, foreign slavers, apothecaries who made deliriants... Relying on her fragmented memories and a beast's sense of smell, she retraced the route she was trafficked on, crossing names off her list one by one.
Gradually, she began to piece together the edges of a vast network. She realized the Crucible was just the tip of the iceberg, with more masterminds hidden deep in the shadows. She had never truly escaped the cage. And to shatter it completely, her strength alone was not enough.

story.text:
If darkness were to vanish, then light would lose its meaning.
When Anneliesis was born, the Plane of Radiance did not yet exist. She came into being within a realm saturated with eclipsing power — a fragile glimmer that could be snuffed out at any moment.
Moon Goddess Monelisse was the first to witness this miracle. Against all opposition, she brought Anneliesis back to the Everlasting Elysium and nurtured her with care.
When Anneliesis had grown powerful in magic, the Moon Goddess personally sent her away. "Go. Create the light that belongs to you."

"In the Plane of Fire, that deranged madman has devoured the last of the old lords."
Hearing the news, Anneliesis instinctively tightened her grip on her blade of light. She could already imagine it — within that realm wreathed in eternal flame, countless ordinary lives reduced to ash by war. A merciless tyrant is always the beginning of catastrophe.
"Should we go take a look? Maybe we can help?"
Anneliesis rejected her attendant's naive suggestion. She was but a gentle light, raised under divine protection, never having taken part in any conflict. In that moment, rather than offering aid, she feared only one thing — being swept into the flames of war.
Since leaving the Everlasting Elysium, this was the first — and only — time Anneliesis sought help from Monelisse.
Help me... before I fall into darkness once more.

The Plane of Radiance, seemingly the most joyous and serene of all, strikes fear into the hearts of other elemental lords.
Legend says that those with wicked intentions who dare approach the realm of light are instantly obliterated into dust. Time and again, attempts have been made — yet not even a trace of the countless spies sent has ever returned.
"It must be the favor of the gods! It must be!" Over time, rumors about Anneliesis began to spread.
In truth, as Bahamut fell silent, the Moon Goddess's power also waned. Hearing the plea for help, she could not lend her aid to Anneliesis.
But she once told her, "When kindness loses its strength, it becomes fodder for evil... You must become a sharp light."
Suddenly, Anneliesis understood — the light is my own, and I choose to shine!

story.text:
High above the clouds of Celestial Isle, a figure in a bluish white robe appeared among the pillars of the temple, graceful as a swan. The whispers ceased. The pilgrims held their breath, gazing at Suwalah's immaculate hem, awaiting a blessing from the god's messenger.
Ethereal syllables escaped Suwalah's lips, like the murmur of the morning wind or the lapping of the tides. Her staff's gentle movements sent out ripples of faint light with her song. Wherever the light touched, wounds quietly healed, and restless souls were soothed.
"I... I can stand again!" An elderly believer rose from the ground, stumbling toward Suwalah. "High Priestess, thank you... thank you for the god's gift..."
Aels deftly stepped in front of the believer. In a moment, Suwalah had vanished into the depths of the temple.

As a student of the High Priestess Suwalah on Celestial Isle, Aels rarely had the opportunity to speak with her. Besides singing, Suwalah barely interacted with anyone.
Most of the time, Aels knelt with the other novice priests on the cold jade steps of the temple, looking up at his teacher on the altar. The morning light pierced the clouds, gilding her in gold. Suwalah began to sing, today teaching the students the eighth chapter, seventh verse of the Hymn of Prayer.
Suwalah sang it three times, and Aels followed along perfectly in his mind three times. To others, he had exceptional musical talent, able to remember every note and pause after just one listen. Yet when he tried to imitate Suwalah's voice, it always fell far short. But... but he hadn't missed a single half-beat!
Aels clenched the corner of his robe, sprang up from the steps, and, mustering his courage, ran in the direction Suwalah had disappeared.

By the time Aels reached the western cliff, a place considered barren, the moon was high in the sky.
He had lost sight of his teacher in the winding corridors, but a strange yet familiar song had led him here.
He had never heard Suwalah sing like this before. She sang to the vast, starry sky, her voice loud and clear. There were no fixed verses; the melody changed with her heart, at times as tempestuous as a storm, at others as joyful as a babbling brook. It was completely different from the solemn chanting in the temple. This song was filled with pure joy and innocent exploration, as if she were facing not the cold night sky, but a dear friend with whom she could share her every thought.
"Listen, that trill just now, wasn't it like the twinkling starlight tonight?" Notes full of life scattered across the land, and faint lights flickered, illuminating patches of wondrous flowers that sprang from the earth. The barren land had become a magnificent floating garden.
Aels forgot to breathe, forgot why he had come. But the person singing so freely under the moon knew that her student had found his answer.

story.text:
Maashtur ascended to the throne on a scorching day during the drought season coinciding with the Water Prayer Festival. On that day, throngs of new parents carried their infants to be blessed by the new king after seeking divine blessings at the temple.
Amidst the cries of the infants and the continuous hum of prayers for the Water Prayer Festival, Maashtur, who had just become accustomed to the weight of the crown atop his head, gently patted infant after infant, and brushed the teal blue mark across their foreheads in turn feeling the weight of something heavier, something that was beyond the crown itself. These burdens had only just departed from his aged father, but they did not remain within his magnificent bejeweled coffin; instead, they came directly to rest upon Maashtur's shoulders.

Maashtur did not grow up in the Royal City. Unlike his womb-brother Halramar who was frail as a child and rarely ventured outside, Maashtur was a fierce tiger raised on the battlefield. Before he became king, he was already in command of the Tigerclaw Brigade and had led the army in aggressive battles against the minotaurs — and these battles had correspondingly become his bargaining chips in his ascension to the crown. 
Military life had conditioned him to be somewhat impatient with those from the Great River Sect; compared to his preferred style of frank and authoritative decision-making, those cautious, mysterious, and deliberative monks were a massive headache. Thus, when the church gradually slipped from his oversight and fell under the control of his dark-furred prince brother, he even felt relieved — but of course, he would eventually come to regret this.

Maashtur harbored especially complex feelings towards his prince brother Halramar. They were once brothers who sought comfort from each other under the harsh tyranny of their father, but they became enemies after certain ambitions spiraled out of control. 
Their divergence had seemingly stemmed from the day Maashtur left the royal palace alone and followed the Tigerclaw Brigade into battle. Halramar had watched his departure, then headed to the church to pray for him — and never stepped foot outside again. 
But when Maashtur witnessed Halramar being besieged by the army, all he could regretfully think was that these feelings belonged to Maashtur, and not the Tigerfolk King — thus, he drew his bejeweled scimitar, chanted the holy name of the Great River God, and unleashed his judgment as king.

story.text:
As the fetid air settled over the battlefield, Seyir hummed a tune while polishing his sword. Queen Sivesta's amethyst eyes reflected her ever-smiling paramour. "Do you intend to repel the enemy with a song?"
"I'm calculating the time it will take for the Thallasen Clan to find us." Seyir suddenly pointed a finger at a passage on the map — the foul, poisonous swamp the enemy had to cross.
And then, this "queen's plaything", once ridiculed by the nobles, displayed terrifying strategic genius. He ordered the army's sorcerers to detonate the spider egg sacs on both sides of the swamp passage, using the resulting acid to form a natural barrier. As the enemy charged, Seyir deliberately opened the eastern flank. Once they poured in, he detonated the shadow runes that had been planted in advance. The queen's elite royal guards were thus able to escort her through the breach, though Seyir knew this was merely delaying the inevitable.

By the time they retreated to the heart of the poisonous swamp, Sivesta's right arm had begun to rot, sprouting foul-smelling tumors — a sign of the corruption. Seyir knelt and began to carve away the putrid flesh, his movements as elegant as if he were peeling grapes.
"Why are you so calm? Is this a trap? Have you colluded with the Thallasen Clan?" Queen Sivesta suddenly seized Seyir's throat. "What did they promise you?"
Seyir admitted it freely. "The Thallasen Clan did approach me, and their offer was very tempting. However..." Seyir looked into Sivesta's eyes, which were slowly losing their focus. "... I have no desire to be their servant, nor, of course, will I continue to be your plaything."

The patrons of the Terminus tavern often wondered about that deep elf who lived in the hidden cave. Where did he come from? And why did he seem to know everything?
One of the patrons, drunk, boasted to the others, "Stop guessing. The fellow's just a common swindler! I have to admit, he's a clever craftsman — he's forged quite a few things. He showed me a ring with the Perenthallis crest, still on a severed finger! Not only that, but he dared to forge the Thallasen Clan's secret scrolls..."
In the hidden cave, Seyir carefully examined a parchment roll, a secret tome detailing the origin of the Blasphemous. At the end, a name was signed: Seyir. His own name. This was the foul truth he had recorded, as a survivor of that bloody battle.

story.text:
After stationing myself at Devil's Snare Tavern for three days, by when I had sampled everything on the drink menu, I finally met its owner, Ivira. 
Her beauty is indeed as outstanding as the legends describe. 
She seemed to know every single person in the tavern. At first, I had assumed that everyone present was a regular, until she came up to me and called my name like an old friend, even offering me a glass of the most popular rum these days — I was surprised to discover that these were no mere coincidences. 
She might truly know everything about Unyielding Silk as the legends say. 
 —— Intelligence Officer Theta, May the Thirteenth

I have to retract my earlier assessment — Her web extends far beyond the Unyielding Silk's territory.
Fortunately, she is rather cordial and talkative for a deep elf. After a few drinks, she let her guard down with me and revealed quite a few things. I already have a basic grasp of the layout of the tavern and her recent movements.
Yesterday, she brought in a secret shipment with her subordinates. When I infiltrated the storeroom, I discovered an array of never-seen-before weapons which seemed to be crafted with dwarven aurelium.
The shipment disappeared today. It was replaced by several crates of hefty medicine jars, stamped with the emblem of the Three Ears.
However, I have yet to find any evidence regarding the matter you have tasked me to investigate.
 — Intelligence Officer Theta, May the Seventeenth

It's truly unbelievable... If I had been a little less meticulous, I would never have discovered such an enormous secret in my lifetime...
That woman... the leader of the rebel army... she's actually still hiding within the Unyielding Silk!
After Ivira returned to the tavern today, she didn't follow her usual routine of having a drink at the bar, but instead hurried upstairs. I tailed closely behind, and from the corner of the staircase, I witnessed a woman leap through the window into her room.
Carrying two scimitars and shrouded in a black cape... I'd never be mistaken!
I'll organize the intel tonight, and we'll go meet the general tomorrow...
(The rest of the writing is stained with blood.)
It's been a while, Aspalta. Do you like this present?"
"Ha, Ivira, I know you've already marked the price of your gift a long time ago... and rejecting you isn't ever an option."

story.text:
On a full moon night, Scaarr ventured alone deep into the heart of a volcano and unexpectedly discovered a runestone on an ancient altar.
Curiously, Scaarr reached out and grasped the runestone. In an instant, lava-like runes crawled all over his body along his blood vessels. From then on, fire eternally danced beneath his skin.
Scaarr struggled back to his tribe, the burning pain blurring his consciousness. The troll shaman, however, declared it a blessing of the power of fire, and the tribe regarded Scaarr as a living war totem.
Only Scaarr knew that it was more of a curse than a blessing. Every dawn, Scaarr would curl up in his stone cave, listening to the sound of his skin cracking. The pain made it difficult for him to sleep.

The battlefield became Scaarr's only analgesic.
When he charged with his burning feet, screams would erupt from the enemy lines — wherever Scaarr passed, raging flames would ignite, melting iron armor into red-hot shackles that roasted the enemies alive.
Those who died under Scaarr's great axe suffered a worse fate; not only would they be burned beyond recognition, but even their skulls would be left with lava patterns.
"I like the crackle of my enemies' bones..." Scaarr often whispered to his smoking axe blade.
After one battle, his kinsfolk found Scaarr kneeling amidst a pile of charred corpses, breaking off the burnt, charcoal-like fingers one by one, as if listening to some kind of music only fire could understand.

As Scaarr lost control time and time again, the trolls in his tribe began to avoid him.
The same shaman, who had once praised Scaarr for bringing the blessing of fire's power, began to consider whether this out-of-control warrior should be exiled.
At the moment of his exile, Scaarr was repeatedly carving fire runes into the rock wall with his scorched fingers. The shaman's verdict made him stop. Sparks flew from his skin and landed on the ground. The sudden burst of light illuminated his scarred face — an expression that looked like both crying and laughing.
That night, Scaarr left, dragging his great axe with him. No one knew where he went.

story.text:
Come, the first toast, to our wonderful meeting.
You should know, it's not easy to come to the Golden Perch, to my banquet hall. Since you've stepped into my domain, please entrust all your pleasures to my care.
Do you prefer the ever-flowing wine pot at my waist, or the never-wilting glowing orchid in my hair? Don't be shy, feel free to pour out all your desires to me...
... Oh, oh, Rose, please let go of my tail first, it's undergoing a softening treatment recently... and the area around the tail is also off-limits...
My apologies, Traveler, let's continue our conversation.
You say you want to know my story?

Then the second toast, to... to this cup of wine.
The reason I came to the Material Plane was to find all kinds of fine wines. Unfortunately, it was also the lure of fine wine that led me to be drugged by an exotic pet trafficker and sold to a nobleman in a northern human kingdom.
Oh dear, don't look so sad — it was actually a thrilling and fun adventure.
With me, the palace had music every night, an endless banquet. And I, as the four-hoofed new favorite, lingered between the seats of various nobles, drinking down the nectar filled with secrets...
Just when I was about to get tired of it, the Crimson Crow found me, and I was naturally happy to... trade old news for new wine.

The third toast... why not to this setting sun, about to sink into the sea of sand!
This is the time when Jannat al-Harr most resembles my homeland — the sun, about to set but not yet gone, shines with intoxicating colors. The sky in my homeland is like this most of the time. Other than that, they are not alike in the slightest.
Outside the Golden Perch, there is nothing but annoying sand. But in the wilderness of my homeland — glowing mushrooms whisper in the woods, and vines intertwine under the moon. Drinking dew wine from an oak cup, we press our horns together and revel all night...
Are you drunk? Haha... sleep, sleep. In our dreams, we shall meet again.

story.text:
If a tourist visiting Anzuluvon inquired about the attractions in the royal capital, every single tigerfolk would provide a different answer. 
From a myriad of textile shops, to the Broken Sands Market that hawked a variety of general merchandise, to the Oasis Treasures Hotel renowned for good liquor of every description... However, there would always be one unanimous recommendation by the tigerfolk: a visit to Shahla's House of Divination. 
Nevertheless, even if this tourist had not done prior research, they were guaranteed not to miss it. 
For no one could resist Shahla's passionate greetings, and the exuberant Shahla would make sure that no one slips her notice.

Well, what's so alluring about Shahla's House of Divination, you may ask? 
Everyone who has been there says: Inside is where all your fantasies within the Tigerfolk Kingdom can come true. 
Firstly, you will be welcomed by the vibrant-coated and sizzling hot proprietress into her cozy little shop, where she will ease your guard with her captivating voice and impassioned attitude — because what bad intentions could such a beautiful and sincere tigerfolk have? 
The lingering fragrance in the shop relaxes you completely, and perhaps even elicit contented purrs from you. 
Hmm? What's that purring sound? 
That's not important. You cast that thought aside and let your body fully sink into the very soft and very plush armchair.

Next, you will be greeted by an even more wonderful paradise. 
The sunlight that filters through the heavy muslin curtains is now so gentle and calming, while the crisp aroma of fine wine and the soothing melody of a harp fills the air. You seem to hear Shahla asking you something, so you answer without hesitation. The sound of the harp changes, and she seems to have moved to a different position. 
The next question comes, but you can't hear it clearly, so you answer based on instinct. And do so for the next, and the next after that... You've lost track of reality and fantasy as comfort seeps from your bones, enters your bloodstream, and spreads through your limbs, indolently caressing your mind. 
... 
When you open your eyes again, it is already dusk. You can feel all your fatigue, worries, and stress evaporate like mist as a fountain of positivity bursts forth from your heart. 
Shahla will share some divination insights with you, and you will genuinely feel as if you have been enlightened with direction and have reaped the answers to life. And so you pull out a heavy bag of gold coins as compensation, promising to recommend others to visit before you finally leave, fully satisfied.

story.text:
In the Intertidal Clan, the strongest merfolk was honored as king. Thus, even before the current merfolk king aged, speculation about his successor had begun.
At seven years old, Fathomdown already had a mature and robust appearance that was beyond his age, one that looked just like a young merfolk warrior. This often led the other merfolk to overlook his age, inadvertently angering this powerful youth. After taking a beating from him, they would remark, "This guy is definitely going to be the future king."
In this way, at just seven, Fathomdown was already aware of his destined greatness as the future merfolk king.

It wasn't until Fathomdown became the true merfolk king that he realized the world of kingship was far more complex than he had imagined. Beyond the simplicity of "strong" versus "weak" lay concepts like "rule," "governance," "checks and balances," "systems," "strategy," and "tactics" — terms that were closely related yet mind-numbingly intricate, none of which he had any interest in understanding.
In Fathomdown's world, complex rules were unnecessary. Hesitation was the excuse of the incapable. Absolute power alone could overcome everything and make anything happen.

"What is absolute power?"
Shinnah had once asked him, and now her voice echoes through the distant memories in Fathomdown's mind.
Absolute power... is the power that can never fail. It is the colossal tentacles of the Abyssolossus flattening Equinoxial in an instant, the eyes of chaos opening from the abyss, the unimaginable force that mortals cannot overstep.
Standing amidst the ruins of Equinoxial, the past world crumbles before Fathomdown's eyes.
A true king can only be born after he realizes his own insignificance.

story.text:
Late at night, in the depths of the celestine alleys of Anzuluvon, an oil lamp still burned in a cramped monk's dwelling.
The young tigerfolk monk, Rashaad, carefully turns the worn pages of court files with his rough claws, his nose almost touching the paper. Outside the window, the curses of a drunkard and the laughter of a dancer drifted by, but he paid them no mind. An anxious old farmer sat opposite him, wringing the hem of his ragged clothes.
"I... I'm telling the truth, but the warrior monks drove me out of the Great River Abbey..."
Rashaad looked up, his amber eyes as sharp as a blade in the dim light. His voice was low but carried a strange, calming power. "Power cannot crush truth."
He pinched out the lamp and rose, disappearing into the pre-dawn darkness — not for morning prayers, but toward the disputed fields outside the city.

Under the solemn dome of the Hall of Judgement, a trial concerning a noble's seizure of farmland was drawing to a close.
The gem-adorned tigerfolk noble in the defendant's box wore a smug expression. The wealthy merchants in the gallery exchanged knowing glances. The presiding judge was already preparing to declare "insufficient evidence".
Suddenly, Rashaad, the scribe, shot to his feet. "I object!"
His voice boomed, drowning out the whispers in the court. He strode forward, ignoring the twisted faces of the nobles, and slammed a thick stack of ledgers and testimonies onto the judge's bench. His patched monk's robe was still stained with mud from the fields.
The case ultimately ended in the noble's defeat. Rashaad's name began to be spoken with reverence both inside and outside the Hall of Judgement, and he became a thorn in the side of certain powerful figures.

Now, the badge of the Chief Justice of the Hall of Judgement rests heavily on Rashaad's chest, yet the hem of his elaborate robe still inadvertently gets stained with cheap spices from the market or seeds from the countryside.
"Lord Rashaad, leaving evidence of your excursions during work hours again, I see." A fellow monk from the abbey, knowing Rashaad wasn't as stern as he appeared, couldn't resist a bit of teasing.
Rashaad shook his head with a sigh, gathered the files he needed, and quickened his pace toward his dwelling. The sound of his steady steps echoed through the deep celestine alleys, his destination still that same cramped monk's room.
Even after becoming the Chief Justice, he insisted on not changing his residence, continuing to live in the old, dilapidated commoners' district. The reason was simple — the hall of justice always needs someone willing to stoop down and pick up the faint voices trampled into the mud.

story.text:
"Old Barne said the monster in the depths of the swamp has even got a green shadow and can swallow people whole. Are you really going, Jones?" Athom lowered his voice, rubbing his hands by the campfire. The early autumn in Nytheria wasn't cold, but the young hunters were trying to dispel not the chill, but the fear in their hearts.
Jones's father had accidentally wandered into that poisonous swamp known as the "Venomire", and never returned.
The tavern owner, wiping a greasy mug, sneered, "Forget it, kid. If you're scared, don't go. Is that family heirloom of yours really more important than your life?"
"Let me tell you, that swamp is cursed. In my grandfather's time, it was just a small patch deep in the forest. These past couple of years... it's swallowed up half the woods! If it keeps expanding like this, I reckon my tavern won't be in business for long..."

"Help! Help!" Jones's screams were drowned out by the thick, sucking sound of the swamp behind him.
Minutes earlier, he had been trying to cut the foul-smelling, dark green vine wrapped around his ankle — the vine tightened, and in the blink of an eye, dragged the screaming young man into the bubbling poisonous swamp.
The swamp churned like the throat of a giant beast, swallowing everything in seconds, with only a hat slowly sinking.
Athom scrambled to the edge of the woods, using all his strength to climb a dead giant tree. His heart pounded. Just then, sticky footsteps came from the depths of the swamp. Athom lifted his trembling eyelids and looked over —
The thick fog in the center of the swamp dissipated slightly, and a tall, dark green woman emerged. Her entire body was covered in a strange green armor, the material of which was neither metal nor cloth, but rather seemed to be a condensation of the rot and resentment of the swamp.

Within the cold armor was an endless burning and festering.
Szecedith felt the venom coursing under her human skin, corroding it. Each heartbeat brought a new surge of excruciating pain. But this pain was far less than the humiliation of the sharp claws that had torn her dragon wings in the depths of her memory — Zmaragdis! This was all the doing of her twin brother, who sat on the throne of the Blue Oak, yet had exiled her here...
Szecedith let out a silent roar, and more venom seeped from the crevices of her armor, dripping into the swamp. The newly devoured prey dissolved beneath the mud, their faint life force merging into this domain nourished by her pain and resentment. Every death expanded the swamp by a fraction, and increased her power by a bit.
One day, the swamp would overflow the mountains and reach the distant dragon lair... Then, that emerald throne would become the sweetest of nourishment.

story.text:
"Saverio, don't eat that bloody meat!" "Don't take off the wolfthorn back-ring! Don't you..." His father's stern reprimands echoed all around.
In his memory, his father had countless rules, and the whole family was filled with a repressive atmosphere.
Saverio tried to resist, but it didn't earn his father's affection. On the contrary, the young Saverio was tied to a chair with wolfthorns for three whole days as punishment.
"You must remember, we are different from those beasts. We must control the madness in our blood and always act with reason." The blood dripping from his fur collected in a hollow of the stone slab, then coagulated as day turned to night.
He had thought his father was the strongest, most rational being, but after a full moon night, his father too fell into madness, broke free from the wolfthorns, and lunged at Saverio.
A guardian warrior's sharp arrow pierced his father's body, and warm blood splattered onto Saverio.
Is our will truly so fragile?

"Not looking directly at the moon helps to suppress the madness." This has been a universally acknowledged law among the wolf clan for millennia.
On the night of the full moon, however, Saverio, carrying a bundle of wolfthorns, resolutely stepped out of the confined space.
He bound himself tightly, waiting for the moon to cross the horizon and announce the arrival of the trial.
A guardian warrior coldly warned him from the side, "Go back to your room before the moon rises. If you insist on staying here, the moment you lose consciousness, I will cut off your head."
"Will I go mad?" "Will I die?" Saverio didn't know the outcome, but — what was the use of hiding? Fear would not yield to evasion.
The pale moonlight gradually filled the sky. The curse of madness in his blood began to invade his mind, and his reason faded bit by bit. Without hesitation, he plunged the tip of a blade into his vulnerable shoulder...
After hundreds of full moons, the scarred Saverio stood in the moonlight, gazing at the moon without any restraints, more sober than anyone.
He understood that he had conquered it.

"He's still young. He hasn't learned to control himself yet. Please spare him." On the eve of the Madness Purge Rite, a desperate plea came from outside the door.
Saverio put down the scroll filled with names. In the last two full moon nights, the number of kinsfolk who had fallen into madness was several times higher than usual. What could have caused this change?
"Check the wolfthorn fruits and the incantations again," Saverio ordered the warrior on duty to investigate.
Soon after, the warrior returned and reported that all the materials used were the same as on previous full moon nights, with no deviation whatsoever.
A black mist carrying a foul stench shattered Saverio's confusion. A cold voice rushed toward him from the bottomless valley, moaning hollowly: "More... there will only be more! Offer them to me..."
Saverio grabbed the greatsword engraved with blood curse runes and slashed at the indescribable mist.
"Tomorrow's Madness Purge Rite is cancelled. For the sake of the wolf clan, we have more important matters to attend to!" Saverio stepped out of the room and announced to everyone.
"Heed the alpha's call!" The cry echoed throughout the village.

story.text:
"Lord? Lord Caroux?... Are you listening?"
"One moment... A perfect string of notes just flashed through my mind. I must write it down..."
No one in Anchorite Spiral's council chamber would be surprised by this exchange, because Lord Caroux's rise to power... was itself an accident.
When his father hopefully signed him up for the election, the young gnome was busy researching how to give his steam-powered bagpipes a more metallic, piercing tone. Forced onto the campaign stage, he neither debated policy nor showcased his research, but simply performed an impromptu piece on his clockwork lute before hurrying off. To his surprise, the performance, a fusion of industrial roars and beautiful melody, captured the voters' hearts, making the note-obsessed inventor an unlikely victor.

To Caroux, his lordship is but an abrupt interlude in a grand symphony, and he constantly tries to return to the main melody.
To his subordinates, Caroux is approachable enough. When they report on official matters, their lord is always gentle and polite, never harsh — it's just that the floating mechanical tuning hand on his shoulder seems to have a mind of its own, always bouncing in the air, adjusting some non-existent frequency.
And out of their sight, Caroux's fingers tap out complex, syncopated rhythms under the table. The moment a meeting is adjourned, he's off like a tightly wound spring, grabbing blueprints and rushing back to his laboratory — a place filled with tuning forks, resonance tubes, metal horns, and magic crystal ores. Here, he is the true "lord".

In this peculiar laboratory where notes and gears resonate, Caroux created the "Sonicboom Lute" — a masterpiece blending a popular instrument with gnomish flintlock technology. It can play elegant, charming melodies, or turn those same notes into howling sonic projectiles to bombard a target.
As for its actual combat effectiveness...
Caroux doesn't care, and neither do the gnomes of Anchorite Spiral. They've created more than enough devastatingly powerful weapons. Why not make room for a work of art?
Perhaps it is because of such "unserious" pursuits that Anchorite Spiral, while not perfectly orderly, is forever vibrant with all kinds of novel creations.

story.text:
The Dawn Square in Dragonsaerie had lately been echoing with resounding songs, drawing many to stop and listen. But most didn't stay for long. Even those attracted by the fame only listened for a moment before leaving.
That was because both the singing and the lute-playing were utterly ordinary. Neither enjoyable enough to appreciate, nor terrible enough to amuse.
"Every note is in tune, yet it sounds exceptionally dull, completely lacking in rhythm," one bard commented. "I suppose that's a talent in itself."
However, the departing audience did not dampen the performer's enthusiasm. After singing in the square for more than ten consecutive days, she managed to gather a group of loyal fans — mostly idle, curious children.

"Why are you always singing about Bahamut?" asked the most loyal of her audience, the fishmonger's eldest son.
"Because there are just so many heroic deeds of Bahamut to sing about!"
"Are the horns on your head supposed to be like Bahamut's?"
"Ah, these aren't just for show. They're my real dragon horns!" As soon as she said this, the children burst into laughter. No one took her seriously. They thought this lady was just like those fanatical missionaries from the Luminary Order, a little too obsessed.
In Dragonsaerie, hymns about Bahamut were already sung far and wide, and zealous followers were a common sight — but this person claimed to have dragon horns! Even the children found it too absurd, and soon, they lost interest and dispersed.

Talethia touched her horns in confusion. They were real dragon horns... Why wouldn't even a child believe her?
However, that wasn't her biggest concern. As Bahamut's most beloved daughter, the most revered being in the Everlasting Elysium, and a crystal dragon with the strongest natural connection to the Positive Plane, Talethia couldn't understand why the people of this Material Plane no longer honor her great father — Bahamut the Platinum Dragon God.
It must be because of that detestable Child of Chaos. If he hadn't started a rebellion, her father wouldn't have fallen into a deep slumber, and this world wouldn't have descended into such endless chaos.
Having traveled the Material Plane for some time now, she was certain of her conclusion. The root of all disasters, including the birth of the Child of Chaos, stemmed from Tiamat's inscrutable and evil hobbies.
It was just that with her father still slumbering, no one could stand against these evils. If only there was a chance to awaken him...
Father, please wake up. This world needs you.

story.text:
The Tigerclaw Brigade lived up to its fierce reputation through constant tournaments and combat trials held under any convenient pretext. For fresh recruits — particularly unknown commoners — these bloodsport arenas offered the perfect stage to forge their military reputations.
Yet newcomers often grew perplexed watching General Majtan. While warriors clashed below, their supreme commander would lounge in her elevated viewing post, idly chewing desert grass and honing her claws with apparent disinterest in the spectacle.
When particularly bold fighters dared invite their general to participate, Majtan's response never varied: a booming laugh, a firm refusal, and the would-be challenger unceremoniously hurled back into the fighting pit.

Yet none questioned General Majtan's ferocity in true battle. The languid tigress would erupt into a whirlwind of claws and flame — enemies, obstacles, all opposition shredded to ribbons before her onslaught, then swept away in the blazing blast of her wrath. Observers claimed this was the only time her battle-lust truly awakened, a spectacle never seen in the training yards.
What only Majtan knew was this: her warrior's heart never cooled. But flesh and blood demanded more than play-combat. Once her claws were bared, only spilled blood could sheathe them again — a reality far beyond what arena-tumbling recruits could endure.

Majtan's ascension sparked outrage when the Tiger King named her as the General successor. This bandit-turned-commander, with her soiled past and dishonorable origins, embodied everything the honor-bound tigerfolk despised. Yet the Tiger-in-Crown himself had anointed her — first as his chosen warrior, then as leader of the Tigerclaw Brigade after his departure. By granting her the highest honors, he transformed her stains into virtues. Small wonder the fierce tigress showed such devotion!
Yet the truth of her loyalty lay elsewhere. Not in the jeweled scimitar gifted by her king, but in shared battles fought shoulder-to-shoulder. Not in royal favors, but in the lifeblood the Tiger King had spilled to save her own. These were the bonds no honor could equal, the true source of her undying fealty.

story.text:
From his first breath, Halramar bore fate's cruel jest. In a culture where tigerfolk prized vivid, striking patterns, his coat grew in dull and indistinct. And when one's elder brother — Maashtur — shimmered with nature's most brilliant markings, this misfortune twisted into something far more venomous.
The scorn began with his pelt, Halramar knew. It followed the brothers through every season of their youth, woven into each childhood memory. Perhaps Maashtur himself never meant to slight him. No matter. The bitterness took root regardless — anger first, then hatred, flourishing in shadowed places.
By the time he conceived his grand design to topple the kingdom, all restraints had long since burned away.

Halramar was not skilled in physical combat, but he believed himself to be more adept at plotting schemes than any other tigerfolk. He thought that his fellow tigerfolk had enjoyed the bountiful protection of their god for too long, which resulted in their naivety, stupidity, and thoughtless habits. 
Of course, this was not a critique of the Great River God himself. As long as this silent god remained mum and did not protest his usurpation of the Abbot, he would continue to be his most devout follower — at least more so than his older brother, who did not often attend the Great River Abbey. 
Therefore, when the Tiger King ventured into the depths of the desert in pursuit of the voice of their god without a second thought, he felt more furious than anything — his brother had surpassed him even in the devotion to their god!

Defeat cost Halramar his messenger — the great bird that had ever perched upon his staff.
In fleeting moments of trance, he almost remembered... Had there been guidance in those days? Whispered counsel from beyond, carried on black wings? Visions that first planted the seeds of his grand design?
But memory proved as fickle as the vanished bird. Now, in the endless twilight of his imprisonment, only fragments remained — the ghost of a beak's movement, half-heard mutterings in no tongue he knew...

story.text:
Bloodstained Aurora, Priestess of Blazeland, Harbinger of Doom — the lizardfolk Queen is known by a myriad of names. 
Her ebony figure, dotted by brilliant red scales resembling dying embers, is draped in gold ceremonial robes. Her maniacal prophecies are tainted with the breath of calamity, devoid of mercy, and have never been proven wrong. 
Her subjects, filled with awe and admiration, embrace their fate and revel in wild abandon as they await their inevitable end.

Amongst the coldblooded lizardfolk, Phaessa possesses a rare virtue — compassion. Her noble lineage and powerful gift of prophecy has unquestioningly secured her position as their Queen. Her ability to foresee calamities torments her, but it also fills her with sympathy for the suffering of others. 
However, she refrains from offering them advice. Disasters are inevitable, and her role as prophetess is merely to relay the dictates of fate. 
Thus, she is tolerant towards her blood kin, Khrysos — tolerant towards his animosity, his disdain, and his eventual departure. 
She has already seen the fated end of this arrogant kinsfolk of hers, and silently laments it.

Foretellers of misfortune are often blamed for bringing about calamities, but Phaessa has no intention of correcting this perception: Being a scapegoat for those who suffer misfortune is the role that she was fated to fulfill. 
The pain of a befallen prophecy burns like a flame; she cannot escape it, yet she welcomes it. 
Let Khrysos embrace his luck and conceit; let him fancy himself a child of the gods and arrogate the duties of the divine — Auric Kith Phaessa just gazes upon all the fates, written and set in stone, and willingly heralds the gods' will to the world.

story.text:
Aboard the Free Hatred, few criticisms could be heard of Stoutbeard, and Orfenna was the one responsible for most of them. Her inventive talent and eccentric temperament were like two horses running neck to neck — any attempt to get close to one will inevitably result in being knocked flying by the other. 
Most people chose to give her a wide berth, but Stoutbeard could not and would not do so, for he was almost like a foster father to her — even if Orfenna herself would never ever admit to this. 
Nevertheless, Orfenna had not made any efforts to leave the Free Hatred. Instead, she would vehemently curse it out while simultaneously transforming it into the most powerful airship in the sky.

Not many aerial dwarves interacted with Orfenna. There was a unanimous belief that with her volatile temperament, it would be impossible to predict when she might whip out her peculiar modified gun and take a shot at some innocent soul. 
But in reality, aside from singeing the beards of her elders with electrical currents, Orfenna had never committed any other egregious acts. She simply detested the traditional constraints imposed by her fellow dwarves, and felt that the "Sky Code" of more than two hundred pages had made the aerial dwarves as mundane and mediocre as those conservative dwarves holed up on the ground. 
Why was Stoutbeard, who was able to abandon everything and pioneer the leading of dwarves away from the surface, unable to break free from those rotten rules and regulations? Orfenna could not understand this, and thus grew even more infuriated.

No one could pinpoint exactly when the discord arose, but it had already become too late to be salvaged once the realization hit. 
The fuse that ignited it all was that one mysterious volcano research mission. 
Officially, the objective of the mission was to collect magma for fuel and energy research. Only the members of the strike squad were aware that upon landing, both Stoutbeard and Orfenna had traveled together to investigate a cave that had obvious remnants of dwarven culture, but when they emerged, the atmosphere between them had already plummeted to a freezing degree. 
There were rumors that it had to do with Orfenna's birth, while others claim that it had stemmed from their drastically opposing views regarding the usage of dangerous energy sources. Yet no one had stepped forward to explain the situation, nor had anyone attempted to reconcile their differences. 
Everyone could feel the invisible ideological chasm extending between them, one that only made them drift further and further apart without hope of reconciliation.

story.text:
The sunset over Lumina cast a golden sheen on Irmoush's bone armor. He caressed the bone bow, carved from the rib of a great beast, and stared at the camp not far away.
Irmoush had heard that Grishnaar and his followers were stationed on the plain. Back when they were in the tribe, both Irmoush and Grishnaar were the fiercest of warriors. They always charged at the forefront of battle, their axes cleaving the skulls of their enemies...

Until that one brutal battle, from which Irmoush barely escaped with his life... As the young Grishnaar helped him retreat, no one noticed the light dimming in Irmoush's eyes.
"The Dragon Remains can get you back on the battlefield!" Grishnaar said by the campfire, a purple-black energy dancing in his palm.
Irmoush reached out to touch it. In an instant, he realized it was a dangerously untamable power. "Listen, I can get back to the battlefield on my own strength. Grishnaar, stay away from this... Dragon Remains! I have a feeling it will devour you..."

"Did you hear? A huge battle broke out in Dragonsaerie on the Lumina Plain! An orc turned into a monster...!" When a merchant told Irmoush this, he immediately thought of Grishnaar and the Dragon Remains — that was why Irmoush had come to Lumina.
Before he knew it, Irmoush was at the front of the camp. Soon, he would find out if the orc monster the merchant spoke of was indeed Grishnaar...

story.text:
Blazing sun. Molten rock. Whirling sand. Astaion stood before the towering Sunfire Temple, straining to hear the voice of the God of Sun and Lava as the Great Shaman promised.
Nothing. Only silence, as always. No divine whispers. No visions. Just the same hollow emptiness that had greeted her every previous attempt.
"You lack true devotion," the Great Shaman intoned. "You remain fit only to be a shadow guard — a warrior willing to die for faith, an ascetic. Only through such sacrifice comes salvation."
How tedious, she thought. The same tired script, recited again and again.
Yet the life of a battle-ready guardian didn't displease her. There was honesty in that existence — no false promises, only the clarity of mortal danger.

Astaion had undertaken innumerable life-and-death missions, yet she had never once heard the call of her god in the moments where her life had hung in the balance. However, just as she was about to conclude that she had been abandoned by her god, a young lizardfolk had appeared. 
She was their young queen who looked frail, cowardly, and timid; she seemed to not even be able to speak at a loud volume. Astaion had been assigned as the queen's bodyguard and tasked with the duty of surveillance, which left her feeling wearisome, for staying by the queen's side was the safest place to be. 
However, after yet another failed attempt to listen for the voice of her god, she saw her queen standing behind her, her pupils glowing with a golden light. 
"Do not listen... Do not listen to it." The queen's voice trembled, but was very gentle, "That is not the voice of our god... Do not listen to it."

However, that voice still descended upon her, in the end. 
After San Ramallan's eruption, a crimson glow described as a miracle filled up the entire sky. She seemed to finally hear the indescribable murmurs, those so-called divine calls. Her whole mind was instantly flooded by them, and all sense of reason immediately disappeared. She seemed to experience a spell of torture, yet it also felt like she had been reborn. 
That was definitely the voice of her god — because who else could wield such power? She thought as she returned to the queen's side once more. 
As for the queen... What was she pleading? "Do not listen?" Well... she was just a weakling trembling in vain.

story.text:
Yfeir was born aboard a ship while the wood elves were migrating across the sea. 
According to the account that his father Soveliss gave, the wood elves had been caught in a fierce storm then, but the moment Yfeir came into the world, sunlight broke through the dark clouds and dispersed the tempest. 
Yfeir loved the story of his birth. Perhaps being born at sea made him feel closer to the ocean and the sun than the other wood elves, and he yearned to embark on maritime adventures. 
Yfeir believed that he belonged at sea from the moment he was born.

Even the most brilliant navigators may stumble.
Shivering at the mountain's base, Yfeir clutched his chest. Seven days had passed since his ship foundered on the reefs near this desolate island at the edge of the Aethercairn Archipelago. No food. No tools. Only the dark clouds swallowing the moon, and the crystal against his skin pulsing with a gentle glow — rising, falling with each labored breath.
This crystal had never left him. From birth it had rested here, over his heart.
His father Soveliss had told the fuller tale: How the migrating wood elves, witnessing Yfeir's birth at sea, saw destiny in the newborn. How they'd unanimously bestowed their most sacred relic — the "Radiant Crystal of the Blue Oak" — upon this child of the waves. A living hope that their scattered people might one day return home.

Yfeir loved this precious and beautiful crystal, but to be honest, he was not particularly fond of the heap of expectations that his fellow wood elves had placed upon him. 
Leading the adrift wood elves back to their homeland? 
Born at sea, Yfeir had firmly rooted himself in Driftwood along with his elders. To him, his homeland was this island surrounded by the azure sea, not some distant and gloomy forest. 
Yet in this moment... on this isolated island far away from Driftwood, Yfeir felt a sense of helpless melancholy, like a plant uprooted from its soil, adrift on still seawater, unable to find ground to anchor itself. 
In his daze, Yfeir spotted a distant glow ahead — a gentle, green glow which resonated with the crystal against his chest... 
—So this was the call from his homeland... 
Wait, no, it was light! 
Yfeir rubbed his eyes to confirm that it was indeed a wooden boat headed towards him — and standing at the bow was his father, whom he had not spoken to in ages. 
Yfeir jumped up and sprinted towards the approaching boat.

story.text:
For the secluded human houses of the Scarlet Vale, time seems to flow much faster than in the outside world. Day after day of study and research is the entirety of their lives.
In such an environment, love and hatred are always passed down for much longer.
Just as the Stolperd house's reverence and faith in the white owl have never wavered since ancient times, the birdfolk's hatred for humans has never faded one bit. And the elder of the birdfolk is herself a white owl — "Fredegonda the Frozen".

Fredegonda's title of "The Frozen" is meant literally — she once single-handedly froze the entire birdfolk valley for ten long years. During this time, the valley was completely cut off from the outside world, and no creature could enter or leave.
The cause of all this began, ironically, with the Stolperd house's reverence for the white owl.
The knowledge-seeking humans longed for a wise dialogue with the white owl elder, but never attempted to understand the principles and order of her people. When the self-righteous humans took the first step toward communication, the birdfolk tribe immediately sounded the alarm.

Hatred flows through birdfolk veins as an instinct passed through generations. Though shorter-lived than humans, this emotion has become one with their blood — an unbroken chain stretching endlessly onward.
For Fredegonda, her inheritance was threefold: the century-old memories of ancestors hunted by humankind, the most secluded valleys painstakingly claimed for survival, and that primal instinct declaring their territory inviolable.
Yet decades of isolation brought unexpected consequences — surpassing human predictions while fracturing the tribe from within.
With each passing season, Fredegonda's doubts grew stronger. Did this self-made prison truly serve them? Must their people remain forever shackled to ancient grudges?
Then came the thaw, and with it, the day time truly began moving forward for the birdfolk.

story.text:
"Da-da-la... da-la-la-la-la... da-di-da... Oh, Blinky, you went the wrong way! It's the left fork!"
To a string of light and bright notes, Blinky carries Alaura through the flowers and shadows of the green fields.
Its master possesses eyes as pure as morning dew and a voice that could make stones weep. When Alaura opens her lips to sing, her beautiful, heavenly voice can make the most frenzied fey in the wilderness hold its breath and listen in silence.
Such a little songbird should be universally adored, yet the opposite is true — her appearance is always met with fear and unease.

As the personal messenger of Ravatrix, Lady of Greeneries, Alaura delivers the queen's praises and blessings, but also proclaims her merciless decrees and punishments.
The fey of the Dawn Court still remember the Midsummer Festival when Alaura, cloaked in morning dew, first appeared before them. Her voice flowed like honey, and flower petals danced with it. But the sweet notes she wove were a decree of permanent exile for dozens of fey.
The joyous feast slowly froze, and only Alaura, with the most innocent and guileless expression, continued to sing and sing.

Many have secretly pried into Alaura's past and secrets — her crippled legs, her weak wings — seeking to prove that she is but a tragic plaything, a mouthpiece stripped of freedom, existing only to carry the queen's will.
Ravatrix never tolerates such noisy chatter. Just like that time she passed by a songbird's nest, the high-pitched, loud chirping grating on her ears. She waved her hand, and the entire nest of birds vanished completely.
As she was about to leave, she found one that had slipped through the net in the thorns under the tree — lame, with a damaged wing, on the verge of death, likely abandoned by its parents due to its congenital defects. The bird saw her, too, and yet it managed to force a string of notes at her from its tiny throat.
So she picked the bird up with a flowering branch. "This one, on the other hand, doesn't sound half bad."

story.text:
Miro lightly tapped the stone wall of the underground ruins with his pipe and perked his ears, listening carefully to the reverberating echoes. 
More than three days had already passed since the squad of adventurers he was leading had lost contact with the camp outside. The supplies they were carrying were about to run out, and he had to find the way out before it happened. 
After rechecking the completed map of the ruins, Miro finally found the key to unlocking the mechanism — a hidden chamber concealed in one corner. 
When the warm sunlight finally shone upon their heads once more, Miro's squadmates embraced one another in celebration of their successful exploration, while he lit what remained of his tobacco and took a satisfying puff. 
Yes, indeed, the adrenaline of surviving against all odds was exactly why he became an adventurer in the first place.

There was a saying in the Crimson Crow: Always check your pockets carefully after conversing with Vice Chairperson Miro. 
One never knew how those shiny little metal coins from their wallet disappeared, then reappeared again. 
The Crimson Crow regarded this as a harmless little prank of his, for he always returned the stolen items to their rightful owners. 
But no one knew that the person most troubled by this inborn kleptomania was actually Miro himself.

For the longest time, Miro's family worried that his kleptomania would land him in serious trouble, or perhaps even end up with him being sent to the gallows. 
But Miro found a way to balance his talents and penchant for stealing before he could get into even more trouble — becoming an adventurer. 
Soon, he became a central figure in the Crimson Crow. In the Arbortean Roost, there was even a massive bookshelf dedicated to housing the maps that he had drawn. 
While he was perhaps not the most accomplished adventurer, he was fully worthy of his title as master cartographer.

story.text:
Gaiolere, warden of the City of the Dead, loiters whilst his prey, a sinner's departed soul, cowers within an urn.
Not every soul in this city is pure and innocent. It is only natural that the sinners outnumber the virtuous in this world, and this is one such sinner.
Heavy footsteps flicker from outside the urn, making the departed soul tremble. It knows that the warden named Gaiolere has never shown mercy to his captives, knows that this warden takes a keen delight in tormenting them.

Gaiolere's footsteps fade away.
Just as the departed soul heaves a sigh of relief, the black armor-clad executioner soundlessly materializes beside the urn, and the spectral blue flames wreathed around him seem to scorch the air. Even though Gaiolere has no head, the departed soul senses his sadistic grin.
So this soul, too, joins the chorus of screaming souls caged by the executioner, and lets out its own piteous scream.

Come the Owlestreia Dynasty's end, Gaiolere had already executed a great many condemned. Whilst he did his utmost to avoid harming the innocent, the number of guilty heads decapitated before his own unjust execution proved uncountable.
Gaiolere does not bare hate for death as some living do.
After all, when they were alive, no matter how eager he may have been to torment sinners, they all died in the end, and thus his merriment came to an end. Now, the sinners' souls have no such escape, a matter of great satisfaction to Gaiolere.

story.text:
A masked dancer had arrived at the tavern in the city. Her dancing was magnificent, untrammeled, and exuded a strong exotic grace. 
People drunkenly babbled about her charms after a few drinks in, except for one intoxicated veteran who was drunk to the point of near-unconsciousness, yet recognized her — who fearfully shouted for help. 
No one paid any mind to his slurred accusations, but the veteran's unclothed body was found near the back alley of the tavern the next day, with the words "Traitor" written across his chest with his own fresh blood. 
Calavera wiped her bloodstained fingers with the hem of her blood red skirt. Satisfied, she departed in search of her next target.

Calavera was once not only the empire's finest dancer, assassin, and spy, but also its most beautiful political sacrifice. 
Even after turning into an Undead, she remained the most beautiful of them all. 
She had lost many memories upon awakening from her grave, but the pain of betrayal was still etched deeply in her soul. 
Killing the men who had toyed with her feelings in her quest for revenge gradually became the remedy of her long, undead existence.

"I love you," her admirers had said while presenting her with fresh flowers and precious stones. 
"I love you," those with ill intent had said, disguising their poisons and daggers with honeyed words. 
"I love you," her betrayers had said before handing her over to the nobles' soldiers. 
"I don't love you." Calavera smiled as she danced. Love was the most unreliable thing in the world.
