story.text:
Illusions born of flames leapt from Caspar's fingers and merged together at the edges of the stage. 
They flickered and danced through various shapes, eliciting cheers and applause from the audience. All eyes were fixed on his flames. 
The Director of the Hysteria Troupe guffawed: a talented performer always had a handle on the pulse of their audience. 
He made an exaggerated bow towards them, before announcing the name of the next act.

Caspar the Carefree has held the Director's cane for decades, and (unless some tragic comedy befalls him) shall likely clutch it until Death itself takes the final bow.
"Boredom is the world's greatest sin!" he declares, conjuring spectacles from thin air when life fails to deliver sufficient drama.
Let those so-called upright gentlemen cluck like hens at his artistic choices — why, the poor dears can't even spell "joie de vivre"!
After all, what's there to say to joyless fools, right?

Daylight is also part of his curse. 
Under the sun's scorching radiance, Caspar often feels as if he is under the illusion of being submerged in the flames he creates. But perhaps this isn't a psychosomatic feeling, for the pain he feels is truly unbearable. 
His troupe members are no different — just like him, they are misshapen beings who have been cursed by their bloodline, which is why all of their performances only take place at night. 
Caspar loves creating dialogue with hidden metaphors, as well as improvisation, for it is only through these methods that each new play is fresh and interesting.

story.text:
The icy blade pierced through Hochadir's helmet. A few icy spikes broke off in the freezing wind, but the curse quickly regrew them. 
His horse had carried him for a long time, but neither of them knew how much longer they had to go. 
Hochadir was looking for an island; it was where he had slept for a long time after being brought ashore by his warhorse in Iskalland.

A grim certainty had taken root in Hochadir's heart — his dynasty lay in ruins.
Once, he had sailed aboard the Emperor's vessel, bearing the sacred charge to investigate an isle in Iskalland. The mission failed before it truly began.
They said a slumbering god dwelled within that fickle island — now submerged, now breaching the waves like a dying leviathan. After months of torment, when hope itself had frozen solid, the mists parted to reveal its jagged silhouette.
What fool's errand had they sent him on? This knight, ignorant as a newborn lamb, understood neither the task's grim purpose nor the horrors it would unleash.

Everyone eventually perished, including Hochadir. They screamed in agony as they were corroded by the sea and devoured by the cold, endlessly tormented as they died. 
The first tsunami carried him away, and Hochadir thus escaped from the island. He remembered clearly that he had refused the god, and lost all his memories as a result. 
What was it that he had refused? A flash of fear invaded Hochadir's numb thoughts. What exactly had he refused?

story.text:
"Hey buddy, what did you get yourself into? He totally messed you up!"
In the dirty, stinking water dungeon, the captives would often use the last strength they had to chat with each other, in order to get through the difficult nights.
As one of the most tormented prisoners, Fihrah is not immune to questions. Though she often has little energy to answer them, she will still make an effort to talk when she can.
"I slept with Grishnaar." Fihrah replies in a gruff voice.

Amidst the laughter of the other captives mixed with groans and screams, only Fihrah knows she isn't lying.
Fihrah is the daughter of the former chief and a tough warrior in her own right. She rampaged through her teenage years — not so much a thug, but a bully nonetheless.
But it's not like she has hurt Grishnaar or anything, she has even provided protection to him and his family.
The abuse she's suffering today has nothing to do with what happened between them. It is clear to Fihrah that Grishnaar has completely brushed off the past.

Having gained her freedom, Fihrah isn't at a loss as to the future.
Her father had wanted her to leave when he was alive, but she feels she still has unfinished business.
The tribespeople who suffer because of the fight between Gragrir and Grishnaar need to be resettled, and the divided orc tribes need someone to bring them together again.
Fihrah's decision is not made out of a sense of duty, but rather as a farewell to her once carefree self.

story.text:
Baelvernal's first dream began with merfolk circling a colossal whale skeleton, their haunting songs just beyond her comprehension...
At the center lay a beautiful merfolk — eyes shut, features stilled, even the ocean currents seeming to pause in reverence around her form.
When young Baelvernal described this vision to her mother, the answer came softly: "You witnessed the Ritual of Requital, child. The sea's way of bidding farewell to its own."

"The merfolk in the ritual... she died?" Little Baelvernal's voice trembled as she grappled with this first encounter with mortality.
"Yes, my pearl. But death isn't an ending — it's the sea's way of making room for new life to rise from the old."
"So... Mom became new life?"
A gentle laugh. "Silly child, do I look dead to you? I'm right here."
Baelvernal's small fingers traced her mother's face — the same delicate features, the same sea-glass eyes she'd seen in the dream. "But... it was you lying there. I saw you, Mom."

When her mother's Ritual of Requital unfolded exactly as foretold in her dream, Baelvernal understood at last — her visions were glimpses of fate's unyielding path.
Though the merfolk scoffed at first, the child's gift proved itself cruelly: her dream of a father perishing in grief became reality within a moon's turn.
"Does Baelvernal the witch foresee the future," they whispered in the coral groves, "or does she summon the calamities she sees?" With each hushed debate, their fins carried them further from her.
Yet their fear meant nothing. For in her mind's eye already danced the world's ending — the loveliest vision she'd ever dreamed.

story.text:
The essence of a scimitar dance lies in its leisureliness. 
Tarulla danced to the melodious music, lost in her own performance — treading with light steps, gracefully extending her arms, and rolling her hips. Atop her head perched a dangerous scimitar, its tassels rustling softly as it swayed. 
The audience below the stage stared at her with rapt attention, watching the dim light slip from the point of the blade to her silky skin.

"You're so... so beautiful..." A drunken guest stumbled towards her. He fumbled as he removed a gemstone ring from his finger, and attempted to stuff it into Tarulla's bodice. 
She smiled calmly as she accepted the ring; at the same time, she lightly pressed the scimitar against the drunkard's chest, pushing him away. 
"Even if it's unsharpened, never approach a woman who wields a blade so easily." 
Her gentle movements and charming voice momentarily stunned the drunkard, who did not even register the attendant's repeated apologies as he dazedly gazed at the dancer's skirt disappearing around the corner.

She casually threw the newly obtained ring into a jewelry box, where it collided with the other pieces with a soft clink. 
Putting away her dancing scimitar, Tarulla drew out another and silently wiped down its sharp blade. 
Today, she encountered that guest again. He had already shown up for many consecutive nights, and the design of the Herboh amulet he wore was the same one she saw on that slave trader many years ago. 
For her next performance, she was going to use this sharpened scimitar to present a real dance of blood for her guests' enjoyment.

story.text:
Araces stood quietly at the Queen's side.
He is taciturn, dislikes speaking before others, and nearly always wields a shield to protect the Queen.
Phaessa reassures him that he need not be so uptight amongst his own tribe — were tragedy to strike, it was determined by fate. But still, Araces stands firm in his pledge, day after day, year after year.

Araces trusts no one but Queen Phaessa.
As Araces sees it, the lizardfolk here are being lured into that court jester's antics, and that jester Khrysos — nothing but a fool — treats preposterous prophecies as a divine enlightenment.
Here in the middle of the vast desert, even if none are able to understand the Queen's intentions, Araces shall forever uphold her dignity.

Araces will never forget the snowstorm that night.
In the freezing Iskalland tundra, it was Phaessa who pulled the dying Araces back from the brink of death. Prior to that, undead prowling the area had whispered to Araces, telling him the deities' world had fallen.
Now that divine favor is no longer dependable, the only being in this world he can count on, is the Queen.

story.text:
The woman and child finally trek to the edge of the jungle.
As her feet hit the flat ground, it is as if the woman has finally woken up from her nightmare. She grabs the child's wrist and walks quickly. Without knowing whether it is a mirage or not, she sees the cooking smoke of a settlement drift up from afar.
Her child shakes off her hand. The woman turns back in panic to see her daughter biting her lip and glaring at the wet leaves of the rainforest behind her.
"I will come back for revenge." the tender voice exclaimed, "You will pay for your crimes."
The woman's heart almost stops, knowing Kyrza's cruelty — she's seen with her own eyes how her husband has died. She curls up and closes her eyes as she gathers her daughter in her arms.
But the girl doesn't close her eyes as she sees the film on the pupils of the lizardfolk's eyes contract and slide rapidly. After a rustle, the lizardfolk disappears, and the girl hears the reply before she leaves,
"I'll be waiting."

Kyrza's career began at an early age.
Of the many raiders in the swamps, Kyrza and her squad are considered the most efficient and well-regarded. She selects her targets with great care, operating only when the risks are manageable, so there are never any missteps.
Kyrza pillages the victim's possessions, and to ensure there will be no future retaliation, she sadistically and indiscriminately kills all the men, leaving only the women and children.
Her compassion manifests in her escort. She takes the vulnerable ones who are unable to survive in the rainforest to the fringe, ensuring they do not die by her hand, be it directly or otherwise.
It seems unnecessary, but Kyrza's underlings dare not be foolish enough to question it. They know only too well: Kyrza requires obedience, nothing more.

Claiming one life or claiming many, there is no difference. Once the killing and plundering begin, they never stop.
Kyrza has trouble remembering exactly how it all started. Seething hatred had once boiled her cold blood. When she lifted her enemy's head in her hands, cold blood spattered all over her, only then did the turmoil settle.
Having taken one life, it stood to reason that she should take more. Those were turbulent, wild, fulfilling days, but unfortunately they failed to rekindle the fire in her blood.
As the thrill of slaughtering her foes faded out of memory, a thought struck her suddenly:
If there are someone able to exact revenge on her, whose hatred-filled gaze is cast upon her, then perhaps, that rush of boiling blood may be recaptured once again...

story.text:
Seidic slowly runs his fingertips over the coarse surface of the chart, encircling tiny marks on it with his fingertip.
Those marks, despite their considerable quantity, only occupy a fraction of the sheet.
This is the wellspring from which the gnome merchant Seidic's wealth flows, and from which he draws his water. But he is not reckless in his usage, carefully conserving the water vein.
The draft illustrates in meticulous detail exactly where Aethercairn's waters hold their ores, slumbering in the depths, simply awaiting Seidic's excavation.

Following years of grappling and sparring on the seas, Seidic has become a prominent merchant in Aethercairn's waters.
In terms of operation, he is regarded as somewhat conservative in his approach. That is not to suggest that his methods are charitable — Don't be silly, now! Is anyone really squeaky clean when it comes to running such a business?
Simply, in contrast to the unregulated rabble, he maintains a steady grasp on his business, not biting off more than he can chew when it comes to pace and scope.

Seidic regards most of his peers with contemptuous disdain.
Any gnome possessing true intellect understands sustainability's importance — one mustn't slaughter the golden goose through reckless exploitation.
Such relentless plundering of the seas invites inevitable catastrophe. Though armed with detailed ore charts and the finest excavation equipment, Seidic maintains cautious restraint.
Oh, he harbors no illusions about fools reforming their ways; he simply prays their downfall won't engulf him as well!

story.text:
Ashqar burst into the room, waving a lanyard attached to a badge. "Sis! I did it! I got accepted into the Tigerclaw Brigade!" 
The young tiger could hardly contain his excitement, and felt a strong urge to sharpen his claws on the colorful door panel of the house. 
But his sister — the beautiful tigress before him — simply hurled a copper pestle at his head. "Shut up, Ashqar! Grind these spices into powder!" 
Despite his sister's ruthless disregard, Ashqar only broke into a silly grin and obediently picked up his tools and got to work.

Ashqar viciously ripped apart the throat of the last enemy. Gruesome shreds of flesh hung from his fangs, while blood had thoroughly matted his fur. With the conclusion of this intense battle, the elite squad of the Tigerclaw Brigade began to clean up the battlefield and gradually make their way home. 
"Ashqar? Where are you going?" asked a curious battle mate nearby, who noticed that his squad leader was heading straight to the reservoir in the deserted village. 
"I'm going to take a bath," replied Ashqar earnestly. "The last time I went back like this, my sister gave me a good thrashing."

In Ashqar's memories, his sister Shahla filled the roles of both father and mother, and assumed the responsibilities that came with them both.
Following the massacre of their caravan by minotaur bandits, the surviving tigerfolk siblings began their harsh journey of survival. The young female tigerfolk sold spices, worked as a dancer, hunted beasts, fed the junior Ashqar with meat from the crevices of her own fangs, and paved the way for him to join the Tigerclaw Brigade, the symbol of honor and strength.
Even many years later, Ashqar, now captain of the Tiger King's royal guard, would still look forward to his sister's homemade delicacies on his triumphant journeys home.

story.text:
Pearl carefully transplanted the seaweed saplings into the crevices of the reef rocks before casting a spell to ward off small fish and mollusks to prevent them from nibbling on her precious saplings. 
These seaweeds, which had been selected and cultivated over many years, possessed potent toxins, but were extremely delicate — even the slightest change in the temperature of the water could cause them to die. 
To cultivate more robust adult seaweed, she had no choice but to leave her hometown for these distant waters, and tend to these weak saplings in solitude. 
This was the task that her teacher had left her before parting for her journey to the deep sea.

Pearl's magic stemmed from parsing seaweed characteristics, with each new species of seaweed adding new possibilities to her spells. 
To date, she has cultivated many new varieties of seaweed. Some could fluoresce autonomously at night, some could thrive near underwater volcanoes, and some could be extracted for their sweet juices. 
But none were more dangerous than the seaweed in her hand — it contained natural neurotoxins, and only a tiny sliver was required to tranquilize an entire surfbeast. "This will be my greatest masterpiece!" murmured Pearl to herself as she scrutinized the sapling before her.

It had been ages since Pearl had returned home. Her saplings were still too fragile, and could not be left without her care. 
She longed for her cottage in her distant homeland, where the sunlight streamed through the cracks in the spiral shell walls onto the floorboards, casting patterns that swayed with the waves. 
Beside her bed were her research materials, each sheet bearing the traces of her hard work. 
What Pearl did not know was that those beautiful things had already ceased to exist.

story.text:
Mera believed that there were inaccuracies in the contents of the sheen elves' historical annals. 
According to the records: Moon Goddess Monelisse — the goddess of light who guards the Everlasting Elysium — possesses the pure power of radiance. 
According to the records: 5,000 years ago, Moon Goddess Monelisse erected the Silvery and Dusky Towers — with the Silvery Tower representing radiance, and the Dusky Tower representing necrosis. 
According to the records: Sheen elves are prohibited from entering the Dusky Tower where the power of necrosis was dense. 
According to the records... Mera thought to herself, why would the Moon Goddess who possessed the pure power of radiance be able to erect the Dusky Tower of necrosis? Why were the sheen elves, the children of the Moon Goddess, forbidden from entering the Dusky Tower?

"That's enough. Stop with those doubts, or at least don't say them aloud!" 
Kailes, the librarian of the Increscenta Library who was considerably uneasy with Mera's thoughts, urged kindly. "Do you know how dangerous your remarks are? The Tribunal has eyes everywhere on Increscenta, and the last scholar who claimed that the Dusky Tower was not the Moon Goddess's creation spent a century in prison." 
—Well, I suppose he was charged with "tarnishing the purity of the sheen elves' faith" or something. 
Mera scoffed inwardly, even as new doubts surged within her... 
If the pure power of radiance was truly worthy of reverence, why would the Moon Goddess also erect the Dusky Tower of necrosis in addition to the Silvery Tower?

"Did you hear? A deep elf broke into Increscenta yesterday and started a big protest... and was executed on the spot by the royal guards." 
In the library, Kailes and Mera had begun discussing recent events. 
"Oh... What did she say?" 
A bored Mera flipped through the pages of her book. The deep elves and sheen elves had been enemies for millennia, so it was unsurprising that a deep elf who had trespassed into sheen elf territory would meet such an end. 
"It's all a bunch of nonsense... That trespasser was shouting about how the Moon Goddess and sheen elves are thieves who stole the power of Spider Mother Cyril to construct the Dusky Tower. Personally, I think she must've been hysterical." 
Mera paused her flipping. In that split second, she had a feeling that she had found the key to unraveling the mystery... 
The Moon Goddess and the Spider Mother, the Silvery Tower and the Dusky Tower... Why were the sheen elves, the children of the Moon Goddess, forbidden from entering the Dusky Tower? 
"What's wrong?" asked Kailes nervously, "Did I say something wrong?" 
"Nothing." Her lips slowly lifted in a faint smile. "Nothing at all."

story.text:
The fox sensed the scent of death. It kicked its hind legs to flee... but after just a few leaps, a sharp arrow pierced its heart!
Dielke put away his bow, walked toward the warm prey, and slung it over his neck.
As the best hunter in the village, Dielke has filled his home with pelts, but he never did it for money. It was simply a way of life.
What is taken from nature will one day be returned. Life is a ceaseless cycle, and he is a part of it.

"Winter is coming, and my newborn has no warm clothes," A fellow villager came to Dielke for help.
"Perfect timing. I just came across a big one recently," Dielke said, taking out a tiger skin that was drying in the corner.
"No, no, this is too valuable. You should keep it for yourself," the villager refused.
"A child's first clothes must be made from the pelt of a fierce beast. Before winter, bears come down the mountain for food and often prey on children. The tiger skin will protect him." As he spoke, Dielke wrapped the pelt in bark and handed it to the villager.
In return, Dielke received two well-made stone axes. Bartering was common in Eulestein.

Like all the elders in Eulestein, Dielke could never forget that brutal war against the orcs.
As a master archer, he had used the advantageous mountaintop as his position and survived the battle. But he had also witnessed the warriors of Eulestein being trapped in the orcs' formation and then brutally slaughtered.
Among them were Errich's parents. After the war ended, he took the young Errich to the battlefield.
Errich asked him, "Why can't we make such elaborate traps? If we could learn their strengths, would my parents not have died?"
Dielke did not know how to answer. Perhaps... perhaps so. But Eulestein had always been this way — closed off, stubbornly guarding their valley and land.

story.text:
Pargu heard an inhuman voice emerging from the cage.
The minotaur apathetically peered in through the cell door made of special metal. A face radiating mania emerged from the shadows.
The prisoners housed within this gaol deep within the Vale are largely wizards. Some, seduced by evil knowledge; others, plumbed secrets nigh unspeakable.

In all his time, Pargu has never seen a single prisoner make release.
He has been the watchman here for many years, virtually at one with the eerie, frigid atmosphere.
Through those long hours, Pargu himself feels imprisoned in a cell, just like those behind the doors here.
As per the wizard family's contract, the likelihood of him ever leaving here is miniscule.

The watcher bore his own sins.
To cleanse the filth from his hands, to follow his conscience's call, to atone — Pargu forged an unequal pact with humankind.
His people reaped the benefits, and Pargu harbored no resentment.
All who pry into forbidden knowledge in this secluded Vale meet the same fate, regardless of race. But unlike the maddened prisoners weeping in their cells, Pargu never knew regret.

story.text:
A drop of glowing cave water dripped onto Cervinia's dagger, reminding her of the wretch from the Corruption Cliff she had dealt with a few days ago. His blood had splattered on her dagger just like this. Cervinia wiped the dagger, her pupils reflecting the spider totem drawn by magic — it was an urgent summons from General Quaesitia.
The soldier who delivered the message curiously asked about the details of her mission. Cervinia, as a warning, left a bloody mark on the soldier's neck. "You just need to tell the general that her shadow blade never misses."

This time, the target was a priest who attempted to leak secrets to outlanders. He was now hanging upside down among the stalactites, his broken ribs piercing through his black robe. The tip of Cervinia's foot crushed the end of the spell he was trying to chant, and her poisoned dagger slowly cut through the flesh along his spine. "You have squandered General Quaesitia's trust." She nailed his screams to the blade that suddenly pierced the back of his head, her movements as precise as carving a crystal.
When the guards rushed into the cave with torches, they only saw a spiderweb pattern made of entrails on the rock wall, and a flayed head pinned in the center — this was Cervinia's final mercy for the traitor.

In the empty royal court, Cervinia knelt before Quaesitia's throne. The general's gaze swept over the burns on Cervinia's cheek, a parting gift from the dying priest.
"Be more decisive. Don't give them a chance to fight back." The displeasure in Quaesitia's tone made all the guards in the court hold their breath.
"As you command." When Cervinia presented the bloodstained priest's emblem, Quaesitia finally showed a hint of a smile. Cervinia knew she was still the general's most trusted subordinate.

story.text:
The midday sun baked the sandstone of the Great River Altar until it smelled of salt. Balsaazer stood before several tigerfolk soldiers. "No one enters without the shaman's permission." The warning in Balsaazer's tone carried a sulfurous heat, and his axe pointed directly at the Tigerclaw emblem on the soldiers' armor.
The tigerfolk soldiers frowned, questioning Balsaazer, "What is the Abbey doing..."
"Allow me to answer your questions myself. Balsaazer, let them pass." Halramar's voice came from within the palace behind them, his serpent-scale staff half-hidden behind a pillar.
Balsaazer meekly bowed his head.

The signs of struggle and the stench of blood on the altar had been thoroughly cleaned by Balsaazer. Just as he was about to leave, Halramar emerged. "The divination shows that my brother will soon face a disaster of life and death."
Balsaazer's pupils contracted into vertical slits, his fur settling as he bowed his head to Halramar. "Anzuluvon should have had a new ruler long ago. I am at your service."

Maashtur's disappearance left the Tigerclaw soldiers anxious, but Balsaazer stood like a rock at the entrance to the Abbey. When the Royal Tiger Guard's spear touched his throat, Balsaazer let out a low, rumbling laugh. "Your Tiger-in-Crown will not be returning."
The ground suddenly shook violently. A major commotion seemed to have broken out outside the Great River Altar. Through the dust-filled air, the last thing Balsaazer saw was Halramar's figure standing on a distant rock hill.

story.text:
Deeno stared at the incessantly chattering Journ and couldn't help but interrupt him. "Listen up, scientist, this is a military outpost, not your research lab. I should be the one giving orders here, not you." 
"But you're the one who invited me out here to help you. If you require my assistance, then you should be the one listening to me. I can guarantee that if you use the bomb that I've just developed, we'll be able to blow up every single one of those damned ratfolk right away, easy as pie." 
"But this bomb is dangerous, isn't it? Can you guarantee that its mechanisms and tracker won't malfunction and hurt our own people?" This silenced Journ at last.

"We want to teach those ratfolk a lesson, but there's no need to risk the lives of our allies." Deeno patted Journ's shoulder. "Let's try a less dangerous approach first. If that fails, we can then consider the bomb method." 
"Fine, let's use a more conservative approach then. This is my new invention." Journ produced a vial of green potion. "Even the ratfolk won't be able to withstand the effects of this poison. I accidentally discovered this during an experiment when..." 
"Alright, I'll listen to your experimental process when I've got time to spare on another occasion." Deeno took the vial from Journ's hands. "Right now, we have a patrol to conduct outside."

Deeno's squad discovered a ratfolk who had snuck into Delver's Deep and was hiding in a secret cave. During the pursuit, Deeno's arrow missed its mark and only grazed the arm of the ratfolk, leaving a shallow bloody wound. 
"I'm a nimble ratfolk from Ticky-Town! You can't catch me!" sneered the ratfolk as he ran — but in the next second, he collapsed. 
"What's going on?" The face of the fallen ratfolk was twisted in pain. "How did I..." 
"It's your turn to have a taste of poison now!" Stepping on the ratfolk's tail, Deeno took aim at his heart and let loose a fatal arrow.

story.text:
Ghellid is predisposed to illness, making him much weaker than a typical goblin.
In the unforgiving subterranean caverns where food is scarce, Ghellid finally spots a rotting apple that can fill his belly. But before he can sink his teeth in, a fist greets his face, knocking him to the ground. The fruit he holds is snatched away by another goblin.
"Heeheehee! Weedy, scabby wretches deserve to starve to death! Let me kick you around a bit and I'll show you a little pity." Shrill cackling rings through Ghellid's ears. A vicious kick connects with his gut, blood filling his vision... He collapses to the ground, unconscious.
Ghellid doesn't have any recollection of who rescued him. When he awakens again, he is surprised to find a deliciously basket of bread beside him.

To survive, Ghellid had no choice but to clamber out of the cave and gather a variety of medicinal herbs. First, he had small creatures sample them, before gobbling them down himself.
A myriad of flavors, bitter and sweet, rolled around his tongue. Innumerable times he was poisoned and fell unconscious, his whole body aching, his life on the line... Without knowing which day it was, or which herb had taken effect, Ghellid felt that his body was steadily replenishing itself.

The moment his experiment succeeded, the foul stench of herbs permeating the room, a warped delight swelled within his heart.
At last! He possessed the power to command his own destiny! Without a peep or a sound, all those wretches who has bullied him so — he'd poison them all!
The medicinal herbs that saved his life had become a deadly herbal poison. Ghellid watched as his enemies writhed on the ground, with a sneering, sinister leer on his face.

story.text:
As the leaves of the last Rune Tree in Sythairelan turned yellow, the idea of "migration" once again crept into Thalorian's mind. 
The wood elf migration plan was no longer a secret within Sythairelan. With the decay of the Blue Oak and Nythurys's thousand-year silence, the wood elves had lost the protection of their ancestors whose souls were rejected from the Grand Cycle. Now, even survival had become a problem... 
"Let's leave Nytheria and look for a new home." ——Thalorian could no longer remember which wood elf had uttered these words, which was initially regarded as a mad idea that no one accepted. But it had planted a seed within them... The destruction of the altars, the mutating monsters, and the pervasion of the poisonous swamp were devastating Nytheria's forest and corrupting both the bodies and souls of the wood elves. 
Until today... "Migrate, and leave Nytheria" had now become a choice that no wood elf could ignore.

Led by Soveliss, the faction of wood elves supporting the migration plan had already chosen the location of their new home — the Aethercairn Archipelago in the Misty Sea, hailed as the last sanctuary in Adenthia. 
In addition to preparing food and tools, the lengthy migration required powerful warriors to protect and escort the group. Being the captain of the Sythairelan guards, Thalorian was the best candidate for executing this plan. 
As the day of departure approached, it became increasingly urgent to make a decision. 
Thalorian did not consider himself to be as devout as his old friends Ivellios or Vicuc, and did not think it a good idea to stay behind in Nytheria to await the revival of their god. His only thought was to protect his kinfolk, yet choosing one group meant abandoning the other.

"Oh, you should go, of course. What's there to hesitate about?" 
On the eve of his departure, Thalorian told his old friends of his decision. He knew that his friends would not interfere with his choice, but their frank support had caught him off guard. 
"Vicuc and I won't be leaving Nytheria out of duty, and we couldn't ask for a better leader than you." 
"We were actually worried if anyone else would be up for the task if you weren't willing to go." 
"I've heard that the Misty Sea is beautiful. I'm so tired of looking at Sythairelan's forest." 
The old friends broke into laughter and toasted Thalorian's departure heartily. Clutching his electrorum, Ivellios slumped onto the table and began snoring loudly, which made Vicuc tear up with laughter. He raised his glass towards Thalorian. 
"This shall be our last drink, old friend." 
"May we reunite at the other end of the Grand Cycle."

story.text:
Just as the Wolfthorn Village is hidden in the shadows of the Scarlet Vale, so do the werewolves live cautiously in gloomy corners. They constantly restrain themselves, suppressing their desires, only releasing a sliver of their wildness through howls when the deep, dark night falls.
In such a tribe, Varathas is an anomaly. He cannot contain the hot blood flowing through him. Nor can he easily suppress his hateful and pointless emotions.
He envies the powerful werewolves who maintain their stability through ascetic practice; their silence, restraint, and controlled bloodlust are always so captivating.
And the most outstanding among them is the great alpha, Saverio.

To young Varathas, Saverio had always seemed weak.
What was a werewolf if not master of the curse singing in his blood? Their kind wore chains of their own making — pain to leash the madness, discipline to harness the beast.
When they spared humans, it was through clenched teeth, from disdain not deference.
Yet Saverio sang praises of human wisdom. The alpha himself urged closer ties with those reclusive mages of the Vale.
Did their leader truly fear book-bound spellweavers? The question gnawed at Varathas like moonrise hunger.

Varathas's perception was completely overturned on that full moon.
It should have been an ordinary night, the self-binding ritual proceeding as scheduled, but the guardian warriors responsible for patrolling and stabilizing their kin were nowhere to be found.
The young Varathas had never undergone the ritual alone. Without the smoke of the wolfthorn fruit and the shaman's prayers, he felt himself growing more and more disoriented. At some point, he left the binding room, his reason and consciousness slipping away together. He could not clearly remember what happened next.
It was not until the light of the full moon burned his eyes that Varathas snapped back to his senses. An imposing figure came into view — it was Saverio. He stood before Varathas, facing the full moon and letting out a continuous howl. His voice, full of reason, called Varathas's consciousness back.
From that day on, Varathas never again questioned any of the alpha's decisions. He named himself — the Loyal Wolfclaw.

story.text:
"Your Majesty, should it please you, my skull awaits your scepter's touch. Every drop of my blood is yours to spill."
Thus spoke Molothorn — the deep elf who rose from gutterborn obscurity to become Sacredeia's most trusted guardian. His methods? Unquestionably... exceptional.
At the quarterly treasury inspection, all watched as he ceremoniously sealed away the queen's priceless "Spider Mother's Ring". "The sacred duty is done," he declared. "Now guard this coffer with your lives." His tone brooked no argument as he dismissed the other sentries.
None noticed the suspicious weight swinging at his hip as he swept from the vault.

Molothorn learned a truth from a young age: all things are cyclical. Even if the monarchy is supreme and immortal, the scepter cannot remain in one person's hands forever.
When the queen's whereabouts became unknown and General Quaesitia forced open the royal court's gates with an iron fist, all the queen's guards and confidants were beheaded amidst panic and wavering loyalty.
As expected, a blade was held to Molothorn's neck. He knelt solemnly, holding out his hands. "Valiant general, I have a gift for you."
Looking at the "Spider Mother's Ring", which held immense divine power, Quaesitia finally deigned to look at him properly. "Where did you get this?"
"Reporting to the general, it is the will of the gods. They entrusted me to give this to you."
Amidst Quaesitia's satisfied laughter, Molothorn knew this deadly predicament had taken a turn.

To escape certain death and then be forbidden from ever setting foot in the Unyielding Silk again — Molothorn was quite satisfied with this outcome.
If one day the missing queen returned, he could tearfully recount his "loyalty", how he had been in exile for her for years and never thought of accepting General Quaesitia's grace.
And if the queen never returned, then his new business could continue legitimately.
Molothorn took the foul-smelling bag from the Three Ears. A new batch of hallucinogenic mushrooms was ready. He would distribute this new stock throughout Teneebria, or perhaps — to even wider places.

story.text:
A pinch of bark powder, a drop of snake venom, a few grass seeds, and a turtle-dove feather...
Dargo hums as he puts them into the potion canister one after another and stirs them well. The ingredients gradually melt into a clear liquid that looks no different from water.
He casually grabs a handkerchief, wipes up the spilled potion, and throws it out of the window. The grass there would wither from the toxin in a few days, but he doesn't care.
He puts a label on the canister and carefully places it in the medicine cabinet, waiting for the poison to ferment.
The creation of artwork requires patience after all.

Many poisoners in the rainforest are masters of killing upon a single hit, and they're good at creating puddles of oozing black blood and shrill screams from their prey.
Dargo considers himself different: he is not an assassin, just an herbalist. His research is not meant for intrigue or violence but simply to explore the principles of life and demise.
Only the most colorless and odorless poison would allow him to scrutinize and record the entire process from life to death.

Many nobles and high officials sought poisons from Dargo. After all, when seeking to extricate oneself from treacherous schemes, nothing serves quite like venoms subtle and slow — those that wither the frame in shadow, leaving no trail for accusers to follow.
But Dargo asked no coin for his craft. His price was a logbook — a meticulous chronicle detailing the gradual decline and eventual death of the poisoned individual.
Within the pages of his manual reside accounts of kings whose sons turned fratricidal before their father succumbed to malaise; of magnates stripped of wealth by trusted hands… Poisons, as he knew, ravage not only the flesh but consume the spirit whole.

story.text:
Chitter felt that the world was unfair to him, as his endeavors seemed to constantly hit a wall. 
First, his former peer, Rook, surpassed him in both prestige and power, and even became their Boss. Meanwhile, he had to pledge allegiance to Rook in exchange for benefits. 
The feeling of serving a former rival was sickening, but what pained Chitter even more was hearing the ratfolk praise how loyal and capable he was, as Rook's subordinate!

The second injustice befell him when Twitch's parents perished. Those fools had wrought chaos, forfeiting both Rook's favor and their own lives. By ratfolk custom, their Velobactin trade should have fallen to his paws.
Instead, he inherited no lucrative enterprise — only a wheezing little rat! His gaze rested on the bewildered scrap of fur, as forsaken as he was. For a moment, the impulse to sink his teeth into its neck seized him.
But Chitter stayed his wrath. The time was not ripe. To break Rook's grip, he would need Twitch — and for that, the runt must live.

The third and final injustice arrived just as victory seemed assured. He had won over Whisk, the albino executioner, and manipulated the dim-witted apprentice Twitch. All was unfolding precisely as designed.
Divide them, sow discord — then strike from the shadows, usurping power as he had so many times before.
Then an outlander, emerging from the gloom as though born of it, shattered his designs utterly. And as his ambitions, his grudges, and his very life dissolved into emptiness, a single vision surfaced unbidden: the wide, uncomprehending eyes of a young Twitch.
So this was Fate’s parting jest.

story.text:
Taldie can "see" into the distant future. 
Underneath the snow-capped mountains near Nytheria, a skeleton lay asleep. The Unstill reported this to his superior, Scharlach, and they were both satisfied. With this information, the cult could soon execute the next step in their plan. 
Taldie had been silent for too long, and was eager to see new changes.

The young man had lost his eyes.
Long before they vanished, Taldie had endured relentless sickness, yet the phantoms plaguing his mind proved more terrifying still.
Even with eyelids shut, visions besieged him — scenes torn from disparate eras and worlds. After that rain-drenched night, Taldie's eyeballs were gone. They vanished without a trace, departing without the courtesy of pain — almost as though they possessed wills of their own, and chose to depart from their sockets.

Taldie had searched endlessly, and at last discovered them there — within that barren, forgotten courtyard.
Though blindness made such a task nearly impossible, his arcane training provided alternatives: spells to perceive without true sight. First came the smell — decay, filth, a choking miasma. Then, the orbs themselves, moving like pale grubs, wormed their way from the altar back into the hollows of his face.
Right after, in a single instant, his entire awareness flooded with what they had witnessed beyond the Material plane — stars, chaos, deities… all of it, in a flicker, for eternity.

story.text:
"The tempo is too fast. Elven music should be calm and refined..."
"Your voice is good, but the music you wrote is not classy enough."
Of course Narzilla knows that, but why elven music has to be modest and elegant? There should also be songs for joy and happiness, dedicated to the flowers, the plumecat... and everything on Increscent!
Wouldn't that be considered good music?

Alone on another midnight shift, facing the vastness of the ocean, Narzilla hums the song she has just written during the day.
Suddenly, a voice emerges behind the reef: "Your song is as beautiful as you are. May I have the honor of accompanying you?"
That outlander bard, Alton, is the first person other than her parents to appreciate Narzilla's song.
Soulful, genuine, appealing, and full of hope... Hearing so many sincere compliments, Narzilla is determined to continue her singing.
Music should never be contained anyway.

Becoming a guard on Increscent wasn't Narzilla's dream at first until she witnessed the brutal war firsthand.
Countless kinsfolk died during the war. Her own father survived but has been bedridden ever since.
Narzilla begins to understand that someone has to guard their homeland and that it is her duty to do so.
Being a guard does not mean she has given up her dream of singing; on the contrary, she knows very well that music can only flourish in peace.

story.text:
"Gragrir has lived a life of dishonor." — If orcs, like humans, would create biographies of their rulers, he has already anticipated what would be written on his page.
Everyone agrees that when he was the chief, he trampled on the dignity and honor of all orcs by relocating the clan and avoiding battles.
Orcs will rather die in battle than run away from fighting — many of the tribespeople believe so, though Gragrir thinks the opposite.

Gragrir's second act of shame comes when he is defeated by Grishnaar. Instead of dying an honorable death in battle, he flees and survives.
Grishnaar is already a madman and cares nothing for old friendships or goodwill. Gragrir realizes this the moment the curse is etched into his body.
He must live and be of use to Grishnaar for his daughter to have a chance of surviving.

Gragrir betrayed his honor for the third and final time as his clan faced renewed peril — dying silently inside a nameless cavern.
In his last fleeting breaths, a vision rose before him: his younger self, triumphant over the former chieftain, claiming the fanged throne as his own.
He had been a champion who stood against legions, a chieftain driven by purpose. Yet, as burning wood must turn to ash, so too did his legacy fade into the unforgiving dark.

story.text:
Theohein stands in front of the towering new machine, listening to the steady hum of its bearings. She has been standing motionless for an entire night, verifying a single piece of data after making adjustments to a component.
Her dedication is commendable, though it often keeps others at arm's length.
What they don't know is that she rarely stays this focused throughout the whole process of an experiment. Often, in the dull stretches of waiting, she will allow her mind to wander and concoct groundbreaking, sometimes radical ideas.
She will then dismiss them, for she well knows the limitations of contemporary technology.

Her return from Mekkashon brought more than just these musings; memories of colleagues who perished in an accident haunted her. Were they truly friends, or merely collaborators?
She had regarded them as nothing more than aids in her quest for inventions, their names barely leaving a mark in her memory. The explosion had claimed Victor's daughter as well, whose face Theohein struggled to recall.
Probably a cute little girl like Donella, she thought.

"Madam, it's time!" A bright, youthful voice pulls Theohein from her reverie. She responds with a slow nod toward the newest apprentice.
Ever since Donella began admitting more students, the workshop grows steadily less silent — where once only master, apprentice, and automatons stirred amidst its stillness.
Now, though she often finds the clamor excessive, its persistent hum does manage to drown out the invasive whispers seeping from the chaotic void.
Some visions still lie beyond her sole capability — but she no longer stands alone.

story.text:
Tatoth laughed, a grating noise that seemed to have no end.
"Give me another!" The goblin drove his foot hard into the ribs of the frail tribesman sprawled before him — the victim of his own crude strike. Leaning down, he hissed, "Don't pretend. I know you've got more. Speak! Or you'll learn what real misery tastes like."
And soon enough, spurred by fresh tales told in trembling, pain-choked tones, Tatoth was shuddering once more with cruel delight.

In this goblin settlement, Tatoth is no different from the other goblins. 
Greedy and cunning, he bullies the weak as much as he fears the strong. He never thinks beyond the next two days, and cannot be bothered to remember what he has done the day before. Tatoth lives in the present, with a fresh zest for life every day. 
Aside from his odd sense of humor, Tatoth blends into his tribe like a drop of water in the ocean, and nobody can tell that he is any different.

Nothing pleased Tatoth more than a good jest — indeed, it was the lone spark of light in his otherwise bleak existence.
Time and again, the goblin had crept into gatherings of other folk, lingering in fire-cast shadows to catch the rise of laughter. He had snatched and pilfered countless volumes of comedic lore, yet none could sate his hunger.
More — always more. These days, he craved the exclusive sort best: the rare tales woven solely by the Storyteller.

story.text:
Careth is the bravest woman warrior of Iskalland. People call her the Iskalland Eagle. She is indeed as valiant and resilient as an eagle.
Unlike most people, Careth possesses a keen eye for detail and a silver tongue.
She knows not only how to solve problems, but also to make everyone calm down and ensure a perfect outcome.

Many lend their quiet support to Careth, hoping to see her ascend as the clan's next Elder. They trust not only in her command during battle, but also in her capacity to reconcile with the Frostbeard Clan.
Although Careth herself shows little desire for the title, this swell of backing has drawn unwanted attention.
For in the game of power, even latent contenders cannot be suffered to remain.

All were stunned when Careth accepted the assignment to the Icebound Rift without protest — an infamous haunt of malevolent spirits, plagued by endless tempests and crawling with foul monsters. To venture there alone bordered on madness.
Yet again, Careth proves her worth. With aid from a certain Traveler, she succeeds in cleansing the rift of its curse and silencing the raging winds.
As the wraith fell beneath her blade, a new conviction ignited within her: she would contend for the station of elder and forge a future worthy of her clan.

story.text:
Gegnu tapped his elder brother Dallbam's arm wordlessly, the rough crystals attached to his arm colliding with his brother's equally hardened one with a crisp sound. 
Dallbam seemed to still be immersed in the frenzy of digging the mine, but snapped out of it a little at his younger brother's tap. 
"Let's go, Brother, it's time for us to head up," said Gegnu as he swung the claw hammer in his hands. 
The two brothers supported each other as they left the mine — they had stayed too long, and no one else was waiting for them.

Gegnu and his brother stumbled upon it together, deep in the mineshaft — drawn too close by a shimmering stone that pulsed with unnatural allure.
Down in the Hypogean District, curses flow not only from the mouths of the defeated — sometimes the land itself births such blighted things.
Slowly, relentlessly, crystal formations spread across their forms, embedding deeper with each passing day. Yet neither Gegnu nor Dallbam paid it much mind.

Gegnu had a premonition, but he kept it to himself. 
Before they got close to the gem, he had vaguely sensed a twisted aura emanating from it — temptations, opportunities, fortune. It was bewitching the two brothers, but Gegnu didn't speak up. 
The gnome brothers were interested in nothing but mining, and Gegnu believed that Dallbam would also share the same view: since they had already seen it, why not touch it too?

story.text:
Nessa raised her longsword and swept it cleanly through the air.
At this hour, the shores of the archipelago were deserted, free from judging elven eyes. Here, she could move with uninhibited grace, her motions reflecting the vibrant strength of a warrior in her prime — secure in her identity and devoted to her craft.
Still, beyond the steel and sweat, lay other aspirations yet unspoken.

Her parents had departed this world long ago, leaving Nessa to be nurtured by the broader kinship of the isle — raised communally by the archipelago elves.
Thus nurtured, her loyalty flows as naturally as the tide, and her upbringing has forged a cruelty toward foes that comes without question.
While studying combat, she sometimes attended lectures by Thelendor, and upon finishing her preparation, entered the ranks of the Royal Guard.

Despite her absolute loyalty to the lord of the Increscenta, Nessa doesn't completely agree with his beliefs. 
As a young island elf who has just reached adulthood, she has always harbored a sense of curiosity about the outside world. During her leisure time, she often goes out to the archipelago's beach by herself to stare across the sea, hoping to communicate with other races. 
Nessa yearns to set out on a journey, but with the current state of affairs, she has no inkling when that day will come.

story.text:
Coins clink with a crisp sound as the pleased Vex weighs them in her hand before slipping them into her pocket.
The ratfolk in the chair, now breathless with a peaceful expression, seems to have just slipped into a deep sleep. Those who are willing to part with their wealth meet a painless end at Vex's hands.
Vex believes in being nice to her fellow ratfolk. After all, why make things hard for each other if there's no conflict of interest?
In this grim and cruel world, everyone seeks ease, even in death.

"This is your payment for the job." Whisk hands over a heavy bag of gold coins, glancing up at her, "You must have made quite the fortune, huh?"
Vex flashes her signature nonchalant smile. "Indeed, it was a prime target. Make sure you keep these coming... Mom."
Whisk's response is as flat as ever, showing no emotion.

By traditional ratfolk standards, their mother-daughter bond is surprisingly thin, but Vex doesn't care.
She never knew her father, nor did she experience the familial belonging other ratfolk spoke of. Whisk is always silent, and her involvement in her daughter's life extends only to recruiting her into the Three Ears assassination squad.
Vex knows that Whisk is pursuing true freedom, though she doesn't approve of it.
To Vex, only money can buy freedom; without it, life is a mire wherever you live — her childhood has taught her that.
As for what to do after amassing wealth, Vex hasn't thought that far, but she imagines she'd be happy no matter what she does... though it's only a vague thought.

story.text:
Lyle slams the table forcefully and walks out of the tavern.
The buzzing atmosphere has simmered down, but this ridge halfling couldn't care less. "Since those shabby folks are jawing about reform again, I ain't sticking around."
Irritated, he paces about, making two laps of the village before heading to the fields, reluctant to heed watching eyes.

Lyle knows his temper is bad.
It was like this before. Ever more of his ridge halfling compatriots at Eulestein fell in with the Reformers. Since then, his outbursts have only worsened, more so recently.
Lyle's precious few friends used to come chat with him and discuss matters, but now, they are all drifting away.
He knows exactly who's responsible, of course he does!

Like his brother Corrin, Lyle despises Errich.
Deep down, he can’t deny that hafling’s magnetism — how effortlessly he draws others to his cause. Yet that very charm only deepens Lyle’s revulsion when their ideals collide.
Powerless to sway his friends, Lyle takes to haunting the tavern daily, eavesdropping on the patrons’ murmurs, ever wary lest these outsiders brew some fresh calamity.

story.text:
The Iskalland night is one of chilled silence. The afterglow of the fire and the lingering inebriation sink the dwarves into a tranquil slumber. Besides a handful of night watchmen, not another living soul ought to be out roaming.
If all of this fails to deter a brazen soul from venturing beyond the safety of the village, they will likely stumble upon a presence amidst the snow: On the surface, she looks to be a dwarf. Yet, in the chill of the frigid night, her breath creates no white haze.
Remember well to keep away from her, for she is an underling of the ice dragon, a scourge attempting to infiltrate us. Long pronounced dead, she has returned in the guise of the living.

For as long as anyone could remember, Gerthin had been a frail child. Nobody expected her to see a long life. Her quiet, withdrawn disposition paired perfectly with her frail constitution. While her peers were playing, she spent much of her time in the role of silent spectator.
Only the beaming light that was the chief's daughter, Beldelle, would come and hold Gerthin's hand, making her a part of their games for which there was no physical demand.
Nevertheless, tragedy so oft befalls the luckless. An underhanded snipe claimed Gerthin. Her parents were killed in the fight. Gerthin's body was never recovered, and thus the people laid her scattered clothes in a grave.
Not a soul could have predicted that decades later, she would return.

The illness was a gnawing torment, longer-lasting than Iskalland’s bitterest gales. It clung to her like a specter, its damp, frozen claws forever gripping her shoulders.
"Gerthin, what sin did you bear? Why must you suffer so? You linger closer to death than life."
"Then cast off your warmth. Surrender to the cold."
And when the ice dragon’s gift came, Gerthin smiled.
A monster now — what of it? In death’s embrace, she found rebirth.
Yet... Amidst her clansmen’s scorn, their venomous glares branding her apostate — why, Beldelle, does your gaze alone brim with grief? With quiet doubt...
Do you pity me still? As you did when we were young — will you reach for me again?

story.text:
"Hey, Nadja, where are you going?" barked the senior warrior monk sternly. "You're supposed to stay here. The Honorable Abbot will be inspecting the ritual grounds tonight!" 
Nadja hoisted her pike and responded with a hint of confusion, "I was only assigned to be on guard duty here this afternoon, and I ought to be leaving once I'm done. I don't see how this is related to the Honorable Abbot." 
She left nonchalantly as the senior warrior monk thundered with rage, ready to finish her duties for the day — just as she had done many times before.

Nadja stood as a paragon among warrior monks — her prayers precise, her asceticism flawless, her combat artistry beyond reproach. None dared question her mastery, not after she claimed victory in the Grand Monastic Tournament. Yet the former abbot had scorned her triumph, branding her "lazy" for refusing needless labor, "impious" for measuring devotion by deeds rather than drudgery. They stripped her honors — until Halramar, the new abbot, restored them.
"What sin stains your soul, child?" The dark-furred patriarch’s smile held the warmth of hearthfire. "To give neither more nor less than asked — this isn’t sloth, but sagacity. This outpost wastes your light. Walk with me instead."

Upon earning Halramar's trust, Nadja's world transformed — yet her methods remained steadfast as mountain stone.
She deemed him the ideal commander: his orders rang with clarity, his expectations stood unambiguous, and never did he waste her time with empty praise once the deed was done.
Such harmony, she dreamed, might endure eternally. But as she accepted yet another abduction assignment — this time with only a shadow of her former conviction — the unwelcome truth crystallized: A flawless superior does not a true leader make.

story.text:
Volthug neither loved nor loathed the Serenity Forest.
To an orc whelped upon frozen steppes, its clinging mists and fecund warmth would never cradle like home. Yet habit had carved its paths — here to hunt, here to shelter, here to let moss swallow his footprints.
Only after leaving the Bloodfang clan did he understand: survival’s true shape is change itself.

Most Bloodfang orcs admired Grishnaar, but Volthug was not counted among them.
He disliked Grishnaar's approach, and didn't believe that sacrificing orc honor and his own people in return for power would truly lead the tribe to prosperity.
Expanding too hastily often spelt a swifter demise. Unfortunately, too many tribesfolk have lost sight of that.

Not all orcs had succumbed to madness. A remnant of clear-minded tribesmen chose to follow Volthug’s exodus from the Old Highlands.
To remain meant certain ruin — Chief Grishnaar would surely hunt down these wayward souls. So they journeyed beyond familiar crags, beyond frosted plains, until the Serenity Forest swallowed their trail.
True, the halflings’ ceaseless chatter grated like rusted steel. But Volthug bided his time. This forest was but a waystation; his true path through the wilderness still awaited.

story.text:
Manda waved the wand in her hand. The energy it emitted brought the magic puppet on the table to life, and it started to wobble. 
The gnome casually tied back her disheveled hair, a result of her immersion in experiments, into pigtail buns, then hurriedly tucked her new creation into her arms and rushed out of the room. 
President Donella had been back from seclusion for a few days and was probably in her office, so Manda planned to show her some new work as soon as possible.

Manda once left Anchorite Spiral, but returned a decade later. 
During her travels, she acquired new techniques which she then shared with her fellow gnomes. Most of these techniques come from the gnomes of different regions of Adenthia,  or individuals from other races who are interested in crystal magic techniques. 
This quickly made Manda a celebrity in Anchorite Spiral, but she soon chose to withdraw from the limelight to focus on her new creations.

Manda had once grown weary of Anchorite Spiral, which was the main reason she got on a boat and left. 
Though her skills and magic puppets brought respect and fortune abroad, Manda soon grew tired. Merchants only valued profit, ignoring the techniques behind her art. 
In the end, she returned home, to the familiar Anchorite Spiral. The atmosphere here is simpler, suitable for a wanderer longing for a purely academic ocean.

story.text:
Taking off her goggles, Eirnin was about to place them on the workbench when another pair of hands immediately snatched them away.
"Your goggles are too old. Not only are they lacking in protective qualities, but also in many new features." Holding the goggles in both hands, Orfenna inspected it from all sides, then shook her head in disdain. "I've got some abandoned experimental products here, and even those are way more useful than this pair. How about swapping this out for you?"
Eirnin shook her head firmly. "No, Stoutbeard hasn't issued any orders to upgrade any equipment. A repair will suffice."
Everyone knew that mentioning Stoutbeard in such capacities would instantly push Orfenna's temper to a boiling point, even if it came from her only friend and closest childhood companion.
"It's always Stoutbeard this, and Stoutbeard that! If he told you to jump off the airship with no flight wings, would you do it too?"
"Stoutbeard would never suggest something so unreasonable."
This statement was like throwing an open flame onto high-proof alcohol.
"Take these goggles and scram! You're nothing but Stoutbeard's lapdog!"

Eirnin stared at the goggles in her hand and inhaled deeply. As an elite warrior and the captain of the strike squad, it was rare to see her looking so dejected. 
She did not want to be inconsiderate, but even more than that, she did not want to see both her closest friend and the person she admired — also the two most formidable people of the airship crew — to go their separate ways just like that. 
There were so many good-for-nothings on this fleet — even the majority of the strike squad she led were wastrels who indulged in bragging, drinking, and gambling — yet Stoutbeard had led their entire fleet to grow and expand. What strong conviction! What excellent leadership! Why did Orfenna have to oppose him? 
If her good friend and her leader could work as one, the future of the airship crew would be ever so bright! 
Every time she thought about this, Eirnin could not help but sigh deeply.

On the matter of Stoutbeard, Eirnin and Orfenna had exhausted every avenue of discourse — from measured deliberations to tempestuous quarrels — yet resolution remained elusive.
Eirnin could never fathom the wellspring of her friend's obstinacy.
She conceded Orfenna's point about the surface dwarves' musty traditions — those antiquated edicts riddled with absurdities. But Stoutbeard's codices? Those were another matter entirely.
The voluminous Sky Code represented generations of practical wisdom, its weight born of careful precedent. When Stoutbeard invoked personal judgment, it was only when circumstances demanded flexibility amidst complexity. How had Orfenna reduced this living tradition to mere blind adherence?
Eirnin's arguments had run their course. Yet she clung to faith — someday, Stoutbeard's wisdom would sway her friend's heart.
This truth she held unshaken.

story.text:
Hirvolm climbed the stairs of the tower and rapped lightly on the door.
No reply came, but the door opened nonetheless. The Archpriestess of the Crescent Order and the owner of the tower, Mithrasea, sat quietly by the window, immersed in the stillness of the darkened room.
As her bodyguard, Hirvolm has already been accustomed to this way of life. He walked over and stood by her side, awaiting her orders, awaiting the silence.

Sound has always been a fuzzy and distant thing in Hirvolm's world. 
His hearing has been impaired since birth, possibly due to an affliction from beyond the Material Plane. Although most elves believe that he is unfit to guard the tower, Mithrasea shares no such qualms. 
Since the Archpriestess is blind in both eyes, in the company of his deafness, their interactions have always been silent.

Hirvolm has always tried to steer clear of the sea. 
Though he lives on an island, he is unwilling to go near the coast. Mithrasea is the only one he confided this to. 
Whenever he comes close to the misty waters, he will hear eerie calls — as if coming from a distant place — in his deaf ears. 
Mithrasea advised him to keep this a secret, promising him she'd handle it. Hirvolm obeyed her advice, concealing his secret to this day.

story.text:
Zraacs grinned darkly, counting the seconds in his head.
The so-called merchant had just closed a deal — both parties pleased. But beyond the trinkets sold, the goblin had slipped in a little bonus: his latest untested invention, a volatile new explosive. "Just a slight jostle, and —
BOOM!
"— poof," the goblin mused.

Zraacs the goblin never stays in one place for long, constantly wandering Adenthia.
An accomplished con artist masquerading as a merchant, Zraacs enjoys a great many hobbies. He's always able to cobble together weird and wonderful things and then sell them off in all sorts of ways.
Zraacs isn't fond of the meticulous artisans in their workshops. His creations are almost entirely improvised at random. But hey, they all work! So why bother with the unnecessary prettiness?

Even among charlatans, Zraacs occupies a special circle of infamy.
The goblin's inventive genius is born of avarice, sharpened by cunning, and tempered with an insatiable curiosity. He tinkers and toys with the world, leaving behind trails of chaos — always at others' expense, never his own.
Zraacs walks his path alone, trusting nothing but his wits and the next spark of inspiration. And with his compulsive collector's soul driving him ever onward, this wandering tale is nowhere near its ending.

story.text:
Bleddyn’s gaze rests heavy on the suspended cauldron, its iron belly swallowing firelight.
His fingers tighten around the spice pouch — Lumina’s bounty, hauled across frozen wastes by merchants braving the Northern Tundra’s indifference.
Such treasures came rarely here, where ice throttled trade routes and profit withered on the vine.
Now the ranger stands at life’s perennial crossroads: gamble these last precious grains upon untested flavors, or sup forever on mediocrity’s thin broth.

He has long been away from his native land, its warmth fading from memory.
Bleddyn was born in a small town within the Dragonsaerie Empire. His family was neither well off nor badly off, with enough to eat, but no leeway for hedonistic pleasures.
He had no desire to be a miner or a farmer, but he was reasonably fit and able. He aspired to see distant lands, like the ones bards crooned about — to be an adventurer!
Bleddyn never imagined for a moment that he would never return.

In his homeland’s warmth, young Bleddyn seldom touched strong drink.
Northern spirits cared little for subtlety — their fire was meant to thaw frozen bones, not please refined palates.
Yet after settling in the tundra, forging bonds with dwarven kin, he came to cherish their liquor’s rough embrace.
Now he drinks deep, laughs loud, weaves his beard into dwarven knots. And when the ale’s warmth blooms in his chest, he tumbles backward — a snowflake returning at last to icy earth.

story.text:
She listened to the wind.
The piercing gale sweeping down from the mountain's summit grew silent, until only Rowena and the mountain remained in the snow.
Aloof and wordless, she always preferred to leave her clan's settlement, seeking solitude on some rarely trodden peak where she would sit gazing into the distance.
Beyond, hidden behind the mountains, there seemed to lie another realm of noise and bustle.

Later, Rowena moved away from her clan.
It hadn't been easy. She wasn't banished, she merely grew to resent the silence.
The mountains of her homeland, once offering their comfort, were now too burdensome and oppressive. Perhaps that merchant caravan's visit had sparked her curiosity about the wider world?
Rowena still adored the stillness of the mountains, but just for now, it was time to leave.

The adventures are always undertaken alone, but Rowena loves this life.
If she wanted to avoid convoluted trade routes and throngs of people, she'd occasionally draw on her past experience and choose somewhere nobody had ever set foot.
Rowena considered having the choice between the hustle and bustle of the crowds and the seclusion of the mountains a bonus.
Even from her narrow bed in the inn, she could still hear that sound. The wind, far, far away.

story.text:
The flickering lamplight cast a trembling, indistinct shape upon the earth.
Nathaniel walked alone through the wasteland, the lamp swinging in his grip.
He had carried this light across countless lands. Sometimes, those who saw him would startle and flee, believing him to bear some ill portent.
Yet Nathaniel never truly noticed them. His eyes remained fixed on the wavering flame, where, between the dance of light and shadow, secrets whispered their tales.

Nathaniel called himself a Nightwalker — though none truly grasped the meaning coiled within that title.
Before he ventured into those ruins, he had been but another mage among many. Now everything was different.
Through the lamp's glow, Nathaniel had glimpsed truth and secret both — and secrets, by their nature, defy telling.
He alone could perceive what lay hidden this way. Just as some are born reading the land's tongue in trembling leaves, so too had the oldest mysteries long since withdrawn from common sight.

Nathaniel walked by night, resting only fitfully in daylight.
The ignorant are blessed — they know nothing of night's terrors. But Nathaniel had lost that blessing. Now he felt bound to watch over those who slept unaware through the darkness.
So he listened. Without pause, he attended to the murmurs of the dark as they slipped through the lamp's flickering light — its sole witness. Should he ever falter, those unspeakable whispers might spill into the waking world.

story.text:
Rava coughed and swept a cold glance at the bedridden patient who was groaning incessantly. 
"Shut up. You're disturbing my concentration with that moaning," said the witch doctor arrogantly, though her hands never stopped healing. However, this only made the patient's pain worsen. 
"Careful," she warned, "If I make a mistake... you're not going to like the result."

She no longer practiced healing within a specific tribe, but instead wandered the plains. 
Rava had been banished from her tribe because she didn't agree with Grishnaar's behavior. 
Ultimately, Grishnaar's reliance on powers external to the tribe was clearly a poisoned chalice that would only be detrimental in the long run, but it was a shame that the orcs around her couldn't see its evils, and just went along with him blindly. 
However, Rava had no interest in explaining her views. Those damned fools were beyond saving — but if they were happy with their decision, then so be it.

Rava never had much patience to begin with. 
Though orcs were inherently an impatient species, and she had tried her best to restrain herself due to her profession as a witchdoctor, Rava still sometimes encountered patients who pushed her to her limits. 
If they had no intentions of valuing the fruits of her labor, and instead kept up with their self-destructive attitudes, then they might as well just commit suicide! 
Having a brain was a fundamental requirement for survival, but her capacity as a witchdoctor didn't allow her to sew a usable brain into their skulls. 
What a pity.

story.text:
Brody put down his telescope and spat into the sea. 
The fog was too damn thick, and the pirates slumped onto the barrels, growing restless as they were unable to see anything. "Alright, no need to rush. We'll anchor here for a few days before we continue sailing." 
Being trapped for three days in the waters near the archipelago was driving up tensions amongst the pirates. Thankfully, Brody was able to keep them in line, but nobody knew how long this fragile peace was going to last.

The ship set sail from Ghost Headland.
On the night before departure, Brody had been dragged into a drinking bout by Karf. The young captain painted visions of riches hidden deep in the isles, urging Brody to return laden with treasure.
Though parting from the Banshee left a pang of melancholy, the pirate departed with a handful of crewmates.
Whether he'd return wealthy mattered little — like most who gathered under Karf's flag, Brody sailed for freedom's sake alone.

Brody's joining the Banshee was purely accidental.
Two pirate ships met head-on in the Somna Sea. After wave upon wave of cannon fire, Karf emerged victorious.
Brody was just an innocent man seized by that defeated ship, and while Karf promised to release him, Brody instead chose to forego it.
He had already lost all his wealth and had nothing. Even if he returned to Dragonsaerie, all that awaited him was poverty and destitution. With that in mind, why go free?

story.text:
Naguk swung his ax, the heavy weapon resembling a mere lightweight toy in the orc's hands. 
He had just finished an exhilarating sport where he chopped off the heads of a whole bunch of enemies. 
Naguk had thought that they were going to flee from the west! But to his surprise, the lot of them actually tried to break out using the night as a cover. Luckily, their chief had the foresight to predict this, so Naguk was able to successfully contain them.

Naguk had always performed his job well — at least that's what Grishnaar said, so he believed it wholeheartedly. 
Compared to the previous dimwitted tribe chiefs he had served, Naguk was convinced that Grishnaar was the most intelligent and strongest of them all! 
Ever since Naguk had come under the command of the chief, not only did he never have to worry about going hungry, but he also got to torture so many stupid losers ever so frequently. In Naguk's heart, there couldn't be a happier and more satisfying thing in the world than this.

Naguk hated overthinking. Priest Dubok, for instance — that one thought too much, even daring to second-guess the chief's orders. What pointless fretting.
If Grishnaar always judged right, why not simply obey? Men like that priest sickened him.
But such musings vanished as quickly as they came, drowned out by fresher, sweeter notions — new ways to make his prey scream.

story.text:
Thia's whip carved a vicious circle through the air before cracking against the prisoner's back.
The prison officer shook her head in disgust. A sharp kick silenced the man's wails, and she slumped into her chair, arms crossed over her chest.
Pathetic. Even after all that, he'd yielded so little.
With a sharp gesture, she summoned a subordinate. "Drag this wretch away," she snapped. "And bring me his cellmate. Now."

She thrived wherever she went, as naturally as a fish in water.
In a place like the Unyielding Silk, morality was nothing but dead weight — a burden Thia had never carried. Instead, she wielded selfishness and greed like well-honed blades.
Excessively sadistic and brutally efficient, this deep elf’s cruelty knew few bounds.
Yet in a prison teeming with strife and struggle as a guard, such mercilessness made her the perfect warden.

There's one fundamental to getting rich... keeping your nose out of some specific business.
Thia's no stranger to it, and is well aware this is the cause of disorder and chaos in her own town, Terminus.
To say she cares about nothing would be unfair. Where the Queen of the Unyielding Silk is concerned, Thia maintains a great sense of loyalty.
Besides, sweeping away the muck in the city's nooks and crannies is just another duty of hers to the Queen.

story.text:
Catherine gazed long at the painting on her wall.
Her bedchamber lacked the delicate adornments ladies favored — this painting dominated nearly the entire wall instead.
There, a knight raised his sword high, roaring as he battled a troll. Behind him marched an allied force of humans and wood elves. The breaking dawn's first light caught his blade's tip, shining like divine grace.
Once more — for the thousandth time — Catherine vowed in her heart: Eurion, glorious ancestor, I shall carry on your legacy.

Duchess Treowbaum never concealed her lust for power.
The Duchess administered Arbortea for far longer than the romantically inclined Duke Treowbaum. She frequented councils and military assemblies, issuing commands. In truth, many of her orders were insolent and devoid of practicality, but as the Duke's absences mounted, Arbortea's authority was quietly shifting.
Some scandalous rumors about the Duchess circulated among the masses, but such baseless gossip made fewer waves than her unapologetically philandering husband.

Catherine loathed the title "Duchess of Treowbaum." She preferred to be addressed as "Eurion’s Heir" — a name that evoked the legendary ruler who had led the human-wood elf alliance to victory in the miraculous Strike of Dawn, driving back the troll hordes.
Her husband was a contemptible weakling, bartering power for petty indulgences. She would never stoop to such folly.
Twenty years had passed since her days as Arbortea’s fairest noble flower. Now, after climbing the political spire, only one figure remained above her.
Just one more to crush beneath her bootheel, and the summit would be hers.

story.text:
Even the mighty Dragonsaerie Empire cannot escape the blight of its slums — a place where survival depends on one's wits. Those with the right talents may still carve out comfortable lives.
Horace is such a man.
Not all who flounder in the gutters are mere strays. Here and there lurks a wolf who chose the collar — and Horace, too old now for reckless adventuring, has settled contentedly into tavern life. The occasional shady job keeps him in ale and stew, and he finds this existence agreeable enough.

Horace likes to say, "All fear stems from a lack of firepower."
According to his drunken bragging, the impressive and dramatic barrel in his hand had been the main cannon of some pirate ship.
Those were his glory days: commanding a ship full of pirates and plundering the seas. Unfortunately, his unchecked pillaging infringed on the interests of other large pirate gangs, and he was driven back to land and became downtrodden, with only his old buddy, the cannon, left to keep him company.
And his old buddy is really useful too. More than once the cannon has helped him scare off his opponents before the fight even starts, leaving him with risk-free loot.

The slums are a true mire — once you're in, sinking is inevitable.
Horace knows this better than most. But the fight's long since left him.
He's no spring chicken. Maybe there was a wife once, maybe kids... No one knows, and he's not telling. After all the faces he's seen, all the deeds done, all he wants now is a safe corner and the occasional harmless job.
At least there's decent liquor to dull the edges. The world's rotten enough — might as well take what joy you can while you're still breathing.
Yet when scrawny kids stretch out their hands by the roadside, he still digs for coins. Useless gesture or not.
