story.text:
The spectral azure flame seared Sifris's flesh, consuming it, burning even more brightly.
The surrounding silence was her only companion. The devout priestess stood wordless and unmoving on the altar, waiting for that voice.
She offered part of her body as an offering, appealing to that most ancient of deities. It wasn't all that long ago that she planted the seeds of her faith well in mind of the kingdom's heir. Doing so fulfilled the task entrusted to her by the Dragon Queen herself.
She hoped this pleased her deity.

Her world had always been submerged in a nebulous darkness.
Being born blind, the light was never hers to see from the very start. Yet, she felt no sense of loss.
She was born to preach the faith of the Dragon Queen. She believes herself lucky, especially compared to those insignificant worms, squirming around, losing themselves. When you're born with your own light, you need not waste your life in pursuit of it.

Sifris is an enforcer of the Dragon Queen's will, unconditionally upholding everything concerning the Dragon Queen.
She is well aware that successfully carrying out her duty requires more than simple devotion, but also appropriate means.
Whilst the burden of responsibility weighs heavily upon her, never does she tire. It is all the Dragon Queen's test.

story.text:
Tonalnan's golden eyes scanned the circle of lizardfolk that stood in the circle around her. 
It was unfortunate, she thought to herself, that no one understood the metaphor she had thrown out. 
Even amidst the Queen and Shaman's verbal sparring, the quality of discourse in the tumultuous atmosphere of the hall disappointed her.

As one of the Queen's closest confidants, Tonalnan has never doubted her own abilities and talents. 
Her martial skills, her intelligence, and even her sparkling, brilliant red scales all indicate that Tonalnan is anything but an ordinary lizardfolk, and she believes that her bloodline holds a greater power. 
Tonalnan is not entirely opposed to the other races, but rather evaluates them according to their worth. If those races can demonstrate their value, then there isn't any harm in interacting with them.

Tonalnan is not an easygoing lizardfolk. 
Her arrogance is evident in her every gesture, and so is her indifference. Even worse, Tonalnan has an atypical perception of emotions, and cannot accurately distinguish underlying meanings and metaphors in language — even though she thinks she does. 
This has sometimes led to disastrous social consequences, but they are always quietly handled by the Queen.

story.text:
Horrus laughs as he slams his beer stein onto the wooden table with a thud.
He has always held his drink well, but tonight he's gone overboard — embellishing his oft-repeated tales of heroism with fresh exaggerations. The regulars exchange knowing glances but applaud politely nonetheless.
After all, Horrus is buying every drink in the tavern tonight.

Most warriors are paid to do their jobs, their wage relative to their efforts. But Horrus is an anomaly of sorts.
Oftentimes, his work depends on the mood, and chatting with employers. Horrus can end up expending a great deal more energy on the job than he has been paid to.
If the employer is inclined to lavish a little extra praise on him over the campfire, then Horrus will redouble his efforts and provide a service that is second-to-none.

Dwarves enjoy telling tales of their exploits with those around them.
While his speech isn't eloquent and the rhythm of his narration lacks finesse, Horrus nevertheless relishes in recounting those memories long past. He has always been a fierce, stalwart warrior. Now though, life is much more peaceful and humdrum than in the old days. Only in the throes of storytelling does he feel like he's returned to those intense, perilous battlefields.
Once he is too drunk, the listeners around him gradually take their leave. But Horrus? He just talks and talks.

story.text:
The guards' footsteps faded at last. Gumm rose from his snowdrift refuge.
His forest-weight garb proved pitiful against the Snowladen Mount — shivers racked his body as he forced stiff limbs down the hidden trail.
Gumm knew the peril. Even as kin-blood, trespassing in Mog-Nach troll territory would only earn a blade's greeting.
Yet faith demanded this pilgrimage. Through grinding cold, he mouthed the sacred invocations...
Then sunset gilded Greeahg Goor's spires.
He fell to his knees. "Ancestor Spirits above." The whisper carried all his devotion, all the triumph swelling his chest.
"Ancestor Spirits above."

Faith in the Ancestor Spirits is a tradition of the Mog-Nach trolls, but Gumm's fervor exceeds that of any typical follower. He had the totem of Ancestor Spirits tattooed on his forehead, and passes his free time gazing out across Snowladen Mountain, quietly chanting verses of prayer.
Thus, when the Mag-Noch Chief, Trolgar, chose to defile the purity of faith by consorting with the outland Unstill, the once-loyal minion Gumm opted to vacate Snowladen Mount, making for the forest.
Yet, his gaze lingered still upon Snowladen Mount, upon Greeahg Goor where the trolls conducted their daily offerings, and the Lake Chastity of legend said to be inhabited by the Ancestor Spirits.

Gumm received a divine revelation on the shore of Lake Chastity.
He was born unable to speak, and was mocked by his peers in childhood. That day, the still tender boy accidentally fell into the lake. Not able to cry for help, he struggled to keep his head above water, sinking downward.
As he thrashed moments from drowning, the whispers of the Ancestor Spirits echoed through his water-clogged ears.
The trolls found the unconscious Gumm at the shore of the lake. Three days later, he awoke with a voice and the power of spell manipulation.
Thus, Gumm dedicated the remainder of his life to Mog-Nach. He tattooed the Ancestor Spirits' totem on his forehead as a reminder to himself and to others: Gumm's life belongs to the Ancestor Spirits. Devotion is all that he strives for.

story.text:
Alfie hums a tune while stirring the thick, bubbling porridge. The sweet aroma of freshly diced apples lifts his spirits.
If only he could ignore the battle outside his window.
With a swift motion, he swings his staff to deflect a stone projectile aimed at his pot. "Bloody goblins," he mutters, hoping his companions will quickly resolve this nuisance before the meal spoils.
Then it dawns on him — after this fight, he probably shouldn't use the warrior's axe for chopping apples anymore. Who knows how much foul goblin blood will coat that blade...

Alfie is "low-stakes" personified. Well, that is to say, no different than the average halfling.
He is passionate about farming, loves to reap the fruits of his labors and whip them into gourmet meals, and then gobble it down with hot tea, motivating him to carry on with his farming.
Of all goodies he cooks up, apple pie is his absolute favorite. His most prized possession is the ancestral apple tree in his backyard.
Incidentally, it was while defending this apple tree from goblin vandalism that the staff in Alfie's hand revealed its true power.

Alfie knows all too well: to live peacefully, one must be ready to face danger.
His optimism never blinds him to threats — whether vermin in his fields or crises in the wider world.
Armed with both skill and compassion, he defends himself readily and aids others willingly.
Sharing hot tea and warm apple pie with kind souls delights him — if they’re patient enough to wait through his apple-picking and the leisurely baking of his famously slow-made pie.

story.text:
Alvis recited his prayers softly. 
His voice was melodious, articulating the complex syllables of the words beautifully but also naturally and intimately, like the babbling of a brook. 
The young elves in the Academy listened intently to the cleric's prayer, and asked him more questions when it was over.

All elves acquainted with Cleric Alvis recognize his passion for art and literature — and his exacting standards in these pursuits.
Yet scarcely any realize that numerous poems ascribed to him were in fact penned by ghostwriters.
With meticulous care, Alvis would polish and alter these texts, erasing all traces of their true origin. The praise and renown they garnered filled him with profound satisfaction.

The cleric despises anything that stands in his way of his ascension to power. 
Similar to Thelendor, Alvis holds a disdain for the uncivilized races beyond the islands. But unlike the lord of the Increscenta, the cleric also harbors malicious intentions and exploits and suppresses his own kinfolk through various means. 
He is greedy, but will never admit to his greed; he is despicable, but has never been caught in the act. Apart from Alvis' own inner fears, he appears to be an irreproachable individual.

story.text:
Shagrol smells blood.
The chill autumn gales rage across this barren land. The orc warrior, with his scoundrels in tow, has just concluded a lethal assault and is now mopping up the lingering survivors.
Shagrol pauses a moment as the wind blows, before speaking words soaked in cruelty, "Listen! Two halflings are hiding."

Although enjoying violence as much as his fellow orcs, Shagrol is not governed by such impulse.
He remembers every creature who fell to him and the strengths and weaknesses of every enemy he fought. These experiences hang like medals on the walls of his mind.
Rather than plunging into frenzy, he remains calm in the midst of intense combat, always observing the enemy for weaknesses.

Long before swearing allegiance to Grishnaar, Shagrol had gone years without tasting defeat. Countless foes underestimated him — each paid with their lives.
Grishnaar proved different. Though the young orc bristled with equal arrogance, his never clouded his tactical sight.
So Shagrol bent the knee. Not for power, but for the promise of battle's ecstasy — this alliance would let him savor combat's sweetest fruits.

story.text:
Vani's father once told her that the most essential thing in any home was the tableware. A table laid with many clean and neat tableware was a sign that a family cared for one another, lived in harmony, and had a prospering lineage. 
"As halflings, our strength and intelligence may not compare to that of other races. However, we are a hardworking and united race, both to our tribe and within our homes," proclaimed the generous owner of Bigfoot Orchard — the wealthiest halfling in the village — with pride. 
Thus, as the youngest daughter, Vani has dutifully cleaned the family's dinnerware since childhood.

After her mother passed away, Vani put away the beautiful set of antique dwarven silver cutlery and carefully placed it in a storage cabinet.
Her father fell ill shortly afterward and was absent from the dining table from time to time. Vani removed his dinnerware as well and put it in his bedroom where he spent most of his days.
Myron began to take over their father's business. He was frequently away from home, and as a result, his walnut dinnerware was tucked away, too.
Often times, there were only Vani and Downey left to dine at the table.
"Hey, sis, why don't you get me some money?" Downey kept bringing up his gambling addiction at the table. "Just one last time, and I'll win big! You don't need to worry about Dad. He doesn't know anything about this."
Finally, one day, Vani's patience had reached its limit. She raised her staff and threw Downey out of the door along with his cutlery.

When they decided to banish Downey, the eldest son of the family, Vani took out all the tableware in the house and polished them one by one. Among them was Downey's tableware, which had been acquired from a pawnshop. 
"Vani, a proper family cannot only maintain the outward appearance of stability, but must also rid themselves of internal pests. Only then can the trees bear good fruit," said Myron, who came over to help her. "Remember, you're not just a caretaker of fruit trees; you will be a fruit tree yourself in the future, and you have the right to defend a proper home." 
Thus, when everything was over, Vani transplanted a new fruit tree beside the mill and pastry shop she inherited.

story.text:
Vidimir, Scholar of The Vale, slides a heavily weathered tome, pages barely intact, back onto the shelf before reclining back into his chair.
The old man rubs his temples, his excitement tempered by a hint of fatigue setting in. He has just concluded a debate. While attending these gatherings of scholars and wizards is a chance to acquire new knowledge and trade arguments together, encountering foolishness is still tiresome.
Fortunately, this small, secluded room in the library is pleasantly quiet. Vidimir closes his eyes, and slips into a nap.

The mercenary peers around cautiously, speaking to Vidimir in hushed tones, "Look, seems to be right there." 
After several days of traipsing through the marshy swamp, they have finally reached its depths. Rumor has it that there are the remains of some lost tribe buried here, and the client wants them to bring back all the writings and pottery fragments in the ruins.
Initially, the mercenary couldn't understand why he should bring this feeble old man along, as it would just be another headache. However, numerous near-death experiences later, he changed his tune towards the wizard.

For all his love of intellectual discourse, Vidimir is not the kind of scholar to be shut in at a desk.
Quite the contrary, he loves mingling with others. As a Grand Wizard with the knowledge to prolong one's life, he has had abundant opportunities to participate in many historical events. When the mood takes him, the Vale Scholar abruptly leaves his little room for lengthy excursions across Adenthia.
In the mind of this elderly gentleman, the line between fact and fiction is not distinct. In his experience, as often as not, they transform into one another, reinforcing each other.

story.text:
Schaltar trudged through the swirling white mists, ascending the creaking wooden walkway toward the heights.
The Vale rarely welcomed outsiders — those who came were mostly knowledge-hungry mages. But here lay the cruel truth: any wizard who couldn't reach the summit by their own power was deemed unworthy. Should they lose themselves in these mists, no rescue would come.
"You've come too late," the minotaur rumbled to the dejected outlander trailing behind. "The Great Library's doors won't open for you now. Best turn back."

Minotaurs rarely interact with the Vale's humans — yet Schaltar keeps a wizard friend.
Among those eccentric spellcasters, this one stands apart with a gentle temper. Though Schaltar often bellows in sudden rage, the mage steadfastly tolerates these stormy outbursts.
Thus Schaltar walks a different path from his kin, his heart free of their hatred for the Vale's human dwellers.

The Vale is far from an ideal home for minotaurs.
Their settlements lie shrouded in near-impenetrable darkness, where even lightning struggles to pierce the dense fog. Yet Schaltar has always been drawn to storms — those flashes of blue-white lightning slicing through the howling wind stir something primal within him, awakening an irresistible urge to roar.
Normally, he fights to suppress these violent impulses. But on nights like this, when the rain pours and thunder rolls, he allows himself to revel in them without guilt.

story.text:
Liko flicked out her tongue, startling the person across from her.
With effortless grace, she swallowed the dancing flame whole, letting it roll playfully down her throat.
The mage grinned and stuck out her tongue again — this time completely bare.
"Don’t worry! Just a little trick!" Liko’s eyes crinkled with mischief as she cradled the fire between her palms. "See? Perfectly cozy."

The firelight was warm, especially in the cold winter of the slums. Sometimes it sustained a life that should have been lost for a few more days.
Liko loved flames, loved nestling up with them, and when she was so hungry it hurt, she began trying to eat them.
This instilled fear in her parents, seeing her getting too close to something so hot.
But Liko wasn't overly concerned: She knew they were companions, not hurtful, and they gave so much more warmth than her parents ever could.

Childhood in the slums didn't last long. Afraid of her, Liko's parents sold her to a circus.
Her love of fire remained, which led her to stand upon the dirty, greasy stage and perform fire-eating stunts for the crowd.
Most failed to see anything special about it until a traveling wizard happened to pass by the circus stage and caught sight of Liko's gifts. Before long, her life drastically changed.
Liko believed it was due to the flames, granting her refuge and joy.

Excerpt from Bronagh's tattered diary: 
Monday, the first week of October. Helped Johnnie run some errands, and he gave me a bag of jerky. 
When I asked him whether the Three Ears Brotherhood was still recruiting, he said I was too young, and told me to come back the next summer. 
 Next summer? Next summer?! I might've already starved to death by then!

Excerpt from Bronagh's tattered diary: 
Monday, the third week of February. The Three Ears Brotherhood posted another recruitment notice! 
I brought my double blades with me and prepared to impress the interviewer with a demonstration of my purse-cutting. 
But she said that according to the notice, they were not recruiting cutpurses now, only big tough guys.

Excerpt from Bronagh's tattered diary: 
Monday, the second week of June. Summer is here, and I haven't starved to death yet. But the Three Ears Brotherhood hasn't started recruiting new members yet. 
Johnnie said that if I gave him a bag of gold, he'd help me pull some strings internally and find me a position. 
But I've been saving these gold coins for several years... Sigh, I'll need to think about it again.

story.text:
Once again, Ylindra ventured into the forest. Smoothing her skirt, she squatted down, parted the grass, and used a wooden jar to catch the fleeing bugs. 
What could dye fabric into a bright red color? This question had plagued her for a long time. 
Berries produced an uneven dye, while amaryllis juice would turn black over time... Ylindra had tried countless materials before discovering this crimson insect. 
They were crushed, filtered, added to water, soaked with the fabric, and steeped for thirty days before drying... Ylindra held up the dyed fabric and examined it closely in the sunlight. 
Yes, this was the color she desired. Tailoring was a profound art as well.

Hunger had ravaged Ylindra's senses. Eventually, she lost her mind and grabbed the weeds on the ground and chomped on them with abandon. 
Was this weed poisonous? Or was this a hallucination before death? She found herself back in that majestic mansion once more. 
The duke's voice seeped through the crack in the door. "Warhorses cannot speak. Pocket the rations... gold... divide them equally." 
Ylindra tried to turn and flee, but accidentally knocked over a pair of scissors on the table. 
"Who's there?! Who's outside the door?!" "It's the dressmaker who came to deliver the lady's gowns today, my lord." 
Ylindra could see the murderous intent in the duke's eyes. It was too late — only her death could bury his secret.

Justice was inconsequential before the might of power. On the third day after leaving the duke's house, Ylindra was mysteriously accused of crimes she did not commit, and sent to exile after her legs were severed. 
In a valley filled with snow white bones, Ylindra succumbed to hunger and the cold. 
Death had swallowed her pain, but it could not quench her raging hatred. 
"I'll tear you apart... skin you whole, and sew it into the ugliest garment in existence!" In the dead of the night, the now undead Ylindra floated back into the palace and raised a sharp knife above the soundly sleeping duke.

story.text:
Good-for-nothing Erren had found a new target to bully — tavern bouncer Alistair. 
Despite being a lizardfolk, he dressed like a human and spoke clumsily. All of the tavern guests treated him like a joke. 
The last time Erren and his buddies ganged up on Alistair and beat him up at a street corner, he never fought back. As he covered his head in defense, a book even slipped out from his lapel. A book! How ridiculous! 
Erren stomped on it fiercely. He didn't know what book it was, since he couldn't read anyway.

The next day, Erren noticed that Alistair's wounds had been properly treated; meticulously medicated and bandaged. 
He had heard that the lizardfolk had been stranded here as a child, and a pair of kind humans had become his foster parents and raised him, teaching him swordsmanship and how to read and write. 
Strangely, all the unhealed wounds on Erren's body began to sting, and he resolved to make Alistair lose this job, and even better, be abandoned by his family and become a pitiful drifter on the streets — 
Just like himself.

Erren led a group of his buddies and stormed into the tavern. They smashed numerous tables and chairs while Alistair's attention was elsewhere, shattering beer glass all over the floor. 
To everyone's surprise, the normally timid Alistair, who never resorted to violence and frequently took beatings without retaliation, whipped out his fleuret and repelled them easily. 
After being chased out of the establishment by Alistair, Erren then heard him apologize to the frightened guests in his usual clumsy manner. "Don't worry, I'll protect you guys." The guests huddled behind Alistair and gazed fearfully at Erren, as though they were looking at a real monster. 
Erren avoided looking at the warm lights illuminating the tavern, picked himself up, wiped the dust from the wounds on his hands, then shuffled towards the shadow of the dark alleys.

story.text:
Sabrina brushed aside the final veil of leaf litter. There, pressed into the damp earth, lay several distinct and unfamiliar tracks.
She sounded the alarm without hesitation. Moments later, the rest of the patrol sauntered over, annoyance written plain across their faces.
"What is it this time? Just footprints," one snapped impatiently. "Could've been an animal, or someone wearing fancy new boots. If you jump at every shadow, we'll never get through this darned woods."
Unperturbed, Sabrina drew the worn handbook from her coat. "Article Forty-Seven of the Forest Code states... Upon discovery of traces belonging to unidentified creatures, the entire company must be alerted..." she began, her voice steady.
"Yeah, yeah, we know! Enough with the rulebook, old fossil."

Sabrina is always meticulous in carrying out the instructions of her superiors, strictly enforcing the rules and relentlessly reporting on any slackers... All of this made her the least popular one on the patrol.
She doesn't care about other's opinions — since when does being disciplined and responsible become a downside for a person?
There have been too many tragedies in the fickle rainforest for anything other than caution to be the way to survive. Let the smart people improvise. She chooses to stick to her rules.

With her patrol complete, Sabrina trudged wearily back to the guard hut and sank onto her cot.
She slipped the Forest Code beneath her pillow and let the rhythm of her own pulse guide her into darkness.
Her diligence has earned recognition from above — and she knows exactly which post to choose: reviser of the Forest Code, where she might apply her experience to mend its flaws.
Seventy-one needs refining, she thought, eighty-two feels imprecise...
Her mind still tracing the lines of text, she descended into profound and untroubled sleep.

story.text:
Rasran scraped the gore from his helm’s eyepiece — flecks of meat and memory sprayed loose from a skull struck open.
Moments earlier, he had crushed the fool’s head with casual force, though the wretch bore no banner of their foe — just another stray caught in the fray, bearing nothing to stir an orc’s heart.
Not that it mattered. Not to Rasran, anyway.

Rasran is very passionate about fighting, because of his obsession with death. The only things he cares about in his tribe are killing his enemies and enjoying the thrill of combat. 
He lacks reason and judgment, but is surprisingly lucky in fights, which has saved him from the brink of death time and again. 
Sometimes, Rasran finds himself wondering about the sensation of his own death. Would it give him the same excitement as taking someone else's life?

Rasran seldom removed his helm.
It concealed a truth the orcish warrior refused to acknowledge: he loathed letting others glimpse his features — loathed glimpsing them himself.
When exactly had he picked up this helmet from a slain foe, and why did he strap it on?
Each attempt to remember sends throbbing pain lancing through his scarred temple, halting recollection cold.

story.text:
"What's your dream?"
Someone had once asked Cykkol. At the time, his response was simple: "I don't have such things."
But if asked again now, his answer would surely be: "My dream is to have a peaceful life."

To Cykkol, serving as a guardian of Equinoxial was the finest duty imaginable. Within the shrouded expanse of the Misty Sea, the Intertidal Clan reigned supreme; no creature dared challenge their domain.
This belief held firm — until the Abyssal Serfs, devotees of chaos, emerged from the abyss and laid Equinoxial to waste.
As one of the few remaining merfolk warriors, Cykkol found himself compelled to take charge, guiding his scattered kin toward refuge and rebuilding.

As the sun dips below the horizon, Cykkol finally has a chance to rest from his guard duty. He stretches his stiff shoulders and sighs deeply.
He must persevere regardless of the hardships.
Tomorrow, the sun will rise again, and his silhouette will once again be seen on the outpost, guarding the shelter.

story.text:
Cifla retrieved her weapon and flicked the blood off it. 
She had completed the mission for her General. As one of Quaesitia's trusted confidants, Cifla is a formidable fighter. However, she doesn't care much about that. The situation in Teneebria hasn't been stable, with everything constantly changing like flotsam in a maelstrom. 
Cifla is solely focused on improving her combat skills, rather than getting involved in political intrigue. She doesn't believe that aligning herself with any particular faction will bring her lasting power.

Being a valuable soldier — one truly fit for use — demands more than martial skill.
Cifla wields cruelty and caution in equal measure, believing mercy in a villain to be the foulest stain of all. When tasked to erase a lineage, she ensures no seed of vengeance remains. Only ashes tell no tales.
That is why she holds such disdain for Quaesitia's inexplicable leniency in sparing the prince during their recent struggle.

Hedonism is at the core of Cifla's life philosophy. 
She has never denied her strong desire for pleasure, and is willing to invest time into finding the right prey for her satisfaction. To indulge in pleasure, she would naturally need to pay a certain amount of time and price to select her target. 
Cifla has had physical relationships with many deep elves, but she doesn't hold any long-term interest in any of them.

story.text:
Grishnaar's decree stood firm: only those orcs who proved victorious in training duels would earn passage to true battle.
Driven by desperation, Aryasso clamped her arms around her hulking opponent in a vise-like grip. The brute merely chuckled, lifting her skyward as if she weighed nothing.
"This is it... I'm truly worthless," she thought, squeezing her eyes shut against the inevitable.
Then — impossible! — her foe staggered. A clumsy misstep sent the massive orc crashing backward, skull meeting earth with a hollow thud. Unconscious.
"By Grishnaar's axe, I declare Aryasso victor!" The officer's roar echoed across the training grounds. At last, the path to warriorhood lay open before her.

Aryasso understood this truth: for the tribe's triumph, sacrifices must be made.
She remembered that battle — the one that had nearly claimed her life. Human cavalry thundered toward their lines, their gleaming blades flashing cold in the sunlight. Then came the searing pain as steel bit into her neck, the warm gush of blood, her fading thought: "This is death..."
When consciousness returned — hours? days later? — she found herself in the healers' tents. Against all odds, she lived! The shaman's words stunned her: of all the front-line warriors, only she had survived.

"Spare your efforts. Strength is birthright — you'll never stand among the chosen." Such "counsel" had been poured into Aryasso's ears for years, yet still she trained.
Of all the warriors who had stood beside her in battle, most now fed the worms. Only she remained, drawing breath still amid the carnage.
This fortune she was grateful for taught her a warrior's truth: So long as you still stand, the battle's song is unsung.

story.text:
The roaring fire of the burning building flickers in Beags' little eyes.
Another victory. The goblins of the Thorns ransack this little camp, taking the opportunity to torch the place while the people camping there are out. Beags is in charge of the explosives. A look of exceptional euphoria adorns his face as he admires the flames, almost forgetting to flee the scene in time.
"Bizarre!" Beags think, "Don't they all appreciate the melodious sound of burning?"

Beags is a terrible teammate.
So fond of flame, so enthralled by it, he often makes reckless mistakes like setting fire to his fellows and the lair.
He is only tolerated for his notable research skills, since his teamwork is awful.
While those inventions aren't entirely innocuous, their affordability and immediacy still make them indispensable in goblin engineering and combat situations.

Beags has never given up on his goal.
Although the chiefs only care about the usefulness of his creations, Beags always believes his talent transcends that. He believes these combustibles and their spectacular flames will transform the world one day, and he has no doubt about it.
The dream that Beags envisions, is a beautiful world of searing red flame.

story.text:
Humans setting foot in Aethercairn for the first time naturally find Nord a welcoming presence, a much appreciated familiar sight after enduring the haughty snub of the elves.
But they will soon be disappointed: A blank-faced soldier, his voice like rusted gnome machinery, uttering monotonous rumblings that offer not an ounce of solace.
Look at that armor! It's covered in rust! Is he really alive? Another person walks away with a groan.
Nord's expression doesn't change a bit, but he mentally heaves a sigh of relief. "That's one less hassle," he thinks to himself.

Nord fits in perfectly, like a bridge, a pillar, a flagstone underfoot. Precious few know his origins: Unconscious, waves carried him to the shore, whereupon a roaming sheen elf came across him and saved his life.
With no attachment and no purpose, Nord simply remained in Aethercairn, fighting to protect the isles.
While it is hard to say how much of a role he plays in maintaining sheen elf order, at the very least, he never complains about undertaking the mundane patrols.

Nord was born of the Northland — where rivers sleep beneath ice, where men kindle fires to drink winter’s tears. They wrestle in snowdrifts and duel on frozen lakes, their breath hanging sharp in the air.
This was to be his inheritance. Until the day his ale trembled, its dancing surface whispering of distant tides. He wanted to see the sea.
So he crossed jagged peaks and wind-scoured valleys, endured the ship’s nauseous rocking, his stomach heaving with every wave. When the storm came — when the mast snapped like kindling and the fog swallowed the world — darkness took him gently.
Now he stands in silent vigil by the sea, where once-alien shores have become home. Though the northern snows still whisper to him in dreams, it's this verdant archipelago that truly claims his heart.

story.text:
Haldy raised a hand and wiped away the beads of sweat on the verge of dripping down his brow. His coarse fingers paused for a moment on the scar on his forehead, as if some phantom pain still lingered there. 
That battle had long since passed, to the point where he had forgotten a lot of its details, but he would never ever forget that bone-deep fear he had felt. 
The fear of death.

A pirate ship with black sails had approached from afar, and Haldy, who had been standing atop the mast for most of the day under the blazing sun, rallied his spirits and gave the signal to prepare for battle. 
"Prepare for a gangway battle, good lads!" Haldy hollered as he slid down the rigging onto the deck. 
For mercenaries on the open sea, the splatter and stench of bloodshed were but another day at sea. 
Haldy was very accustomed to this lifestyle, and experiencing these battles succeeded by celebrations was his way of enjoying life.

For mercenaries adrift at sea, their scars symbolized their victories in battle; after all, the opponents who had left them these scars were already dead. 
But Haldy preferred to treat the scars on his body as a notebook that served as a constant reminder of the mistakes he had made. 
The knife wound on his waist was inflicted during a drunken brawl, the whip marks on his back originated from a fierce gangway fight, and the scar on his face was incurred from his reckless actions during his youthful prime.

story.text:
Roberta yanked out the dagger lodged in her upper abdomen, her face twitching slightly in pain, yet not a single sound escaped from her lips. 
Just moments ago, the ice blade she manipulated had pierced through the skull of the Abyssal Serf, but that was not enough. She would never stop as long as she could continue to fight. 
She had grown accustomed to this strategy of trading blows, and the physical pain only fueled her rage. 
Only revenge could alleviate the agony within the depths of her soul.

"NO!" 
A nightmare startled her awake, and Roberta's hand, which had reached out into the air, fell helplessly limp. Even in her dreams, she was unable to catch her child's thin fingers. 
Severe sleep deprivation made her eyes sting unbearably, and a tear escaped from the corner of her eye, melding with the seawater without a trace. 
In that catastrophe that ravaged her distant homeland, Roberta had lost everything — her home, her partner, and her child.

Another skirmish concluded. Roberta smeared salve across the lattice of her wounds — fresh cuts over old scars — binding them with strands of torn kelp.
"You need rest." Her companions' words hung in the water, met only by the silent pendulum of her head.
Since that fateful day, only one fire burned in her veins: vengeance, thick and dark as clotting blood.

story.text:
The sacrificial offering's swollen eyelids flutter open, revealing a crimson-robed figure — a living flame. No glimpse of eyes pierces the mask's slits, only darkness staring back.
With his last defiance, the prisoner hocks blood at that impassive visage. "Do your worst," he rasps, clinging to the belief that death marks existence's cruelest threshold.
Behind the mask, exposed gums twist in a grotesque smile. Teeth part like burning curtains: "The world is an ever-living fire."
A scream tears through the chamber as the man's left arm blackens and curls. Pain unlocks his tongue faster than any blade — secrets he swore to keep spill like molten wax from a broken seal.
Satisfied, the Crimson Robe watches the dance of charring limbs, nodding approval as flames claim their final pirouette.

Countless robes whisper through these halls — gray as forgotten tombs, black as starless voids, red as freshly opened veins.
Not faces, but masks. Not individuals, but vessels.
They have slipped time’s leash to embrace truths the world dares not name. Selves dissolved into the greater will, their quietude screams rebellion against false order.
Faith is their armor, patience their blade. And their reward?
When the new dawn breaks, they shall stand first among the chosen. What the blind call suffering — what fools name cruelty — these are but Child of Chaos’ whetstone, honing souls for paradise.

The Crimson Robe has long forgotten how to breathe.
Back in the days when he still breathed, there were many who remembered and recounted his full name. His full name represented the young man's impressive exploits and the glories his father had accrued. He was burdened with the expectations of an entire kingdom, to seek out the world's innermost secrets.
Later... well, later the kingdom perished. The youth uncovered the world's innermost secrets. He espied the world's hidden injustices, glimpsed the woes beyond the plane.
Thus, he renounced his full name. He became the Crimson Robe.

story.text:
Gulal sang the ballad for the thousandth time. 
He had used a sharp stone to mark the sand beside the Hearkening Circle as a counter, until it was covered with scratches. 
He knew that some things couldn't be erased, and in this savage Bewilderness, forgetting was his greatest fear. 
At least he remembered the ballad, which he wrote with his wife by the lake in Nytheria. On that very day, they had promised to be together until the end of their lives.

No one blessed their union. What future could exist between a Mog-Nach troll and a human?
Yet to them, it meant nothing. Gulal had known since childhood that he was unlike the others, and his wife remained the only soul who ever sought to understand him.
He loved her — with every shred of his life and spirit.

The promised end of their shared life had not yet come.
To save his dying wife, he sought out those Chaos-worshiping heretics. He regretted nothing — not the bargain, not even his exile by the Dragon Queen. For her, he would sacrifice everything — this had been decided long ago on Nytheria's shores.
His sole regret was being parted from her side. Yet their tale remained unfinished — this he still fiercely believed.

story.text:
Dench shook his skull staff, chanting a stream of spells which flowed from his lips like water, which then condensed into a poisonous mist on the battlefield. 
It was a narrow victory, but a victory for them nonetheless. 
Dench believes that victory is everything — losers have no say, and anything they have to say is unimportant. Dench always stands with the victors. If the side he is on loses, he'd simply jump to the other side and change his allegiance.

In a more distant past, Dench had roamed the Hypogean District. 
It was a harsh place to live, not only due to the ruthless and unpredictable deep elves, but also the diseases and unrest that plagued the region. When his tribe was annihilated, Dench made his way to the surface world. 
For a long time, he drifted from orc tribe to orc tribe, but this was not without purpose. Dench carefully selected settlements which he deemed to have potential, and waited for the right moment to strike.

His first step was not the perfect one. 
Although he had joined the most powerful orc tribe on the Plains and quickly rose to the rank of officer, Dench sensed that the winds of change were coming: victory was temporary, and it would not favor a leader forever. It was time to act. He quickly sided with Grishnaar, who was leading a coup, and used this as a launching point to reestablish his footing. His foolish fellows had not been so lucky.

story.text:
An alert Zadie checked his surroundings, then waved his hand. 
Getting this batch of goods delivered was not going to be easy, especially in a territory patrolled by orcs, and there would likely be some casualties along the way once they reached Teneebria. 
However, this client of the Three Ears Brotherhood was offering a generous remuneration that Zadie simply couldn't resist. 
After calculating the risks, Zadie concluded that even if he lost a few comrades, his profits would still outweigh his losses!

Zadie held a lot of responsibilities. In order to thrive in the Three Ears Brotherhood, specializing in just one trade just wasn't enough. 
Though each skill was valuable in itself, the more skills a ratfolk possessed, the more money they could earn. 
Zadie not only handled the transportation of goods, but he also worked as a guard in his spare time. Sometimes, he would even help enforce discipline on behalf of his clients. 
As for the extent of that discipline — Zadie didn't care how far it went. As long as there was money involved, the clients' words were gold.

There was once a brainless individual who attempted to cheat Zadie after giving him a commission. 
Admittedly, the intelligence Zadie provided wasn't entirely accurate, but that was no excuse to cheat a diligent ratfolk! 
Hiring someone to kill another was no sweat off the Three Ears Brotherhood's back; after all, who didn't have enemies in Adenthia? "Resolving" a situation was as simple as delivering the right information at the right time.

story.text:
To this day, Mulier still couldn't quite comprehend what being an imperial knight truly entailed.
The highborn always kept the Knight Order of Platinum busy — some tasks made sense, while others left him utterly bewildered. Why bestow gifts upon Famos' townsfolk only to impose heavier taxes? Didn't it all balance out to nothing?
But with endless errands demanding his attention, the question soon faded from his mind like morning mist.

Of all the tasks the Order has in store, Mulier's favorite is going to Summerwatch.
Whether it's merely an escort mission or delivering correspondence, he is especially fond of spending time in the halfling village. With the sweet fragrance of fruit and the gentle warmth of the sun, he can hunker down in a shed or a haystack and enjoy a pleasant afternoon nap.
A break after all that work is essential. Regular rests are his secret to staying energetic!

No-one knows why Mulier chose a knight life, and he has never outwardly stated his reasoning.
But simply put, he wants to restore his masculinity — to be a man capable of action. Unfortunately, despite being a member of the Order for a long time now, he is no closer to his goal, as routine work has filled his days.
There are moments, transient and barely perceptible. When he cries out "Glory to the Empire!", that spark of desire is relit within him. Mulier loves these moments. He clenches his sword tightly, his voice resonant, loud and clear.

story.text:
To imagine what one has never seen proves arduous indeed — for the wood elf Altin, the Nytheria of old was such a vision.
He picks his way through the dense undergrowth with care, dreading any encounter with those Sylvan Furies that might force another bloody skirmish.
Herb-gathering remains perilous, yet Altin has grown accustomed to this existence.
From elder wood elves' tales, he often hears of Nytheria's bygone splendor and the Blue Oak's luminous majesty... like some half-remembered dream.

Altin was born a wood elf after the great tragedy, counted among the younger of his kind.
Though many deemed it sorrowful to have never witnessed the Blue Oak's radiance — mentioning this to him often — Altin himself harbored little regret.
What one never possessed, one could not truly mourn. Besides, to dwell in the present remained paramount: this wood elf held that safeguarding today's Athalean mattered above all else.

Immeral had wanted to cultivate the young wood elf further, but he'd refused.
Altin knew himself too well. Thinking wasn't his forte, and sometimes too much thinking gave him a headache.
He was happier settling matters by force, rather than having to deal with devious outlanders and recognizing who among them was a good sort.
Of course, Altin knew he wasn't suited to such, so he didn't want any part in big decision making: It's best left to Immeral!

story.text:
Altair counted his coins again, before slipping them into a tightly secured bag and hiding it in a secret compartment in his room. 
He had modified this small space to ensure that his years of savings wouldn't be stolen by some random nefarious thief. 
The dwarf engineer pounded his sore forearms and flopped onto his bed. It'd be best to get some sleep as soon as possible, since there was still work to do tomorrow! 
Altair drifted off into a dream, where he stood in a gentle breeze that caressed his beard.

Altair had labored on this ship for a very long time.
As an engineer, he was skilled in the maintenance and construction of flight equipment. Though he was proficient, he was not really outstanding, and thus relied on taking on increased quantities of work to gradually accumulate his savings.
Altair had a dream of one day leaving this ship and working independently. 
Though there was nothing wrong with Durem's Free Hatred, Altair had his own goals to pursue.

Altair possessed a blueprint, his own design.
It was born from decades spent crafting and repairing flying machines. This schematic distilled his life's work, a tangible bridge between reverie and reality.
It detailed a single-pilot flight apparatus, engineered for sustained, low-energy journeys through the skies.
Now, coin purse heavy with savings, he would forge it from finest materials, discarding his current rig. The Free Hatred's deck would know his footsteps no more — beyond the cloud-veil, a solitary voyage awaited.

story.text:
Arlow weighed the coin purse in his hand, then after a moment's consideration, slung the unconscious merchant over his shoulder and dumped him in a nearby cave.
The man had already been robbed once, but Arlow prided himself on his mercy — he'd even left the fool some scraps to survive on.
Leave him on the road, and he'd either be robbed blind or end up dead.
"What a bleeding saint I am," Arlow mused, whistling as he ambled down the high road toward the city's pleasures.

Over a few drinks, Arlow once claimed to have survived three days in a swamp without a single scrap of food.
Obviously, no one believed him. After all, he wasn't a known name in the business, just some third-rate mountain bandit.
To say he is truly remarkable at anything is something Arlow himself doesn't even believe without a drink in him.
But it is the truth. He excels at surviving in the most extreme of conditions. Whenever he thinks death is imminent, Arlow always scrambles away from doom on his hands and knees.

In this business, if you want to be famous, you have to be ruthless. Strength is only one aspect. There must also be a deterrent.
But Arlow has no lust for fame. He commits robberies to keep himself afloat, because he doesn't want to work, but still needs money.
If you actually get famous, there's sure to be some immeasurable benevolent sort who's going to make it his mission to see you off! 
It's best to be a no-name mountain bandit, Arlow says cautiously. He doesn't fancy himself as prey added to a certain someone's list. He only wants your money, not your life.

story.text:
Bronwyn slouched into the rocking chair, leaning sluggishly back, listening to the slow, mellow creak it made.
Oh, perhaps it's time to replace it, the halfling thought hazily to himself. But it had been in the family for many years, back when his grandmother was around...
Bronwyn yawned again as he unconsciously caressed the engraved patterns that had been worn smooth.
There's no hurry, I'll think about it after a good night's sleep.

Bronwyn lived a largely uneventful life. It became even less eventful following his daughter's marriage and restoration of his faming tools.
Life in Uerus had always been one of peace and tranquility. He had never traveled far from the Serenity Forest, nor was he keen to.
The world outside was far too complicated! Although plenty of halflings felt that venturing out into the world of business was a way forward, Bronwyn only wanted to live a quiet life.

Bronwyn had recently developed a new passion: cooking.
He hadn't thought much of it, until the day he brought soup to his daughter's newborn. Her polite but persistent hesitation spoke volumes.
The terrible truth dawned: all those years, his former family had merely pretended to enjoy his culinary creations.
But Bronwyn wasn't one to admit defeat. This year, he vowed silently, the old halfling would master the art of the kitchen — or die trying.

story.text:
Sigrid needed long years to grow accustomed to her new life.
In truth, she fared remarkably well. Though she'd come to soldiering late, her skill and diligence surpassed many career comrades.
Promotion now seemed within reach — medals already filling her palm one by one.
Yet Sigrid measured their worth differently: not in material advantage, but in the honor they proclaimed.

As a teenager, Sigrid never envisioned a future in the military for herself.
Despite coming from a military family, it was a place she found to be oppressive.
Her father only ever spoke of the Empire and of honor, never concerned with Sigrid.
Thus, she left the family and drifted into the city, something that certainly angered her father, but Sigrid only found delight in such retaliation.

Those tumultuous days drew on a long time, until Sigrid joined a merry band of friends and engaged in dealings she ought not to have done.
She struggled to forget that feeling, seeing her father's disapproving countenance amidst the raucous revelry in that place ripe with the stench of alcohol.
Before she even had chance to justify herself, her friends turned on her, throwing her in harm's way.
She survived — her father died trying to protect her. Sigrid wasn't sure if that was for her, or for the honor he spouted.

story.text:
Dain wasn't fond of chitchat.
Even during breaks, he invariably turned down invitations from other dwarves, and this day would be no different.
They probably wouldn't invite him to these time wasting affairs anymore. Dain breathed a sigh of relief as he watched the other guards leave the room in their cliques.
He intended to carry on exercising a while longer, improving his hammer wielding skills for enemy encounters.

Dain boasted a heroic physique, believing himself more capable than the guards who slacked off on exercise. He invested more heart and energy into it than they ever would.
Time was finite, and Dain elected to spend it more meaningfully.
As for all that time in taverns blowing off steam and indulging in hedonism... only inept dwarves engaged in that, and he didn't care to be associated with them.

He pursues strength relentlessly, yet struggles to find the path forward.
His body and combat skills have been honed to perfection — what more can be done? Dain desperately seeks a breakthrough, but the answer eludes him.
Still, he refuses to let frustration take hold. With no immediate solution, he persists in his training and search.
He will find it. Dain knows with absolute certainty: he shall become the clan's mightiest and most loyal guardian, eventually.

story.text:
Berrik rests the shield in his hand a short distance from his feet. As he finds a convenient spot by the tent, he sits down, shaking off the ice on his beard.
The distant ice reflects a bleak light. Staring at it can hurt the eyes. However, the dwarven guards have long grown accustomed to gazing at it day and night.
Although Berrik's duties as the clan leader's escort are often dull, he has never been lax in carrying them out.

Of his Iskalland clansfolk, Berrik is not a fellow that stands out.
He never thinks about anything too complicated, for there are people for whom it is appropriate to mind those things. He thinks only of today and tomorrow. To contemplate the day after tomorrow would invite anxiety. He enjoys perfecting his hammer and shield technique, and grooming his beard at his leisure — a matter of concern to most dwarves.

Though merely an ordinary guard stationed beside the clan leader, Berrik harbors a secret he never shares with anyone.
That is, his deep admiration for the leader's daughter, Beldelle, whom the clan affectionately calls the "Winter Sunshine." Whenever he glimpses her lush red hair cascading from beneath her circlet, a warm glow fills his chest, spurring him to work with renewed vigor.
Yet given how often he openly sings Beldelle's praises, whether this "secret" remains truly hidden is anyone's guess.

story.text:
Yagnatz swung the weapons in his claws with practiced ease, cleaving the prey into neat segments.
The crowd clustered around his stall came less for meat than for spectacle — this peculiar lizardfolk made for rare entertainment. Though outsiders weren't uncommon in this desert-edge town, reclusive lizardfolk seldom lingered.
Yet here Yagnatz remained, a full month now, showing no signs of moving on.

Fresh to the human settlement, Yagnatz often became the source of unintentional amusement.
Though many local customs still eluded him, his earnest enthusiasm and thirst for learning won over the townsfolk — who good-naturedly overlooked his frequent blunders.
"Like a big child," the tavern mistress observed with a chuckle. "A rather simple one, perhaps... but that Yagnatz means no harm!"

Yagnatz was an outlier among his kind.
From his earliest days, he'd displayed an uncommon fascination with other races. Often he would vanish from the tribe for days, shadowing passing outsiders simply to observe their ways of living.
When this peculiarity finally made him a pariah among his people, the lizardfolk made his choice — silently following a merchant caravan across the sands to this town that would become his home.

story.text:
Magic spills from the staff Enna lightly holds, softly coiling around the vines.
They spring to life at once, climbing eagerly up the pillars, unfurling leaves and bursting into bloom. The wood elf smiles faintly, tilting her head to listen to the rustling flowers, arranging them where Jathalea might glimpse their beauty.
Her time as an apprentice priestess has been brief, and throughout it all, Jathalea has guided her with care. Each day, Enna longs to grow swifter — to ease the burdens of the High Priestess she holds in such esteem.

Enna sighed heavily and sank onto a moss-strewn boulder in the forest's heart.
Reluctant as she was to admit it, she had wandered hopelessly astray — this land lay too far beyond Sythairelan's familiar paths. Unlike her Nytherian kin, whose senses never failed them, her own directionality remained stubbornly tied to childhood haunts alone.
"Nythurys guide me", she prayed silently. With a resigned internal sigh, she gave up on her own sense of direction and reached out to beg passage from the whispering greenery once more.

Occasionally, Enna dreams of that other forest.
In Nytheria, where the mists have parted, streams murmur softly, every leaf dances lightly in the wind, and flower buds shimmer with golden light. Under Nythurys' protection, all creatures live without care in this tranquil land.
Each time she wakes from such dreams, a wistful ache lingers — could these visions be some wood elf's ancient memory of the forest's lost purity?

story.text:
Sallyanne stands silently at the Duchess' side, resembling an untraceable shadow.
She speaks little, a characteristic her master is fond of. Lady Catherine is a woman of many secrets, and people with many secrets invariably favor the soft-spoken, especially those so often in tow.
Sallyanne always vanishes into Arbortea's corridors and footpaths exactly when needed, and likewise, phases into view precisely when required.

From childhood, Sallyanne had shadowed Lady Catherine's footsteps. Even in years that should have brimmed with youthful exuberance, her voice rarely rose above a whisper.
Before that, she'd been a wraith of the Arbortea markets, all sharp elbows and hollow cheeks, scavenging survival from the refuse heaps.
She knew, of course. Knew Catherine's gaze had never held equality. But what of it? The lady had granted her breath, and heartbeat, and bread. What more could she dare ask?

She knows the secrets hidden in the Lady's heart. Catherine bears no love for her husband, merely a fondness for this little kingdom of hers.
And therefore, Sallyanne isn't surprised to witness the murder. She is downright baffled as to why it has taken Catherine so long to make her move.
But, Sallyanne is equally unable to fathom the Duchess' desires... Even if one becomes ruler of it, what glory does this waning territory even hold?

story.text:
"The dragon flew over the city-state, its shadow obscuring the cathedral's divine light."
War orphans gathered around the campfire, listening to Hector tell The Dragon Slayer's Tale. As the story unfolded, the dancing flames reflected in their captivated eyes.
This was Hector's favorite story since childhood. He had countless times imagined becoming such a great warrior, defeating maddened dragons with mere flesh and blood.
When he grew up, Hector passed the knight order's rigorous selection as he had wished.

"Dragonfire engulfed the castle. Amid the ashes, a warrior stood atop the tower, spear in hand."
In the renowned Knight Order of Platinum, what they never lack is: courage and determination. Countless young dreamers of heroism were crushed by war, becoming mere fertilizer for battlefield weeds.
War is merciless, with few tales of legendary heroes single-handedly turning the tide.
After the war with the orcs ended, Hector remained long mired in grief over lost comrades and his perceived inadequacy.

"The warrior pierced the great dragon's heart! With a mournful cry, it fell... On the tower, the hero waved the banner of victory!"
In the children's eyes, Hector saw the same reverence and yearning he once had.
Alas... stories are just stories, and most people never become legendary heroes.
Hector stood up: "That's all for today, I must go on duty. Don't forget to get your bread from the tent."
As the children ran off laughing, Hector took up his sword and headed to the watchtower to continue his daily guard duty.

story.text:
Meteoric Iron, Starlight Ores, Magic Crystals, Hypogean Crystals... Forbrit remembers every single item he has hidden in his treasury. 
Since the beginning, he has been enamored by these exotic materials, perhaps due to his dwarven nature, and at some point, he became the most adept at utilizing them out of anyone on the continent. 
The armor that Forbrit crafts is universally coveted, and at the height of his success, his creations had been worn by kings, generals, and even the offspring of gods. 
For that, he should have been content.

But Forbrit was not content. 
He craved more: he coveted greater renown, better craftsmanship, and stronger materials. 
Eventually, the whole of Adenthia couldn't fulfill his desires anymore. So, when the strange skeletal creature offered him treasures from the Outlands, he accepted them without hesitation. 
That was the decision that catapulted him into the Chaos Universum.

In hindsight, Forbrit wondered if his boundless, unshakable passion had been his salvation.
He had witnessed too many exiles — broken by the endless solitude and torment — descend into madness, reduced to hollow, wandering Bewildered. But that would never be his fate. He had known it from the start.
Even the Chaos Universum teemed with mysteries, with wonders unimaginable elsewhere. Without this experience, he would never have beheld such a realm.
He would return. He would bring his revelations home. And then, perhaps, forge a new armor, one perfected by all he had learned.

story.text:
Usha, head soldier of the Dragonsaerie Empire, concludes her brief report and exits Hegio's study.
Although no significant disturbances have occurred near the capital of late, she nevertheless insists that all existing defensive and inspection measures be carried out one-by-one. Such measures seem utterly tedious in these times of tranquility.
However, contrary to the perceptions of nobility, Usha sees through the city's tranquil surface and feels the turbulence below.

If the thriving Dragonsaerie capital can be said to have many lines of defense against hostile forces, Usha will surely fight as its ultimate line of defense.
Her disposition is composed and stoic, and her temperament, like her weapon, bears a tinge of bitter chill.
Yet, as a knight and guardian of the Empire, Usha's heart doesn't bear the same frostbite. Rather, it was her mission that drove her to become the person she is now.

Usha knows well the turmoil bubbling within the Dragonsaerie Empire capital, and seldom becomes involved with the strife.
In spite of being raised by the Knight Order of Platinum, she always knew that her bloodkin, her mother, belonged to the Knight Order of Dragon Blood. These two Orders, both in service to the Empire, parted ways over a complex internal struggle.
Usha has no desire for issues of identity to compromise her allegiance or hinder her mission as a guardian. Hence, she practices deference and detachment, even though she's uncertain as to how long this delicate balance will hold.

story.text:
Uloar pressed down on Enna's wrist and shook her head.
"This is no good, Enna, you're too tense. " She addressed the wood elf priest in training, demonstrating that spell for her once more. "It must be like this... The High Priestess told you before, did you forget? "
Uloar spoke patiently, with the kind of tenderness that outlanders and traitors would never be shown.

As one of Jathalea's entourage, Uloar had been at her side for a long time.
Sometime ago, she had witnessed firsthand how the young Jathalea had fought tremendous pressure to secure a safe haven for Sythairelan, at a time Nytheria was plunged into darkness.
Back then, they weren't so very different. Jathalea was the most diligent one of a group of mentees.
Many years later, Uloar advanced from being her subordinate, to becoming her successor.

She knew she spoke curtly, but what of it?
Uloar wasn't concerned with how the outlanders viewed her, nor did she care what they thought.
Guarding Sythairelan was already a struggle. If they had followed the principles of weakness and kindness in everything, they'd have long since been overwhelmed by the encroaching forest.
Deep down, she'd never approved of Jathalea's ideas and handling methods. As for Enna... Given her willingness to be a naive wood elf, that's her choice.

story.text:
Everyone in the tribe knows that Urzog isn't very bright, but he's incredibly strong.
When the chieftain ordered fifty stones brought from the quarry for building military tents, Urzog couldn't count them, so he brought back every stone he could see.
After being scolded for bringing too many stones, Urzog silently carried the extras back to the quarry.

Urzog's slow wit caused trouble now and then, but in a tribe that valued strength above all, his brawn and simple nature made him well-liked.
When Urzog passed the warrior trials, cheers echoed across the training ground.
Urzog, confused, stared at his unconscious opponent. He lifted him up and shook him, trying to wake him.
Little did he know, the vigorous shaking only made his opponent more unconscious.

Urzog's loyalty to the tribe is absolute, always charging at the frontline to clear obstacles.
Lifting thousand-pound rocks to crush enemies, breaking shields forged from fine iron with bare hands, uprooting towering trees to use as battering rams...
No finesse, just pure brute strength!

story.text:
Heksandra still remembers her Great Library back in Scarlet Vale. 
It was her sanctuary, her kingdom, her paradise. She recalls the days she spent immersed in ancient books, undisturbed and carefree, with only an endless amount of knowledge waiting to be discovered. 
Those are the happiest days in her reminiscence.

"Your curiosity will be your undoing one day," an elder once told her. 
She had discovered a rift in the world — this was her conclusion after poring over countless tomes and ruminating deeply. Everyone believes in the perfect design of the Creator, the Dragon God, but it is clear that even gods make mistakes. Otherwise, the Child of Chaos wouldn't exist in this world. 
Unable to resist exploring that flaw, she turned her attention to Planar Magic — something that belongs to the realm of gods.

Following the failure of a bold attempt at Planar Magic, she found herself in Chaos Universum. 
She knew that she had crossed planes, and also knew that the Dragon Queen wouldn't tolerate such a transgression after the Child of Chaos' rebellion, so this had been within her expectations. 
She was more optimistic than she anticipated, and the knowledge that she had acquired over the long years taught her that this rift in the world will never disappear. History is going to repeat itself, with some greater destiny driving everything towards a particular direction. 
Thus, she believes that one day, the tides of fate will turn once more for the world, and she will be transported back to her Great Library to observe where the world will ultimately head.

Awstin follows the narrow path up the Vale to the narrow entrance in the mountain wall. 
He comes here to retrieve some goods — the new works of a wizard family on behalf of his employer. 
While most things can be transported via scrolls or magic, there are always some dangerous goods that are better handled through more conventional means, and Awstin is one of the few individuals who can easily travel in and out of the Vale. 
The ranger plucks a crimson leaf fluttering in the breeze and tucks it into his waist pouch.

The ranger hails from Northland. 
Having traveled all over Adenthia after leaving his hometown, Awstin has witnessed countless landscapes and recorded them all in his sketchbook. 
This efficient ranger has a hobby where he sketches the plants he encounters on his journeys after completing his missions, so his sketchbook overflows with colorful illustrations of these plants.

Awstin discovered it in a washed-up crate on the shore. 
Shipwrecks are common at Northland Port, and their cargo sometimes float back to shore and are picked up by the inhabitants here. 
When he was just a child, Awstin discovered a foreign plant inside that crate. He brought it home, and it miraculously survived in this harsh environment for a long time. 
Later, as if possessed by a strange nightmare, the ranger left his home in search of the plant from his memories.

story.text:
Another soul fall for Jijel's deceit.
The woodsman watched as the group conferred briefly with the troll mercenary before trudging off in the direction he indicated. A quiet sigh escaped him — whether they'd return was anyone's guess. Fortune's favor alone would decide.
But stirring trouble served no one. Once more, he held his tongue.

Jijel, the troll, deals with numerous requests, most of which can't be made public, leading him to have dealings with a diverse spectrum of clients.
Jijel is the picture of proper courtesy for his employers, but his typical demeanor is rather ornery and he is prone to foul language.
But, who doesn't like money? Jijel would never be so foolish.

Jijel is always famished.
It's hard to tell if the hunger is physical or spiritual, but the symptom long existed for Jijel, right back to when he still lived within the troll tribe. His kinsfolk are largely aggressive and dimwitted in nature. Jijel however, considers himself a clever fellow. Life among a band of idiots is immense torture.
Jijel prefers his identity as a mercenary over that of his race. Just a superior level of deception and combat skill is all it takes to momentarily alleviate that ravenous hunger.

story.text:
Fizzle snuffled his enormous nose and gave a broad grin.
The goblin tightened the bag around his waist and plunged into the water with a "sploosh".
This pool wasn't terribly deep. Fizzle was fairly certain he could swim through the underground waterway and reach his destination unscathed.
He was sure of it, the band of mercenaries assembled here must have treasure! They must have wanted something at the other end of the waterway... but it's all his now!

Bombs are wonderful things — efficient, swift, devastatingly powerful, and so delightfully portable... utterly adorable, really.
Fizzle feels no particular reverence for their technical intricacies, yet he remains utterly obsessed with amplifying their destructive potential.
While goblins typically move in packs, Fizzle stands apart. A lone operator, he prefers working solo whenever possible.
After all, why share the spoils when one can claim every last glittering trinket for oneself?

Fizzle didn't linger for long at the base he started out in.
He was too immersed in improving his bombs and wound up blowing up the recently established base.
Not too long ago, the base had been attacked by a mob of human soldiers, and Fizzle's behavior only aggravated matters. Naturally, he was thrown out by the goblin leader.
That wasn't a problem anyway, after all, he'd wanted to go solo for a while now.

story.text:
Caledo furrowed his brow and wavered a moment. Eventually, he decided to double-check.
Although the other guard had already initiated the hand-off, he didn't deem his job to be done yet.
Something was lacking... It might be acceptable to hand over to the next guard, but Caledo believed it unfair.
He always obeyed the rules and espoused others to do so, too — intending to lead by example.

Life for Caledo flowed with predictable rhythm — so steady that his peers often teased him for its dullness.
Though elves were never a race given to whimsy, even by their measured standards, Caledo's rigid ways stood out as exceptionally wooden.
Yet this was the life he knew, the one that fit him like well-worn leather.
Only in rare moments of solitude would he wonder: Had his unbending demeanor drained the joy from others' revelries?

Caledo's unwavering integrity earned him both the affection and respect of his fellow guards.
Yet he remained — after all these years — only a sentinel of Increscent. No promotion had ever come, though not for lack of skill.
No, it was the very brightness of his character that barred his way. For where light burns fiercest, shadows gather thickest... and Increscent's gleaming surface hid darker currents beneath.
A man like Caledo, whose honesty cut through such gloom, could never be fully embraced by it.

story.text:
Zethos let out a discreet sigh — he didn't want his companions to hear him. 
The minotaur's head hung apathetically as he paced back and forth with his weapon in hand. He knew that soon enough, his companions would start complaining, and ask him to stop. 
But he was unable to restrain himself any longer: this was too boring and dull... This wasn't the life Zethos wanted for himself, but he had no other choice.

He had heard about the battle between Leader Bionphray and their previous leader. 
Zethos had never witnessed it firsthand, but he had heard various variations of this story from numerous minotaurs. 
Becoming a powerful and courageous minotaur had once been young Zethos' dream — he wanted his name to be remembered by his tribespeople. 
But now, that dream lay buried in his heart, never to sprout again.

Zethos had once possessed great ambitions, but he rarely speaks of them now, for fear that his companions would mock him. 
Indeed, he was just a guard stationed at the entrance of his tribe at present, and his only job was to watch over it. 
It was impossible for him to improve his combat skills by staying in this role, or achieve anything significant. 
Sometimes, Zethos finds himself secretly wishing for invaders to attack, so that he would have an opportunity to showcase his abilities — yet, he also harbors doubts about his own combat prowess, fearing that he might not be able to match up to his enemies... He sighed again.

story.text:
Anyone encountering Livia for the first time finds her somewhat detached and aloof.
The wandering knight often looks stern as she roams Nytheria, great sword in hand.
Unlike others who eke out a living in the forest, she doesn't strive to take every job going or aim to get rich, preferring instead to do just enough to fill her stomach a while.
Oftentimes, Livia can be found sitting on the pebbly ground by the stream, gazing into the lake, as if reflecting on the past.

Although not fond of socializing, Livia will not sit idly by when she encounters someone in distress.
Whilst her preference for solitude makes it hard for her to socialize, her moral compass ensures she acts with charity and kindness. This is why Livia always has work enough to keep her head above water, even if her lifestyle is an oft changing current.
It is not about gains or losses for Livia, but rather, her instinctual knightly principles.

Livia cherished her sword.
The blade had lost its youthful sharpness, bearing the inevitable scars of time — the dulled edge, the creeping rust. Yet atop the hilt, the family crest remained defiantly clear. That crest had once bound her oath.
Years had passed since she left their service. More years still since that house vanished silently from the ranks of the plains' noble families.
When duty and principle clashed, Livia had chosen her conscience. No regrets lingered... only the occasional pang of memory, fleeting as the plains' evening wind.

story.text:
Quarion executed his spell deftly, completing the task at hand, then let out a sigh. 
"If there are any other issues, just send word to me," the wizard said to the elf who had summoned him. He could finally leave after dropping some pleasantries, and he did so hurriedly. 
Quarion holds no animosity towards the elf. In fact, he is a good-natured and amicable elf who gets along with everyone. 
He simply has a distaste for work and will not spend more time than necessary on it.

As one of the wizards of the archipelago, Quarion doesn't share the typical sense of honor and responsibility like the other elves, but he has his own reasons. 
Not only does he have no interest in magic, but he is also even more apathetic about conducting in-depth research in this field. However, his physique isn't aligned with his interest of being a sword-wielding warrior, so he begrudgingly accepted a more suitable path. 
Though Quarion doesn't shirk his duties, he often feels helpless and weary about them.

When not participating in the activities on the archipelago, Quarion enjoys spending time alone in his own residence. 
He has a private penchant for admiring his own appearance in the mirror. Although Quarion's looks aren't particularly noteworthy among the many elves on the archipelago, this doesn't diminish his pleasure from doing so. 
Nonetheless, Quarion isn't keen on revealing this hobby of his, so he typically dresses modestly and plainly when heading outside.

story.text:
Noteera can no longer remember what Teneebria looks like. 
Ever since she was exiled to the Chaos Universum, all she has seen are endless repetitions of the same scenes — the bleak Bewilderness, the wailing Bewildered, decaying ruins... 
She hates it all.

Long ago in a distant past, Noteera once had a home of her own. 
She was the deadliest assassin in her clan, ready to sacrifice everything for her leader. But one day, she got the idea of killing Spider Mother Cyril. 
... Tragically, she cannot even remember the reason behind her plan now. The only hint is a blurry silhouette of a boy in her memories, perhaps her brother, she thinks. 
Nonetheless, the Dragon Queen's spies could not let this act of treason go unpunished.

Becoming a ferrywoman was but a compromise — the Bewilderness brimmed with peril, yet stood as the Chaos Universum' sole realm where novelty might yet be found. Delphina claimed she waited perhaps for something, though what precisely eluded even her own grasp.
Delphina herself had been unforeseen. Never had Noteera imagined forging bonds within this vast prison, yet the unpredictable had transpired. Unmarked by any particular moment, they became each other's.
When all concludes, she will endure with this friendship intact, as once agreed. Arduous, yet not beyond reach. A fighter she was, as she had ever been.

story.text:
Immeral is ever occupied.
Though Athalean is no sprawling settlement, its wood elves perpetually seek his counsel or aid — particularly regarding dealings with nearby human towns, matters for which his kin often lack patience.
With a sigh, Immeral fastened his twin blades despite the late hour. Such was the burden of a clan leader whose care knew no rest.

Immeral once thought about whether everything would have turned out differently if his father had been more steadfast. 
During the incident that changed the fate of Nytheria's wood elves, where although all the wood elves had made many decisions under duress or deception, Immeral still believed that his father should have persevered and not chosen to compromise. 
Any son would have wished for his father to act more valiantly.

Immeral stared into the depths of the forest, at the gloomy darkness that was looming over Nytheria's forest. 
He never once forgot the tragedy of the past, but there had been no time to investigate before everything had been decided. 
Immeral brimmed with remorse at this, and turned it into a heavier sense of responsibility that he took upon himself. He wasn't as submissive as he looked, and didn't believe in the supposed official explanation from Sythairelan, but rather began to take matters into his own hands.

story.text:
Letalis lifted the crystals, drawing his masked face near.
Steeped in those exquisite emanations, inquietum suffused the blighted land, transmuting the earth's essence into something other.
A substance dire for mortal creatures, yet one that filled him with exhilaration. During the rites, it rendered the murmuring voices startlingly clear.

Letalis was transformed by the elder into an Unstill, yet he, unlike Vasska, had not yet been afforded access to the deepest recesses of the voices.
He had listened to the master's commands, of course, but the ashen cloaked Letalis had never actually met Him... Still, it was enough to be instructed, and he would obey.
Later, once all traces of that master were lost, Letalis accompanied the shadow cloaks in listening to the songs of the deities, those voices silent yet exalted.
If only he could grasp its true meaning one day!

Letalis' voice, hoarse and shrill, hissed from behind the mask as he surveyed the ruined village.
These creatures' lives meant nothing, true. Yet they'd dared conceal what was never theirs, stashing the Four Witches' relics in their pitiful cellar.
Ah, the folly! To stash sacred artifacts in rotting, filth-crusted "treasure" chests!
No explanations would grace the living. The ashen robe needed only to act: reclaim what belonged to the coven, then slip back into the world's darkened folds.
