story.text:
First-time visitors to the Free Hatred could always expect the same treatment — a booming-voiced aerial dwarf would barrage them with questions:
"Name and origin? Purpose aboard? What say you of the Free Hatred? And of Captain Stoutbeard?"
Fail to properly praise either ship or captain, and Gloin would take mortal offense, challenging the fool to single combat on the spot.
Such was Gloin's peculiar notion of "security duty."

Gloin is the most dedicated guard aboard the Free Hatred. 
Flying in the vicinity of the ship seems to be this aerial dwarf's favorite thing to do, and he is also the first one to roar and charge at any attackers. Although he doesn't have a good memory, he knows everything about the Free Hatred by heart — especially the heroic deeds of Captain Stoutbeard, which he can ramble on about from dusk till dawn. 
His ultimate wish is to become guard commissioner to Captain Stoutbeard. However, given his hotheadedness, loud voice, and rough demeanor, it seems like this wish will never turn into reality.

Unlike his prideful kin, Gloin made no secret of his devotion to Captain Stoutbeard, a fervor bordering on religious zeal.
The roots ran deep. None knew how the captain had pulled him from despair's abyss, for Stoutbeard had sworn him to silence. Not once, even in his most ale-addled stupors, had that oath been broken.
The Free Hatred was home. Stoutbeard, his captain. This truth alone contented him utterly.

story.text:
Wilt pointed at the frost-encased beast for the cottage couple to see.
"No ghost haunts your home," the wizard explained with deliberate slowness. His words came in that perpetually muted tone of his — one had to strain to hear. "Just magic-maddened beasts. Some failed magic experiment, likely. Best you don't inquire further..."
"Now then, good folk." Wilt extended his palm. "Problem solved. That spellbook of yours belongs with me."

Before becoming a squalid wizard, Wilt was held prisoner on board a ship.
It was a transport ship, taking away those banished from Dragonsaerie. Wilt, however, was kept on board for his good behavior. Some time passed and the ship docked at Iskalland. It was then that he decided to make a run for it.
Much time has passed since Wilt was branded a criminal, and marks of his past have been erased with magic. Still, his ingrained habits of wearing long, heavy garb to hide his identifying tattoos have not been shaken off.

Wilt only asks for spellbooks as payment.
His interest seems like that of any other wizard, but the truth is far more sinister. Wilt enjoys collecting and reading the lost, lonely books. After reading them, he burns them, sating his twisted, grotesque possessiveness.
As if, once the books are gone, he would become the only person in the world to know of them.

story.text:
People who dislike Nedda call her "Fiery Lunatic", possibly because she always resorts to violence in disagreements, or because she never listens to wrongdoers who try to raise a dispute, or because her berserk fire magic terrifies them. 
In the eyes of ordinary villagers, she is Errich's most loyal henchwoman. They believe she relies on Errich's status to stay in this village, and also uses his reputation to seek revenge against those who dislike her — there are even many who believe that she has ambitions to become the chief's wife. 
In the past, she would have blasted flames at these people, but now, she ignores them, as per the teachings of the books that Errich has given her.

There was a long time when Nedda lost her name. 
Branded as "that traitor's niece" due to her uncle's mistakes, she had been stripped of her name by the furious tribespeople, and had even been bullied, insulted, and outcast by the extremists. 
While she understood that this was a case of misplaced blame, she thought that it was unreasonable. The villagers had been in need of sustenance, and it was also their decision to allow an outsider into the sacred grounds. However, at the horrible consequences of the corruption in the sacred grounds, they simply chose to unleash their anger on a single scapegoat. 
"This is unfair, but their feelings will persist," said Errich to her, "Because you're still too weak, and they're not intelligent enough."

Nedda admires Errich, but it isn't a feeling of infatuation or adoration — rather, she sees it as an unequivocal recognition, support, and heartfelt endorsement of him. 
This isn't only because Errich protected her from the bullying she endured, but because he saved her from her naive anger, hatred, and resentment — and his enlightenment made her stronger, and she has become one of the tribe's warriors. 
Although she still has a broody, irritable, and aggressive demeanor, Nedda feels that she is no longer the child she used to be, who hated everything, including herself. 
If she truly despises something now, she figures that she can simply set it ablaze.

story.text:
Irina loves socializing with people.
Conversation is fun. Words and phrases, one statement to another, countless secrets and tales unfold from people's lips. As a good communicator, Irina has always been a woman who keeps her ear to the ground amidst this dense forest.
Occasionally there can be weariness coming over, but such feeling is so fleeting that her curiosity can always take her over before long. Even when drunk, she'll listen to a particular whisper floating around the tavern before she passes out.

Always on the move between locations, gathering intelligence and running errands, Irina scarcely knows rest.
As her connections expanded, employers began urging her to leave the forest for lengthier assignments abroad. "The pay is substantial," the man insisted, "and won't take overly long. Do consider it."
Irina responded with a laugh and a firm shake of her head.
"Repeated invitations may be construed as threats," she countered smoothly.\ "I'd strongly advise against persisting in this manner."

The folks of Aquitaine always assume Irina is an outlander owing to her extensive travels and expertise in interesting things abroad.
However, this is not actually the case. Irina originally hails from Nytheria, where she left in childhood, only to return after considerable hardship. As to exactly why this displacement occurred and when, it is something Irina has never spoken of.
Some things spoken are pointless, some things spoken are useless.

story.text:
Tioh weighed the purse in his hand to show the newsmonger before him that he meant business. 
This was a small, inconspicuous corner of Teneebria, perfect for the kind of activities deep elves loved, like assassinations, trading, and fighting... Tioh acquired what he needed and left hurriedly. 
There are no truly safe places in the Hypogean District, and having survived as a soldier to this day, Tioh understands this intimately.

Tioh nurses ambition, carefully measured, always displayed in just the right doses.
He is nothing if not adaptable, a man who bends with the wind. In this realm where allegiances shift like desert sands, information is his currency, and even a minor player can thrive with enough of it.
The Thallasen Clan had overthrown the Perenthallis Clan to claim the Royal City's throne. And before them? Power changes hands faster than most can track. But Tioh knows — one day, his fingers will close around it.

Tioh is one of the few soldiers who has a close relationship with Prince Auster. 
Objectively, Tioh cannot deny that Auster's current situation is rather dire. In terms of temperament, Auster, who still has a bit of a warm heart, isn't necessarily the best investment either. 
However, this deep elf still chose to take a smaller gamble and intentionally approached the hapless Prince. Auster is merely one of Tioh's various investment targets, but the potential for a big payoff from taking small risks is always higher.

story.text:
Meggan trailed her fingers through the water in the copper basin, untangling strands of her auburn hair. As a handmaiden to House Ptolemy, she would soon attend yet another round of her lord's diplomatic visits.
The first wizards to settle in the Vale, the Ptolemies had always been the most sociable — the driving force behind its newest institutions and alliances.
A sigh escaped her. These visits would change nothing, she knew. The other four families had long since lost their way, their so-called pursuit of truth having led them astray.

Like every handmaiden in the household, Meggan had been raised by the Ptolemies since childhood.
She studied magic at the family head's side, mastering not just spells but the intricate dance of etiquette and politics — an education far beyond what mere servants required.
But the Ptolemies expected more.
When the moment ripened, these carefully groomed women would take their places as valued pieces on the board, moved across the shadows where true power played its game.

Beyond magic, Meggan also has quite the passion for painting.
She enjoys making observational studies of the portraits hanging on the walls, generation after generation of Ptolemy matriarchs and patriarchs. Some have passed away, while others have simply shut themselves away in the Vale's depths, withdrawing from familial involvement.
When nobody is there, Meggan paints alone in her room, depicting those faces with the same chestnut red hair.
She likes red. Intense and exuberant, like the red leaves that climb the cliffs, stretching out from her canvas and up into her dreams.

story.text:
Dora meticulously works the chisel in her hand, polishing each component with exacting care.
The parts have already taken form, but under the dwarf's skilled touch they grow smoother still — every potential snag or burr eliminated.
Where these pieces might ultimately find use, she couldn't say. Perhaps in some great machine where precision matters little; perhaps as part of a scholar's delicate new instrument.
It matters not to Dora. Each receives the same devoted attention, the same inexhaustible patience.

Dora has a gentle disposition, though her friend Gitouna would describe her as weak.
Dora doesn't see things quite the same way as Gitouna. In her opinion, not everything is about winning, and often winning doesn't mean anything in itself.
Instead of comparing herself to others and being competitive, she prefers to remain calm and happy.
While she is happy to settle for the status quo, yet isn't it a status quo that she has chosen and earned?

Dora has not complained about her coworkers, although sometimes their carelessness distracts her.
Unless the mistakes are deliberate and persistent, Dora prefers to quietly dispose of defective parts herself.
She doesn't hate the boring job; she likes to do her part without causing trouble for others.
Hopefully, no one else will give her any trouble either, Dora prays silently in her heart.

story.text:
Gerana wiped her mechanics tool set meticulously before carefully returning them to her pouch. 
She had had this pouch specially custom-made to prevent any damage to her tools. Nevertheless, her need for tool replacements grew increasingly frequent, for it was difficult to contain her love for elaborate tools. 
Gerana spends a significant portion of her salary on such tools, but she has never once regretted her purchases.

The Magic Puppet Guild of Helix Island is highly prestigious in the continent of Adenthia, and has thus attracted many skillful people to join, such as its president, Donella. 
Gerana had been drawn to this place by its frequent birth of remarkable creations. It was only upon her arrival to the island that she realized that the versatility of magic crystals was far wider than anything she had witnessed before. 
It was not easy to ascend to the top — without extraordinary talent, she could only start her climb up the ranks as a junior mechanic.

Being occupied with the dull, monotonous tasks of her apprenticeship all day long meant that Gerana didn't get to enjoy much leisure time. 
The masters had enough free time to refine their blueprints, but she needed extra time to comprehend and digest them. 
Despite this, she was not a grouchy gnome who resorted to complaints. Since she had already chosen this path, she was determined to plough on steadily. 
One day, her works would also be showcased on the display shelves of the Magic Puppet Guild.

story.text:
Enraged, Vojeh kicked the pile of debris before him. The excessive force caused some of the remaining skin and flesh attached to his skeleton to fall off with a disturbing, rustling sound. 
This only added to the undead's frustration, and he hissed incomprehensibly before leaving the room. 
He had gained nothing and wasted a lot of time — the spellbook Vojeh was looking for wasn't even here.

In life, Vojeh had known comfort.
His family's wealth ensured ease — though unlearned and vain, he wanted for nothing, indulging in idle pleasures without care. Then came the day magic caught his fancy, and fortune's wheel turned sharply downward.
The tragedy lay not merely in his lack of talent, but in his utter blindness to it.

Vojeh's death was somewhat ridiculous as well — it was caused by an accident, and the perpetrator was none other than himself. 
Despite his lack of talent, he still wanted to pursue magic, so he resorted to risky desperate measures, which was unwise in the field of magic. 
However, even after becoming a wandering undead, Vojeh hasn't given up his dreams. Sometimes, he even forgets why he is looking for those books — it boils down to an instinctual urge.

story.text:
The bowstring between Adrie's fingers trembles for the briefest of moments, before loosing an arrow into the darkness, just like a shooting star.
She hears a thud.
Another foe has been eliminated. This insurrection is nearing its end. It swept in, driven by momentous disdain, but no good yet came of it.
"Rebels that defy the Queen will never prevail!" she thinks, taking aim at another head.

As a warrior under the Queen, Adrie has always been outstanding.
She not only manages the Unyielding Silk's affairs, but also traverses the underworld as needed, ensuring priests safe passage in their dealings.
Many things unintended for her ears have been heard, but never has she uttered a single one. For that reason, she feels certain she yet lives.

Was it a nightmare? Adrie wasn't sure.
She proceeded towards the subterranean, traversing the murky waterways, arriving where searing lava flow met the frigid underground rivers.
It was here the Cyril, the Spider Mother, revealed Herself. Profane and twisted, beauteous yet hideous.
No hypogean elf could resist bowing their head in awe to such an avatar, and Adrie was no exception.

story.text:
Thea narrows her eyes, listening to the sound of the rolling dice.
"Come on, ladies and gents! Take a punt!" She urges her fellow thieves gathered around the campfire, hoping more will partake in the gamble.
This is a favored pastime of hers, but impossible to enjoy when traveling solo.
For the sake of keeping the fun alive, Thea would deliberately lose a few games, just here and there.

Thea felt no particular fondness for robbery — it was merely the most efficient path to wealth. Had quicker, easier methods existed, the rogue might have embraced them.
Alas, the world offered few roads to unearned riches.
Gold burned through her fingers like summer lightning. More often than not, an entire purse would vanish across the gambling tables in a single night. Not that Thea lacked cunning — she simply reveled in the delicious torment of chance's whims.

She encountered a peculiar gambler.
Out in the slums, this gambler appeared before her. Thea was sick and exhausted. He invited the girl to gamble with him.
Perhaps it was fate? Unbelievably, Thea won three rounds in a row, and the gambler, shrouded in a black cloak, paid her the promised stakes.
Thanks to that, Thea survived. Despite knowing the unlikelihood, she still believes she'll run into that character again some day, probably at the gambling tables.

story.text:
Evania stretched languidly, breathing in the salt-kissed wind that danced between her bare toes.
She had chosen this secluded spot on Increscent deliberately — here, far from prying eyes, she could shed her armor like a second skin and simply be.
The young elf wandered the tideline in endless loops, her mind adrift on deeper currents.
More often than not, her thoughts turned to fantasies — vivid daydreams of what might lie beyond the horizon's shimmering edge.

Evania had never set foot beyond Increscent. For years, this never struck her as strange.
Why would it? Her world overflowed with simple joys — every complication smoothed away by elder hands. Schoolwork and drills filled her mornings; her afternoons were spent idling along sunlit shores.
Happy. Content. She loved the elves around, thrived in every lesson and sparring match. What more could life possibly require?

Her curiosity arose from a particular battle.
Evania shouldn't have been involved, but all the other guards had been mobilized by the Order that day, thus the overachieving Evania was drafted.
The battle itself hadn't been taxing, and despite a minor injury, that didn't bother Evania!
But her foe... a creature she had never before observed in earnest, it was incredible. Evania saw the blood drain from the corpses of her enemies, and it turned out they were just like her...
Suddenly, she was intrigued, curious as to where these strange creatures had come from, and what it was like over there.

story.text:
Korth's most profound feeling about death is the cold.
The inexhaustible winds and snow flurries bring death. Those dead ones, which then become the undead, are the ones who let the cold persist without end.
Korth stares mutely at his armor. Its original metallic luster has begun to tarnish, turning a ghastly white.
Everything tarnishes — just like his perception of the world.

Korth is well aware that he can never escape death because fate has chosen him.
No, of course not. Death is the best place for the dead, and Korth has become what he is through the Order intervention.
True enough, there are still things he wishes to do in the world of the living, so to call this unlucky wouldn't be entirely fair. That said, it's not a blessing, either. He'll never again be able to taste his favorite fruit wine.

Long before the cold embrace of death claimed him, Korth had dwelled with Araces in the wilds.
The land offered little comfort — its dangers were many, its climate cruel. Yet with a trusted companion at his side, even survival's harsh trials became a shared adventure.
When Korth awoke reborn from snow and stillness, his first thought was for Araces' fate.
To learn his friend lived, only to have joined the desert-dwelling lizardfolk... This truth left Korth torn. Did he wish these tidings real, or false? He could no longer say.

story.text:
Dubok waved the staff in his hand, sending flames sprawling across the earth.
He stopped, gave a shake of his head towards the young orcs bumbling around him, then pounded his staff against the ground a few more times.
"Simmer down, young'uns." Pointing to the swamp just ahead, Dubok exclaimed, "Feed the dwarves to the crocodiles! We've got what we came for. Back to Khoriz Khu."

Dubok doesn't hold the same loyalty to Grishnaar that many of his compatriots do.
Not a young orc, it's apparent that he's enjoyed plentiful opportunities for a long life in the desolate chaos surrounding Khoriz Khu. Those more reckless than he would have soon found themselves dead.
Dubok would never disobey Grishnaar, of course not! But that's the extent of it.

As the tribe's shaman, Dubok possesses more caution than his fellow orcs... and a peculiar little vice.
He favors flame-seared sustenance over raw, bleeding flesh.
Fire is kin to Dubok, for it has won him status and victories, while filling his belly when hunger called.

story.text:
Lorarii cautiously surveys his surroundings, pulling his cloak over his face as he picks his way through the dense undergrowth.
In the distance, voices carry — speaking with the familiar imperial accent. These same voices had hailed him as a comrade mere days prior.
Now, everything had changed. He had become a mark of shame, an object of scorn — a deserter. Yet to his own surprise, no regret stirred within him.

Lorarii's pursuit for justice had naturally led him to join the army of the Dragonsaerie Empire. 
However, life was not easy for him. 
As an insignificant pawn, he struggled to keep up with the politics played by the upper echelons, and the realities of his situation soon shattered Lorarii's idealistic visions of life. He was assigned to the Knight Order of Dragon Blood, a unit stationed at the frigid border.

At first, Lorarii tried to convince himself to accept reality, that there was still value in upholding justice even when no one was watching. 
He encouraged himself and practiced martial arts while shivering in the bitter winds. He had thought of escaping, but in the Knight Order of Dragon Blood, failed escape attempts led to execution. 
However, after the gruesome battle where he witnessed how the orcs tore his comrades apart and splattered blood all over his face, Lorarii finally broke down. He fled, and once he began his escape, there was no end in sight.

story.text:
Born into poverty, Vethak became a Tribal Warrior driven by his obsession with gold, hoping to make some coin along the way.
Unfortunately, in their rigidly hierarchical society, both gold and their life were controlled by noble bloodlines.
Since conscience couldn't earn him gold, he abandoned it, taking the path of accepting favors.

Vethak's honest demeanor is just a facade — he's willing to act against his conscience for gold.
Stealing lizardfolk intelligence, letting outlanders into restricted areas, selling noble secrets...
Vethak fears being caught and burned alive in lava by his tribesfolk, but he wonders — is it wrong to wish for just a little gold from his own labor?

Beneath Vethak's cot rests an ironbound chest hewn from volcanic stone.
Its obsidian surface secured by three rusting padlocks and a fading ward-spell.
Only in the tent's solitude does he lift the lid, gazing upon the accumulating hoard. Each glint of gold sets his pulse hammering against his ribs.
In these stolen moments, he dreams in hues of flight: river-carved valleys, forgotten woodlands, beautiful coasts... Anywhere but here, once the chest brims full.

story.text:
Among the many gold mines under Blazeland lizardfolk control, Volcano Island was once considered inconsequential.
Yet in recent months, the lizardfolk have watched in astonishment as the island’s gold output surges — not due to newfound high-purity veins, but through the relentless efficiency of their new overseer, Eleuia.
Through sheer force of will, she has boosted mining productivity by nearly half. Such results, of course, have not gone unnoticed.

Eleuia's secret for success lay in something simple and cruel: the whip. 
Her whip doled out lashings to lazy miners and those whom she deemed were slacking off. 
Eleuia had no tolerance for excuses. 
If the miners didn't feel like working, she would make sure that they paid a price more painful than labor itself. If they were unable to work, she would simply replace them with new miners. She wasn't going to be soft-hearted like the previous foreperson was, who haphazardly approved sick leave that led to a decrease in their production. And it was precisely because she caught this mistake of his and reported it that she cinched her current position. 
She was going to make the most out of her post.

Eleuia had once received a prophecy. 
The royal lineage of the lizardfolk were renowned for their exceptional prophetic abilities, and Eleuia's parents had the fortune of receiving a few cryptic words regarding their destiny: their offspring would be their goldmine, and something brilliant and dazzling would be born from them. 
As long-suffering gold miners, her parents thus placed all of their hopes on their daughter, Eleuia. They spared no effort in nurturing her until they died in a mining accident. 
Just like her parents, Eleuia firmly believed in that prophecy. Employing underhanded methods, she created her own opportunities and resolutely rose up the ranks. The lives and deaths of the miners under her whip were unimportant, as long as they could continue accumulating enough capital for her promotion...

story.text:
Gusni maneuvered her way through Sinner Swamp, where the viscous and damp mulch concealed dangers at every turn, and the dense vegetation obstructed her view. 
However, the orc didn't stop, for she still had a mission to complete. 
Grishnaar needed her to cross Sinner Swamp tonight and make a delivery. Despite knowing that the dark night would mask the dangers lurking in the plains, Gusni didn't hesitate in taking up the task. 
Why should she? After all, this was for the glory of her tribe.

Gusni could tell that not all orcs in the Bloodfang were as loyal as her. 
She seized every opportunity to admonish them, but regretfully, new fools and traitors would always crop up every time. Eventually, she gained the trust of the chief and was allowed to deal with some of the insignificant traitors within the tribe. 
Not every traitor was worthy of Grishnaar's time, so she took it upon herself to act on behalf of the chief she served.

Gusni sought honor on the battlefield, but was aware that battles could be fought on more than one front. 
Orc warriors indeed found pleasure fighting in the midst of blood and gore — but it was pathetic to have no particular purpose, and Gusni believed that she was not a pathetic orc. 
Gusni has poured all her unwavering loyalty into the Bloodfang, and would defend its glory up until her very last moment.

story.text:
Edgar glanced at the distant town one final time, then slipped his helmet back on.
He had no intention of taking it off ever again, fearing no one would want to see the face beneath it. At least, exposing his face wasn't considered a sound move given Edgar's intentions.
Edgar had only recently learned of his story in this town. Frankly, it was the most preposterous story one could imagine.

Edgar was once an officer. Devoted to his duty, he never questioned his superior's orders, and never considered betrayal.
During that violent, savage battle, Edgar was wounded. However, one thing he never expected was for his best friend and fellow soldier, whom he trusted without reserve, to abandon him, leaving him for dead on the battlefield.
Edgar was carried back to a settlement by outland monsters, tortured to the point of wishing for death, and enslaved.

In time, Edgar found his moment and slaughtered every last one of those wretched creatures.
He was human, after all. Of course he longed for home. What man wouldn't?
Yet when he finally dragged his battered body into the first human settlement, he found himself cast as the architect of tragedy. The town's whispers accused him: Traitor. The army's downfall. The reason for their ruin.
The absurdity of it all threatened to choke him — until only one purpose remained. Vengeance.

story.text:
Rephe blew the whistle she carried with her, the short and rhythmic notes quickly attracting the other gnomes to her. 
After a fierce battle, they successfully repelled the Decayed, but their side had also suffered some losses. 
Rephe's alertness had prevented even greater losses, but she didn't have time to accept thanks as she hurriedly escorted the wounded back to their settlement in search of a healer.

Rephe barely has a personal life, for she has made communal living a part of her private life. 
Always busy, Rephe charges ahead as a warrior of the Hypogean District's gnomes, as if nothing else matters. Even on quiet days, Rephe will patrol until it is time for her shift change, before exhaustedly falling into a contented sleep.

Occasionally, Rephe will have nightmares about losing her family. 
As a skilled warrior under Nissa, she is an orphan who was raised by the gnome tribe, after an attack by the deep elves had caused many families to lose their fathers. Sadly, her misfortune only continued into her adulthood when she lost both her child and her husband. 
With her grief draining her spirit, Rephe feels incapable to start a new family, and thus devotes all her efforts into ensuring the tribe's safety, hoping that tragedy will never strike again.

story.text:
Yamyra grabs the pumpkin and hurls it away.
"Right, are we done now?! I hear you — loud and clear! Got it! How much more prattling?!" the halfling yells, visibly spooking the small crowd of halflings standing around.
They are her family, but also her greatest source of pressure. At this moment, she finally snaps, unable to hold back any longer.

She detested rules, and hated having them repeated over and over again. Yamyra felt repeating herself more than once was unnecessary, but her family were very old-fashioned.
Since they couldn't imagine going together, Yamyra decided to walk away and leave the home. Exactly where hadn't been decided yet, just as long as it wasn't here.
She knew the world beyond Uerus might be dangerous, but her hatred of discipline was too great.

Despite being a novice traveler, Yamyra had — somewhat surprisingly — avoided any true calamity.
Perhaps it was her sharp vigilance that kept misfortune at bay. Adenthia had no shortage of villains, she knew, but when confrontation seemed unwise... well, avoidance worked just as well.
Yet even in her direst hours, Yamyra refused to join any company. The risk of constraint still haunted her — better to wander free than be caged again.

story.text:
Fitz staggered across the battlefield, his skeletal fingers trembling around the hilt of his sword. The air reeked of rot and blood, but he no longer had lungs to gag with.
Memories eluded him — not just his name, nor how he died, but even the force that had bound his bones to this wretched half-life.
Nothing remained.
A rustling bush drew his hollow gaze. For a moment — just a moment — something like hope rattled in his ribcage. Then the scavenging jackals looked up from their meal, and his jaw clacked in hollow disappointment.

Before this existence as a mobile skeleton, Fitz had been a soldier serving a lord.
This lord ruled a small city-state, which was soon wiped out during one of the many forgotten wars of the plains.
The conflict Fitz fought in was just another insignificant scuffle. Every soldier there had been possessed of the same ferocity and fear.
He remembered nothing of it. Forgotten were his insignificance, forgotten was his life's trivial story.

Before taking up the sword, Fitz had been but a farmer's son.
His family worked the stubborn earth, their days defined by empty bellies and desperate remedies. When the hunger grew too sharp, he enlisted — one less mouth to feed, one less weight upon their shoulders.
Righteous foes or wicked, his lord's cause just or damned — such distinctions meant nothing then. They mean nothing now.
All memories have faded. Only the hunger remains, an ember that outlived death itself.

story.text:
Trader Wellby lounges in his chair, a glint in his narrow, squinting eyes.
The rural halfling caresses the jewel-encrusted ring on his short, stubby finger and surveys the lively marketplace sprawling before him. He has been sitting here for half a day, a number of vendors hollering at him as they pass by and Wellby summarily waving them all away.
This upbeat merchant is watching. Watching the beating commercial heart of this town, and how the blood courses through it.

Following the dim path, Wellby strides steadily towards his destination.
The tip of the staff in his hand is glowing softly, just a minor adaptation. After learning some magic, the halfling acquired the staff for the sake of protection during long journeys between settlements.
But far more often — such as this very moment, Wellby finds it more practical as a place to mount a lamp when walking at night.

Wellby considers himself a lucky chap.
Adenthia is not a peaceful land, for prosperity and decay are both lurking beneath its surface. But for traders, this is a great commercial opportunity. In fact, since the collaboration with the Crimson Crows, his assets are flowing faster than ever.
Still, as a prudent businessman, Wellby keeps watching, watching to see if this opportunity brings fortune, or catastrophe.

story.text:
As he gazed at his sleeping son, a surge of excitement coursed through Tauricen. In the deep Vale, edible food was scarce, and he hadn't tasted blood for a long time.
"Blood... fresh, warm blood..." The voice swirled in his mind, driving away his remaining sanity.
The blade was already pressed against the steadily rising and falling throat when Tauricen snapped back to reality.
What am I doing? No, absolutely not! He raised his blade and slashed his own arm, the searing pain jolting him back to clarity.

Even as a child, Tauricen was drawn to combat. The savagery in his blood made him a skilled warrior, but it also led him to revel in the fleeting joy of killing.
In the deep shadows, the out-of-control Tauricen swung his blade at his comrade.
"What are you doing?" The great axe blocked his brutal strike, as Bionphray glared at Tauricen's blood-red eyes.
"Surrendering to desire — how are you any different from a mindless beast?"
Many years later, though Bionphray had been exiled, Tauricen still remembered his words.

"By the gods' command, do not gaze within! Escort this to the forbidden grounds where someone awaits."
Thus spoke the missive delivered unto Tauricen. Yet as his convoy trudged onward, the cage emitted whispers and howls that chilled his marrow.
Those echoes were not of this world, but of some abyssal plane where hope withers beneath tyrannical will.
Against all wisdom, the warrior's curiosity prevailed. A fleeting glance between the slats revealed... something stirring. Pupilless eyes yawned open. Reality itself seemed to lurch, and then darkness took him.
He awoke abed in camp, unharmed. When pressed, his fellow companions would only remain silent.

story.text:
Loris patrols the underground space. Tables and chairs upended, detritus strewn all over, he again reaffirms that nothing has slipped though his net. That's another of Penultima's strongholds nicely "cleaned up".
The Dragon Queen's warrior straightened his crooked helm, askew from the chase. The sword he wields still bears a chill.
He wordlessly offers a prayer, relaying all that he has witnessed. This includes evidence of Penultima's next move that he has found within this cave.

In his daily life, Loris is a man of singular focus.
His existence revolves around three duties alone: safeguarding priests, eliminating fools bold enough to cross him, and purging the taint of Chaos. Beyond this holy trinity of purpose, he shows no interest in worldly matters.
When not engaged in these tasks, he will kneel motionless before the effigy of the Dragon Queen, his lips moving in ceaseless devotion.

In his youth, Loris often heard the eerie cries from within the void.
Those bizarre, yet marvelous sounds reverberated non-stop, driving the boy's psyche to the very edge. His parents were long dead, and all the villagers believed the boy to be hysterical, abandoning all hope for him once the priest gave up.
On another dark night, Loris suffered a complete mental breakdown, running feverishly from the village toward the darkness of the mountains.
He plummeted through a crack in the mountain road, falling into the endless abyss. It was there that Loris found his salvation.

story.text:
Broll puts his palms into the bay's waves.
The current brushes against the back of his hands before rapidly retreating, disappearing in the endless blueness.
He raises his head again, gazing at the big ship, worn and rotten from having remained in this haven so long.
The sheen elf is agile enough to climb up the mast quickly. He takes the telescope inherited from his grandfather and begins to observe the other side of the sea.

Broll is a sailor who has never sailed.
Such is the fate of a sheen elf born too late — by his coming of age, Increscent's sea-lanes to distant shores has already faded into legend.
The handful of visitors who still come do so only for the Cresent Order or the lord. Broll is no part of those stories.
So he remains in Lacunae, where the waves whisper of journeys he will never make.

His father and grandfather passed him that title. "Seafarer" — how intriguing it sounds!
During his childhood, he practiced for his future voyage in the big ship, which was not yet rotten, entertaining the dream of becoming a true seafarer.
However, those countless ships that used to shuttle to and from never arrived at Lacunae again. He could only touch those nautical charts again and again in his imagination after listening to his elders' stories.
But Broll never gives up. He still expects someday to embark on a long voyage.

story.text:
Little urchins like Grover are commonplace in the Dragonsaerie slums.
After losing their parents, the orphans had to fill their stomachs all by themselves. They burrowed like mudfish, smooth-talking and deceitful, learning of every skeleton in every closet of this seedy quarter better than any adult.
For authentic intel, a little urchin like Grover is exactly the right person to approach. Just remember to keep a tight grip on your wallet while talking to him. You'll want to avoid unwelcome hands reaching in while you're distracted.

Grover is considered one of the luckier orphans. He'd attended school a few days, recognized a lot of words, making him better equipped than the other kids to handle premium jobs that involved message delivery.
His loyalty is also well-reputed. As long as he had a crumb of bread, he wouldn't allow his fellows to starve. The many shady, sinister sights he had seen had not dimmed the brightness of his eyes: He repays kindness to the benevolent, yet this flexible kindness won't hinder his casual emptying of fattened merchant's wallets.
Robbing the rich to give to the poor. That's what he always says.

Grover adored the Upper City of Dragonsaerie.
Its streets lay spotless, its residents clad in tidy attire, dwelling in spacious chambers adorned with blossoms and melodies — not the raucous tavern ditties, but music pure as mountain springs.
Perhaps... he dared imagine, perhaps one day he might secure a messenger's post up there. The occasional lordly coin for his troubles, lighthearted banter with laundry maids... No more curses or empty bellies, just crisp linens and unfeigned smiles day after day...
Ah. Best ponder tomorrow's supper first.

story.text:
Haug stood upright in the dense fog, motionless, like a stubborn stone dampened by the morning mist. 
There had been no trespassers attempting to enter the forbidden zone, but he was always stationed there, day after day, year after year. 
Compared to this place, perhaps even the prison in Scarlet Vale was much more lively. Haug had worked there before, but being a jailer was likewise not a desirable job. 
Occasionally, shadows would appear, moving about in the dense fog. Perhaps they were of the same race as that mentor, Haug surmised.

Frankly speaking, the minotaur had no idea what the forbidden zone he was guarding contained. 
There was no need for him to ask. Even if he did, it was unlikely that he would get any answers, but rather put himself in danger instead. 
There were too many secrets hidden within Scarlet Vale, and too many human wizards pursuing forbidden knowledge who gathered here. Of course, there were also wizards of other races, but it was difficult for them to blend in. 
Just casually coming into contact with forbidden knowledge was deadly, and Haug was well aware of this.

Conversation seldom came to him, save for the occasional visit from Schaltar, who would pause to share a few words.
Yet even these exchanges were fleeting, for most of time this companion wandered the thick mists, guiding lost outsiders back to safety.
Their bond had deepened years ago over one particular wanderer — a reckless human Haug had meant to dispatch, until Schaltar intervened with unexpected mercy.
Haug had acquiesced then, though to this day he still cannot fathom Schaltar's peculiar softness for humankind.

story.text:
Merideth was born into a poor family in Tavira. A plague in her childhood took her parents. In her despair, a passing cleric of the Knight Order of Platinum saved her from the brink of death with a healing spell. This experience solidified Merideth's belief that faith could bring salvation and hope.
Upon reaching adulthood, Merideth joined the Knight Order as a field cleric. Before every battle, she would recite scriptures to the soldiers, her firm voice recounting the legend of Bahamut vanquishing darkness with holy light.

During one war, Merideth's unit was besieged in a cliffside fortress. When the enemy set the granary ablaze with firebombs, she rushed into the inferno, tearing away charred beams with her bare hands to rescue trapped soldiers. Her right arm was severely burned, but she uttered no sound, instead using her remaining strength to stanch the wounded's bleeding.
In the final, brutal breakout, the army had all but lost its will to fight, and the general had to call a retreat. The enemy seized the opportunity, launching a fierce assault on the withdrawing troops. Fearlessly, Merideth stood at the forefront, held her holy symbol high, and a miraculous dragon-scale barrier blocked the volley of arrows.

After the war, Merideth declined an invitation to stay at the temple, choosing to continue serving with the army on its campaigns. At every camp, she personally built simple altars and sewed sacred cloths.
Veterans tell a story of a snowy night when Merideth knelt alone before the ruins of a trench, pressing the dog tags of the fallen to her chest. Snowflakes fell upon the platinum epaulets on her shoulders, as if crowning a warrior. To this day, new recruits can still see Merideth praying all night outside her tent — just like the cleric who healed her years ago, building a bridge of faith with piety and protection.
